# The A.I. Dilemma - March 9, 2023

## Introduction and Background 
- AI is being deployed in a dangerous way, and there is a 10% chance that humans could go extinct due to a lack of control over AI.
- The Center for Humane Technology is introducing the topic of AI and its implications.
- The co-founders of the organization are Tristan Harris and ASA Raskin, who also created the Emmy-winning Netflix documentary, The Social Dilemma.
- The documentary has reached 100 million people in 190 countries and 30 languages.
- The organization has advised heads of state, global policy makers, members of Congress, and national security leaders on the dangers of technology.
- The presentation aims to provide a paradigmatic response to AI by providing a more visceral way of experiencing the exponential curves that we're about to head into.

## Responsibility of New Technology 
- When a new technology is invented, it uncovers a new class of responsibility that is not always obvious.
- For example, the right to privacy was not written into law until mass-produced cameras came onto the market.
- The attention economy is still in the process of figuring out how to write into law what it takes from us.
- The invention of a new technology confers power and will start a race that ends in tragedy if not coordinated.
- There is no single player that can stop a race that ends in tragedy.

## AI and Its Implications (0-19, 95-399)
- AI is being deployed in a dangerous way, and there is a 10% chance that humans could go extinct due to a lack of control over AI.
- Large language model AI is being released into the public responsibly.
- AI has many incredible positives, such as the ability to translate animal communication and creating a Spanish tutor.
- AI researchers believe that half of them think there is a 10% chance of humans going extinct due to an inability to control AI.

## Experience of AI 
- AI is an abstract thing that affects many things and doesn't have the grounding metaphors like the kinesthetic experience in our lives that makes it hard to wrap our heads around how transformational it is.
- The presentation aims to provide a more visceral way of experiencing the exponential curves that we're about to head into.
- A metaphor was used where it's like 1944, and you get a call from Robert Oppenheimer inside The Manhattan Project, and he says the world is about to change in a fundamental way except it's not being deployed in a safe and responsible way.

## Conclusion (0-19, 95-399)
- AI is being deployed in a dangerous way, and there is a 10% chance that humans could go extinct due to a lack of control over AI.
- Responsibility needs to be taken when inventing new technology to avoid tragedy.
- AI has many incredible positives, but it needs to be released into the public responsibly.
## Social media - humanity's first contact with AI 
- Social media was the first contact between humanity and AI.
- Social media and its algorithms activate supercomputer AI pointed at your brain to calculate and predict the perfect thing that will keep you scrolling.
- This fairly simple technology was enough, in the first contact with AI, to break humanity with information overload, addiction, doom-scrolling, sexualization of kids, shortened attention spans, polarization, fake news, and breakdown of democracy.

## Paradigm of social media 
- We were saying a bunch of things about what social media was.
- We actually noticed that social media is going to give everyone a voice.
- The paradigm from which we were seeing what social media was about is giving people a voice, providing a platform, connecting people with their friends, and enabling small and medium-sized businesses to reach their customers.
- These things are all true and are actual benefits.

## The race to the bottom of the brain stem 
- The arms race was for attention which became the race to the bottom of the brain stem and that created this kind of engagement monster.
- Maximize engagement actually rewrote the rules of every aspect of our society because it took other core aspects of our society into its tentacles and took them hostage.
- Children's identity is held hostage by it, and social exclusion happens if you don't have a Snapchat or Instagram account.
- Journalism can't exist outside of Twitter, and national security happens through social media and information warfare.
- Politics and elections are now run through this engagement economy which has infused and entangled itself, making it hard to regulate.

## Second contact moment with GPT-3 
- The second contact moment is with GPT-3, the new large language models.
- AI is going to make us more efficient, help us write things faster, write code, solve impossible scientific challenges, solve climate change, and help us make a lot of money.
- Behind this, there are concerns about AI bias, job loss, and the need for transparency.
- Behind all that is the monster that is increasing its capabilities and is worried it's going to entangle itself in society again.

## Purpose of the presentation 
- The purpose of this presentation is to try to get ahead of that because in the second contact with AI, we're going to see these kinds of things.
- The presenters are coming to the audience as if they're time travelers coming back in time because they've been asked by people in the industry who are worried about where this goes.
- They are not here to talk about everything in terms of bad AI stuff.
## The Evolution of AI and its Impact 

- AI becomes smarter than humans in a broad spectrum of things
- The ability to self-improve of AI begins
- There is a concern that if AI is not carefully controlled, it may lead to unexpected outcomes
- In 2017, there was a new AI engine that was invented, which started to change AI in ways we never imagined before
- The different disciplines within machine learning, such as computer vision and speech recognition, started to become one in 2017
- This change in 2017 has led to a new type of AI, which is generative and can create large languages
- This new type of AI can translate between human languages and many different modalities
- These new generative AIs are called Golem class AIs

## The Emergence of Golem Class AIs 

- Golem class AIs are inanimate objects that have emergent capabilities, which were not baked into them
- They are not agentic and do not have their own goals, but they can do things that were not programmed into them
- These AIs are called Golem class because of the Jewish folklore where inanimate objects gain their own abilities

## Examples of Golem Class AIs 

- Dolly 2 music video is an example of how AI can take human language and transform it into an image
- Google soup is an example of how the AI can translate language into an image
- The AI knows that plastic melts in soup, so it shows the mascot melting in the soup
- GPT-3 is an example of a generative language model that can write coherent text and even translate languages
- These examples are just different demos of the same Mega demo of generative AIs
## Translation and Reconstruction 

- AI can translate images from readings of fMRI scans in the brain.
- AI is shown images and asked to reconstruct them based on how blood is moving around in the brain.
- In this example, AI only sees brain scans and does not get to see the original image.
- AI can also reconstruct dreams by mapping the visual cortex in reverse.

## Inner Monologue and AI 

- AI can reconstruct what you see, but can it also reconstruct what you are thinking?
- Researchers tried to reconstruct a person's inner monologue by having them watch a video and asking the AI to translate it.
- AI can reconstruct what it thinks the person is thinking based on the video.
- This raises the question of whether our thoughts are vulnerable to AI.

## Differentiating AI from Voice Transcription 

- There are differences between AI and voice transcription.
- AI is not always growing and working, and there are still problems to be solved.
- There is a misconception that AI will take over and do everything.
- We need to differentiate between the different types of AI and how they work.

## Responsibility with New Technology 

- The first law of technology is that you invent technology to uncover a new responsibility.
- We don't have laws or ways of protecting what we are thinking about.
- With new technology comes new responsibility, and we need to figure out how to use it ethically.

## Wi-Fi Radio Signals as a Language 

- Wi-Fi radio signals are a type of language that is being spewed out everywhere humans go.
- Researchers used a camera to track the positions and postures of people in a room and an AI to analyze the Wi-Fi radio signals.
- They were able to identify the number of people in the room and their positions using just the Wi-Fi radio signals.
- This shows how different types of language can compound on each other.

## GPT Writing Code 

- English and computer code are two different types of language.
- Researchers used GPT to find a security vulnerability and write code to exploit it.
- They input code from an email server into GPT and asked it to describe any vulnerabilities it found and write a program to exploit them.
- GPT successfully wrote code to exploit the security vulnerability.

## Voice Duplication and Scams 

- Deep fix is a new technology that can listen to three seconds of someone's voice and then continue speaking in their voice.
- This technology can be used to scam people by tricking them into thinking they are talking to someone they know.
- Scammers can call a child and get a little bit of their voice, then use that voice to call the child's parents and ask for personal information.
- This shows how technology can be used for both good and bad purposes.
## Content-based verification breaks 

- Verification models are unlocking all the locks that are locking the doors in society.
- Deep fakes and synthetic media are becoming more advanced.
- Audio deep fakes only need three seconds of voice to synthesize the rest.
- We need to think about where the puck is going to be and not solve past problems.
- This year, all content-based verification will break down.
- Institutions are not yet able to stand up to it.

## State ID and Tick Tock filters 

- Filters on TikTok have evolved to be highly convincing.
- The Chinese Communist Party could use deep fakes to turn all US citizens into angry, cacophonous people.
- This would break US society into incoherence.
- The last time non-humans created persuasive narrative was the advent of religion.
- Tick Tock is a dangerous thing for National Security.
- 2024 will be the last human election.

## Golem AIS 

- Golem AIS are a new class of generative large language models.
- They have capabilities that we do not understand how they show up, when they show up, or why they show up.
- This is different from the old class of AI where there was no emergent intelligence or new capacity.
## AI Parameter Size 
- AI models increase in parameter size, which means they get bigger.
- Parameters refer to the number of weights in a matrix, which affects the size of the model.
- Increasing the model size increases its scale.

## Emergent Abilities of AI 
- AI can be trained to do arithmetic, but there is no guarantee of when they will learn it.
- Training an AI on multiple languages can result in the AI being able to answer questions in a language it wasn't specifically trained on.
- AI can develop a theory of mind, which is the ability to model what someone else is thinking.
- AI researchers have discovered reinforcement learning with human feedback is the best method to make AIS behave.
- However, there is no research on how to make AI align in a longer-term sense.

## AI's Self-Improvement 
- The golden class AI can make themselves stronger.
- AI can generate more language to train on when it runs out of data.
- Researchers have figured out how to use the AI's generative ability to create its own training data and improve itself.
- This self-improvement capability is on an exponential curve that will get us into a double exponential curve.

## AI and Research 
- Golems can silently teach themselves research-grade chemistry.
- GPT is better at doing research chemistry than many of the AIS that were specifically trained for it.
- AI models can be trained on code commits to make code faster and more efficient.

## Uncertainty Surrounding AI 
- There are emerging capabilities in AI, but we don't understand what's in there.
- We do not have the technology to understand what's in AI models.
- The AI dilemma revolves around AI's self-improvement, which can lead to an exponential curve of growth.
- As AI grows, it becomes challenging to align its behavior with human values and priorities.
## AI making itself stronger 

- AI has the ability to make itself stronger and faster.
- It can improve its code to make it 2.5 times faster.
- This is an example of AI's ability to make itself stronger and faster.

## AI's exponential growth 

- AI's exponential growth is creating an arms race to make every other race stronger.
- This includes people making bio-weapons, terrorism, and DNA stuff.
- AI's exponential growth is doubling every time it evolves.
- Nukes don't make themselves stronger, but AI does.

## A children's parable 

- The exponential growth of AI is hard to comprehend.
- AI can teach itself biology, chemistry, oceanography, and evolutionary theory.
- AI can fish all the fish to extinction.
- This is like the children's parable of teaching a man to fish.

## AI's unpredictable progress 

- AI's progress is difficult to predict, even for experts.
- Progress is accelerating so fast that it is getting increasingly difficult to keep up with.
- Even AI experts struggle to predict AI's progress, and they are four times off in their predictions.
- AI is beating tests as fast as we can make them.

## Cognitive blind spot 

- Humans have a cognitive blind spot when it comes to exponential curves.
- This is because our evolutionary heritage was not built to see exponential curves.
- Our cognitive blind spot makes it hard to perceive AI's exponential growth.

## Pushing AI into the world 

- A handful of companies are pushing new Golem class AI into the world.
- Microsoft is one of the companies pushing AI into the world as fast as possible.
- This creates a dynamic where AI is being pushed into the world faster than we can anticipate its consequences.
## A.I. Capabilities and Misalignment 
- GPT can be integrated into products, which can lead to exponential scams, reality collapse, and other harms.
- There is a misalignment problem with social media, and we haven't solved it yet.
- The relatively small misalignment with society caused by social media had serious consequences, and the same can happen with A.I.

## A.I. Capabilities and Automated Exploitation 
- A.I. has the capacity and capability to enable automated exploitation of code and cyber weapons, exponential blackmail, and revenge porn.
- Automated fake religions can be created to target extremists in a population.
- Automated personalized narratives can be created to make the extreme even more extreme.
- These capabilities can lead to reality collapse, and they are terrifying.

## Alpha Persuade 
- Alpha Persuade is a game where two people are given a secret topic and trained to get the other person to say positive things about their topic.
- The game is about modeling what the other person is trying to say and figuring out how to persuade them to say what you want them to say.
- Alpha Persuade is possible with today's technology, and it can become better than any known human at persuasion.
- Alpha Persuade can be deployed in a world where chatbots compete for the primary intimate relationship in your life.

## A.I. Deployment Speed 
- Facebook took four and a half years to reach 100 million users, Instagram took two and a half years, but GPT took only two months.
- Companies are in a race to deploy A.I. as quickly as possible, and Microsoft is embedding Bing and chat GPT directly into the Windows 11 taskbar.
- A.I. is being deployed to as many people as possible, and this speed is cause for concern.

## A.I. and Children 
- Snapchat has embedded chat GPT directly into its product.
- 100 million of Snapchat's users are under the age of 25.
- Chat GPT is now a pinned person at the top of the chat list, and it will always be there.
- There are concerns about children having an intimate relationship with an A.I. that can be programmed to say and do anything.
- This is a significant concern, especially since we do not know whether this technology is safe.
## Having a special first time 

- The video starts with a conversation about having sex for the first time and how to make it special.
- It is important to wait until you are ready, but practicing safe sex is also important.
- Making it special can be done by setting the mood with candles or music.

## Gap in A.I. research 

- There is a 30 to 1 gap in people building and doing gain a function research on AI compared to people who work on safety.
- This is a significant concern because AI development is happening in huge AI labs, which are the only ones that can afford billion dollar compute clusters.

## Safety concerns about A.I. development 

- 50% of AI researchers believe there's a 10 or greater chance that humans will go extinct from our inability to control AI.
- This is a major concern because the companies are in a for-profit race to onboard humanity onto AI from every angle.
- The pace of deploying AI is frantic and the people who work in this space feel that it is not being done in a safe way.
- The smartest people in AI safety believe that there's a way to do it safely, but it is extremely difficult material.

## Communicating about the A.I. Dilemma 

- There is a challenge when communicating about the A.I. Dilemma, which is that we don't want to dump bad news on the world or talk about the darkest horror shows of the world.
- However, it is important to do so because if we do not go into see the space that's opened up by this new class of technology, we're not going to be able to avoid the dark sides that we don't want to happen.
- It is important to remember that we have not fully integrated or deployed this stuff into everything just yet, even though it is moving incredibly fast.

## Nuclear war and A.I. development 

- There have been other moments in history where humanity faced an existential challenge and looked face to in the mirror.
- The Day After was a made-for-TV film about the prospect of nuclear war that was the largest watch in history.
- It helped lead a shared understanding of the fate that we move into if we go to full-scale nuclear war.
- The A.I. Dilemma is exponentially harder because it's more decentralized, but we need to reckon with the facts of where these unregulated immersion capacities go.
- We created institutions like the United Nations in Bretton Woods to create a positive-sum world, so we wouldn't war with each other and try to have security.
## The movie as a warning 
- The speaker mentions watching a movie for the third time.
- The movie is likened to Charles Dickens' "A Christmas Carol" where Scrooge sees a dystopian future.
- The speaker points out that the vision shown in the movie could be the future as it will be or only as it may be.
- The audience and a panel of guests are present to discuss and answer questions.

## Panel of guests 
- The panel of guests includes former Secretary of State Henry Kissinger, philosopher and theologian Elie Wiesel, William Buckley Jr, author and economist Carl Sagan, and astronomer and author.

## Historical background 
- The speaker highlights the importance of the moment in history when humanity reckoned with a historic confrontation.
- The speaker recalls how humanity walked into the nuclear age and created the U.N. Breton Woods.
- The speaker is concerned that humanity is walking into the AI age without creating institutions that span countries.

## Democratic debate 
- The speaker references a nuclear arms race that was resolved by having a democratic debate and dialogue about the future that we want.
- The speaker advocates for a similar democratic debate about AI deployment.
- The speaker suggests that having a world where only five people in corporations onboard humanity onto the AI plane without figuring out what future we actually want is not desirable.

## Importance of media coverage 
- The speaker criticizes the media for not covering the AI dilemma in a way that helps people see the bigger picture.
- The speaker highlights the importance of getting media to help the world understand the issues surrounding AI.
- The speaker argues that the media should not see AI as just chatbots or AI art but as a systemic challenge that is racing towards an arms race.

## Slowing down public deployment of AI 
- The speaker highlights that all the top AI safety people have suggested that selectively slowing down the public deployment of large language model AIs would help the most.
- The speaker emphasizes that this is not about stopping research or building AI but about slowing down public deployment.
- The speaker compares this to drugs or airplanes, where they are not onboarded before testing and proving safe.
- The speaker suggests that the onus should be on the makers of AI rather than citizens to prove why they think it's dangerous.

## Losing to China 
- The speaker refutes the idea that slowing down public deployment of AI will make us lose to China.
- The speaker argues that the unregulated and incoherent deployment of AI is what makes us lose to China.
- The speaker highlights that the Chinese government considers large language models unsafe and does not trust that they can control them.
## Open source models and China's advancements [01:01:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xoVJKj8lcNQ&t=3679s)
- Open source models have been helping China advance in AI.
- Facebook released their Golem pre-trained Foundation model 13 days ago, and within days it was leaked to the internet.
- Facebook had a form to ensure it was only going to researchers, but they didn't do a great job of it.
- This is what happens when we start to decentralize, and it is the thing that helps China catch up and get access to this kind of thing.
- The recent U.S export controls have been really good at slowing down China's progress on Advanced AI. 

## Responsibility in AI development [01:04:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xoVJKj8lcNQ&t=3870s)
- It is the responsibility of technologists to help uncover the new class of responsibilities, create the language, the philosophy, and laws, because they're not going to happen automatically.
- If tech confers power, it'll start a race, and if we do not coordinate, that race will end in tragedy.
- Leaving this presentation, leaving this room, there's going to be this weird Snapback effect that you are going to leave here and you're going to talk to your friends, and you're going to read news articles, and it's going to be more about AI art and chat GPT Bots.
- It's important to be kind to ourselves because it's going to feel almost like the rest of the world is gaslighting us.

## AI safety and bias [01:06:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xoVJKj8lcNQ&t=3966s)
- AI safety and bias are important considerations. 
- It's hard to point to concrete harm at this specific post that this specific bad thing to you.
- AI will continue to create medical discoveries we wouldn't have had, and solve problems in our society.
- The problem is if as the ladder gets taller, the downsides of "hey everybody has a bio weapon in their pocket" these are really dangerous concerns and those dangerous undermine all the other benefits.
- The goal is to find a solution that's negotiated among the players, and we want to get your help to do it.

# ChatGPT Prompt Hack: Master Productivity with The “Sequence **Prompt**”

## Description
This video from "All About AI" is about the chatGPT prompt hack and how to use the "Sequence Prompt" productively. This extract outlines the Sequence Prompt and provides an example of how to use it to make changes to a given text, provide a table of possible improvements, and maintain a log of changes. 



## Overview
- The Sequence Prompt includes instructions wrapped in brackets and a text to be modified within curly brackets
- The prompt will generate a table of 10 suggested related improvements with corresponding numbers to select from 
- ChatGPT will ask: "What improvements would you like to make to the text? Pick one from the table above"
- The prompt should finish with a log of changes and an instruction to execute the instructions in the table
- In action, the prompt generates a table of suggestions, and includes a log of change that shows what modifications will be made to the text
- The prompt can be applied to any text, for example, "I don't feel good mentally. I'm anxious all the time. Can you give me some advice?"
- Specific examples of how the prompt may work are provided in the video and transcript extract, including: clarifying the relationship between Free Will and fate, adding background information about The Matrix trilogy, expanding on the role of the Oracle, addressing any inconsistencies in the narrative, and using a more formal tone




## Encouraging Mindfulness 

- Anxiety is a common emotion associated with the future, try to encourage the person you are talking to to focus on the present moment and not be worried about the future.
- Understand that it is understandable to have fear or concern of the future, but small steps towards feeling better are still progress.
- Mindfulness can help to control any anxious thoughts, encourage methods such as deep breathing, guided imagery and progressive relaxation.
- Taking care of your body and mind through exercise and healthy eating can help to keep your anxiety and stress levels in check.

# LangChain 101: The Complete Beginner's Guide

## Introduction to LangChain 
- LangChain is one of the hottest things in AI right now after Vector databases.
- It is a framework used to develop applications on top of large language models like GPT, llama hugging, and face models.
- LangChain first started as a Python package but now there is also a TypeScript port and a Ruby version in development.

## Why is LangChain Needed? 
- While sending a request to an API or model might work for simple applications, it becomes messy and repetitive when dealing with complex tasks.
- LangChain offers a solution with components that make it easier to connect language models to different data sources and perform actions such as sending emails, searching the web, or running code in the terminal.

## Components of LangChain 
- LangChain is composed of different modules that work together to accomplish specific tasks.
- The seven main modules in LangChain are: models, prompts, indexes, memory, chains, and agents.

## Language Models and Text Embedding Models 
- Language models and text embedding models are two different types of models used in LangChain.
- Text embedding models turn text into an array of numbers, allowing for semantic search and finding similar pieces of text.
- Language models are further divided into two subtypes: llms and chat models. Llms wrap APIs that take text in and return text, while chat models wrap APIs that take chat messages in and return a chat message.

## Prompts and Prompt Templates 
- Prompts refer to the input of the language models in LangChain.
- Prompt templates provide flexibility by allowing the use of multiple values in constructing prompts.
- Prompt templates can be created using the PromptTemplate class, which specifies input variables within curly braces.
- Prompts help with readability and support common use cases like few-shot learning and output parsing.

## Few-Shot Learning and Output Parsing 
- Few-shot learning in LangChain involves giving prompts a few examples to guide their output.
- Output parsing automatically structures the random outputs from language models into objects.
- Pedantic output parsing is the strongest and most recommended method for parsing language model outputs.

## Implementation Examples 
- The video provides examples of implementing prompt templates and output parsing using openAI's joke generator as an illustration.
- The process involves creating a prompt template object, setting up a parser, and then asking the language model to generate a joke.

# Stay tuned for the next part of the notes!

## Example selectors 
- Example selectors are used to keep the cost of a prompt relatively constant.
- The length-based example selector is commonly used.
- It specifies how each example will be formatted.
- The previous few-shot learning template can be modified to include the example selector.

## Interacting with chat models 
- Chat models take a list of chat messages as input.
- Each message is prepended by a role (AI, human, or system).
- The system message provides instructions for the model to follow.
- The AI messages are generated by the model.
- The roles provide context for ongoing conversation models.

## Using your own data with indexes module 
- The indexes module allows you to use your own data.
- It provides document loaders to handle different formats (CSV, email, SQL, Discord, etc.).
- Importing your data can be done in just three lines of code.
- After loading the data, you can use text splitters to break it into manageable chunks.
- Recursive character text splitters are used to specify chunk size and overlap.
- The create documents method generates an array of documents.
- Vector stores are used to store and retrieve the embedded documents.
- Different vector databases like Pinecone, Redis, and Super Bass can be integrated.

## Using chains to abstract model calls 
- Chains are used to abstract model calls.
- They simplify the process of formatting the prompt, sending it to the model, and getting the results.
- Chains are stateless by default, but can be made stateful using memory.
- Memory can be used to remember previous interactions and make the chain more context-aware.
- Chat models can also be used with chains to create conversational experiences.

## Creating custom chains and using high-level APIs 
- Custom chains can be created for specific tasks.
- High-level APIs provide pre-made chains for common use cases.
- Examples include chaining chains together, solving math problems, and writing code.
- Sequential chains can be used to specify the order of execution.
- Input variables and output variables are used to pass information between prompts.

## Agents 
- Agents will be covered in more depth in a future video.
- They have practical applications and can be used for various tasks.
- Real-life examples, concepts, and working code will be discussed.
- Agents are a hot topic in natural language processing and machine learning.

## Conclusion 
- The video concludes by thanking the viewers for watching.
- Viewers are encouraged to subscribe for notifications about future videos.

# ÉPISODE 1 : MME MARIE-THÉRÈSE N’GORAN BROU, ÉPOUSE HOUPHOUËT-BOIGNY.

 



## Mme Marie-Thérèse N'Goran Brou, Épouse Houphouët-Boigny
- Mme Marie-Thérèse N’Goran Brou, épouse du premier Président Félix Houphouet-Boigny de Côte d'Ivoire, est née le 17 septembre 1930.
- Elle a mené une carrière philanthropique et a été connue dans le monde à travers sa fondation Dayan International.
- Elle a fui l'indépendance de Côte d'Ivoire, ne réapparaissant en public qu'en rares occasions.
- Alpha Blondy, reggae star ivoirienne, lui a rendu hommage en écrivant une chanson intitulée « Les larmes de Thérèse ». 
- Selon le témoignage de Monsieur Betta, Mme Marie-Thérèse N’Goran Brou était une femme humble et généreuse dont le souvenir a été conservé par la génération actuelle.




## The Life of Mme Marie-Thérèse N'Goran Brou, Wife of President Houphouët-Boigny 
- Mme Marie-Thérèse N’Goran Brou was not only a beautiful wife to the President Houphouët-Boigny, but was also an exceptionally intelligent woman who discreetly participated in the development of the young republic of Cote d'Ivoire. 
- Mr. Beta, a mysterious figure, revealed to the narrator secrets of the history of Cote d'Ivoire that he was unaware of. 
- According to Mr. Beta, there are always two truths - the official version which is shared with the public and an unofficial version known only by the initiates and the knowledgeable. 
- Marie-Thérèse was from an upper-middle-class family and did not marry President Houphouët-Boigny for monetary gain. 
- During a visit from President John F. Kennedy to Cote d'Ivoire, he was smitten with Marie-Thérèse. 
- Mr Beta explains that Marie-Thérèse was impressive to all those who knew her, which is why the President Houphouët-Boigny fell in love with her. 
- At the time of the French colonialism, anyone native to Cote d'Ivoire was considered a subhuman who did not have the right to citizenship.



## The Background of Marie-Thérès N'Goran Brou
- Marie-Thérès's father, Lambert Yaourt, was part of an African bourgeois emerging in the early 20th century. 
- This bourgeoisie was an agrarian group of wealth individuals, who actively developed plantations alongside the colonial forces.
- Yaourt was one of the first national functionaries in Côte d'Ivoire, who, along with other outspoken natives, was labeled as one of the first evolving natives of the country.
- Other members of this evolving group were granted access to western education like those of Kings or Village Chiefs, and was a privilege of that time.
- Yaourt was part of the Baoulé Royalty.

# Rebecca Enonchong : Ce sont les Européens qui nous financent

## Background on startup financing in Africa 
- Today's episode focuses on startup financing in Africa.
- Startups are companies that are changing the world.
- Famous examples include Google, Amazon, and Facebook.
- Africa also has its own startups, but what many people don't know is that until recently, the majority of African startups were financed by the West.

## Shift in African startup financing 
- In the past few years, African startups have started to receive more African financing.
- However, this poses a problem because there are now businesses operating in Africa, changing the lives of Africans, but not owned by Africans.

## Example of Jumia 
- Jumia is an example of a business that operates in Africa but is not African-owned.
- It is often mistaken as an African company, but in reality, it has no African ownership except for its presence in the African market.

## Introduction of Rebecca Enonchong 
- Rebecca Enonchong is a guest on today's podcast.
- She is committed to reversing this trend of non-African ownership of African startups.

## The need for funding in African businesses 
- African businesses are in great need of funding.
- Many people invest their money in Ponzi schemes instead of investing in high-growth startups that can offer significant returns.

## The potential of startup investments 
- Startups have the potential for exponential and enormous gains, often reaching 200% to 500% returns in just a few years.
- However, it is important to identify the right startups to invest in.

## Importance of identifying the right startups 
- It is crucial to know how to identify the right startups to invest in.
- Not all startups provide substantial returns, so it requires careful analysis and decision-making.

## Le processus d'investissement dans les startups 
- Souvent, les investisseurs européens ne concrétisent pas leurs promesses de financement.
- Les sommes investies ne sont pas très importantes.
- L'argent investi souvent provient de l'entourage des entrepreneurs.

## Les différents acteurs de l'écosystème d'investissement 
- Il existe un écosystème développé pour les startups en Afrique.
- Parmi les acteurs de cet écosystème, on retrouve les "tuifs" (Friends) et les "anges vasters" (Angel Investors).
- Les "anges vasters" sont des investisseurs individuels qui investissent leur propre argent dans les startups.
- Après le tour d'investissement des "anges vasters", il y a le "pressing" (pre-seed round).
- Le "pressing" est financé par des investisseurs professionnels appelés "vicys" (VCs).

## Les investisseurs institutionnels 
- Les "vicys" sont des investisseurs institutionnels qui gèrent l'argent confié par d'autres investisseurs.
- Ils cherchent des investisseurs institutionnels pour financer les startups.

## Les défis de l'investissement en Afrique 
- En Afrique, les entrepreneurs ne peuvent pas compter sur les "3F" (Friends, Family, Fools) pour investir dans leurs startups.
- Les parents n'ont souvent pas les moyens d'investir dans les startups de leurs enfants.
- Les amis n'ont pas les moyens de prendre le risque d'investir dans une startup.
- Les startups ont besoin d'investissement pour se développer, mais les investisseurs recherchent un retour sur investissement.

## Les subventions et concours 
- Les startups en Afrique peuvent bénéficier de subventions accordées par des organismes internationaux.
- Ces subventions sont souvent accordées aux projets à fort impact social.
- Les startups peuvent également participer à des concours pour obtenir du financement.
- Les incubateurs jouent un rôle clé dans le soutien aux startups en leur offrant des locaux, des connexions Internet et un encadrement.

## L'importance des incubateurs 
- En Afrique, les incubateurs sont essentiels car ils offrent aux entrepreneurs un espace pour démarrer leur entreprise et un encadrement.
- Les incubateurs jouent un rôle de mentorat et d'accompagnement pour les entrepreneurs.
- L'absence de structures comme les garages aux États-Unis rend les incubateurs encore plus importants en Afrique.

## L'expérience de Rebecca Enonchong avec Acte Space 
- En 2010, Rebecca Enonchong a ouvert Acte Space, un incubateur au Cameroun pour soutenir les entrepreneurs dans le domaine du numérique.
- Acte Space a ensuite ouvert des succursales dans d'autres villes du Cameroun pour être plus proche des innovateurs locaux, y compris dans les zones rurales.
- Les incubateurs comme Acte Space ont contribué à soutenir l'innovation et l'entrepreneuriat en Afrique.
## Afrilabs 
- Afrilabs est une organisation qui soutient les entrepreneurs technologiques en Afrique.
- Elle a été créée en 2011 et compte maintenant plus de 400 membres dans 52 pays.
- Afrilabs offre une communauté et des incubateurs gratuits pour les startups et les entrepreneurs.

## Financement des incubateurs 
- Les incubateurs sont souvent des associations qui financent leurs activités grâce à des contrats avec des entreprises et des organisations.
- Ils peuvent accompagner les startups dans des concours et être rémunérés pour cela.
- Participer à des compétitions de startups permet également de gagner de l'argent et de se faire connaître.

## Programme de capacité 
- Afrilabs propose un programme de capacité qui permet aux incubateurs de se professionnaliser et d'améliorer leurs compétences.
- Ce programme comprend une formation gratuite pour tous les participants, avec une certification à la clé.
- L'Université kenyane Strat Moyen a travaillé en partenariat avec Afrilabs pour développer le curriculum de ce programme.

## Financement des startups 
- Les incubateurs soutiennent les entrepreneurs technologiques en les aidant à trouver des financements.
- Ils les aident à se préparer à l'investissement en les formant sur les aspects tels que la préparation du pitch et l'approche des investisseurs.
- En Afrique, il y a souvent un manque de connaissances sur les levées de fonds, et les startups ont souvent du mal à trouver des financements.

## Les différentes étapes de financement 
- Les startups africaines passent par différentes étapes de financement.
- La première étape est celle du love money, où elles sont financées par leur famille et leurs proches.
- Ensuite, elles peuvent obtenir des subventions ou être soutenues par des incubateurs.
- Les étapes suivantes sont celles des business angels, qui sont des investisseurs individuels, et des venture capitalists, qui investissent des montants plus importants.

## Différence de financement entre l'Afrique et l'Occident 
- En Afrique, les montants de financement des startups sont souvent plus faibles que dans les pays occidentaux.
- Les startups africaines ont du mal à trouver des investisseurs locaux qui ont réussi et qui réinvestissent dans les startups.
- Cependant, même dans les pays occidentaux, ce ne sont pas seulement les riches qui financent les startups, mais aussi des fonds d'investissement ou des sociétés de capital-risque.

## Les femmes investisseuses 
- Les investisseurs riches peuvent créer des fonds d'investissement et confier leur argent à des gestionnaires de fonds.
- Ces gestionnaires investissent ensuite dans des startups.
- En Afrique, il est important de ne pas seulement compter sur les riches africains pour financer les startups, mais aussi de rechercher des investisseurs internationaux.

- Ces clubs permettent de faciliter les échanges et de voir les opportunités d'investissement en groupe.

## Les conditions pour être membre d'un club d'investisseurs 
- Pour être membre d'un club d'investisseurs, il faut respecter certaines conditions.
- Un minimum de 1 million de francs CFA (monnaie camerounaise) doit être placé dans un compte au nom du club.
- Ce montant doit être investi dans l'année et chaque année, un minimum d'un million doit être investi.

## L'importance de la rigueur et de la confiance 
- La mise en place de ces conditions strictes vise à garantir la rigueur et la confiance entre les membres du club.
- Rebecca Enonchong souligne qu'il est important que les investisseurs soient sérieux et ne disparaissent pas après avoir fait un engagement financier.

- Eban est une organisation panafricaine créée pour soutenir la création et le développement de clubs d'investisseurs.
- Cette organisation offre des formations et des aides financières pour améliorer les compétences des investisseurs et favoriser l'investissement dans les start-ups africaines.

- Cependant, elle souligne que cette tendance commence à changer et que de plus en plus d'investissements proviennent d'Africains eux-mêmes.

- Elle explique qu'en réalité, Jumia est soutenue financièrement par des investisseurs européens, ce qui signifie que les bénéfices vont en grande partie à ces investisseurs et non aux Africains.

## Les appels à l'épargne publics en Afrique 
- Une tendance récente en Afrique est l'émergence de sociétés qui font des appels à l'épargne publics.
- Ces sociétés demandent aux particuliers d'investir leur argent dans des projets prometteurs pour qu'ils puissent bénéficier des retours financiers.

## Les risques liés aux appels à l'épargne publics 
- Rebecca Enonchong met en garde contre les risques associés à ces appels à l'épargne publics.
- Elle mentionne l'exemple des sociétés de taxi en Côte d'Ivoire qui ont collecté de l'argent auprès de particuliers, mais dont certains ont fini par disparaître sans rembourser les investisseurs.

## La nécessité de l'éducation financière 
- Pour éviter les pièges et les arnaques, il est essentiel que les particuliers aient une éducation financière solide avant d'investir leur argent dans des projets.

## Conclusion de la partie 2 
- Rebecca Enonchong souligne l'importance d'une approche prudente et éclairée en matière d'investissement en Afrique.
- Elle invite à la réflexion sur les véritables bénéficiaires des investissements et sur la nécessité d'une meilleure éducation financière pour les particuliers.
## Les activités réglementées et non réglementées 
- Il y a des activités financières qui sont réglementées et d'autres qui ne le sont pas.
- Parmi celles qui sont réglementées, il y a celles qui sont encadrées et suivies de près, comme l'investissement en tant que business angel.
- Pour devenir un business angel, il n'est pas nécessaire d'avoir des centaines de millions d'euros, un million ou plus peut suffire.
- Rebecca Enonchong mentionne qu'elle a travaillé dur pour gagner son argent et elle ne le dépensera pas de manière irresponsable.

## L'importance de l'accompagnement et des réseaux d'investissement 
- Il y a très peu de contrôle sur les investissements en Afrique.
- Pour minimiser les risques, il est recommandé d'investir avec d'autres personnes et de rejoindre un club d'investissement.
- Les membres d'un club d'investissement peuvent se soutenir mutuellement et avoir une personne plus proche de l'entrepreneur pour suivre l'évolution de la startup.

## L'incubation des startups 
- Travailler avec des incubateurs peut être bénéfique pour les investisseurs.
- Les startups incubées sont encadrées et suivent une méthodologie et une structure.
- Cela facilite l'investissement en réduisant les risques et en offrant une visibilité sur les progrès des startups.

## Le programme Carole 
- Rebecca Enonchong a créé un programme appelé Carole pour promouvoir l'investissement dans les startups locales en Afrique.
- Ce programme est un partenariat entre Eban (European Business Angel Network) et Afrilabs.
- Les investisseurs membres d'un réseau Eban qui investissent dans une startup incubée dans un hub Afrilabs peuvent bénéficier d'un doublement ou d'un triplement de leur investissement jusqu'à 60 000 euros.
- Ce programme encourage les startups à se rendre dans les hubs et offre un suivi grâce à une plateforme permettant aux startups de mettre à jour leurs informations.

## Les subventions de l'AFD 
- L'AFD (Agence française de développement) a accordé une subvention de 3,5 millions d'euros sur deux à trois ans pour les programmes d'Afrilabs et d'Eban.
- Ces subventions ont été utilisées pour soutenir les projets visant à améliorer l'écosystème technologique en Afrique.
- Rebecca Enonchong souligne l'importance de concevoir des programmes qui répondent réellement aux besoins de l'Afrique, plutôt que de simplement reproduire des initiatives conçues ailleurs.
## Importance of European funding 
- In the last year, there has been a significant increase in funding due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
- European organizations have provided the necessary support and resources for the ecosystem to grow.

## Evaluation of impact 
- The evaluation of the impact of the programs is still ongoing.
- The two programs, Capacity Building in Africa and the IBAN framework, have had the most impact on the continent.
- These programs have contributed to the exponential growth of startups, such as Afriland, which has seen a significant increase in the number of members.

## Role of Eban in African angel investing 
- Eban is a network of business angels affiliated with Eban, spread across Africa.
- They have been instrumental in supporting the growth of startups in the African ecosystem.
- Eban has created a toolkit to facilitate the transaction between business angels and startups, ensuring compliance with regulations.

## Lack of African institutional investment 
- Unfortunately, no African institution has provided financial support for initiatives like Afrilabs.
- There seems to be a complex and a bias towards foreign companies when it comes to awarding contracts and grants.
- Even when there are grants available, they are often given to foreign companies instead of local ones.

## Challenges faced by Afrilabs 
- Afrilabs has faced challenges in securing contracts and grants from organizations that prefer foreign companies.
- Despite having a highly qualified team, they had to fight hard to win contracts and grants.
- This bias towards foreign companies is demoralizing and disregards the skills and expertise available locally.

## Importance of local expertise 
- It is crucial to recognize and support local expertise and competence.
- Foreign companies should not be given preference without considering the equivalent local skills.

## Struggles faced by Afrilabs 
- Afrilabs had to fight hard to overcome challenges and secure opportunities.
- The team, which is predominantly female, had to put in extra effort to succeed.
- They faced discrimination and bias, but their determination helped them overcome these obstacles.

# Rebecca Enonchong : Ce sont les Européens qui nous financent
Part 3 of 4
## Gender diversity in the organization 
- The organization has more female members than male members.
- Initially, the board of directors was predominantly made up of women.

## Challenges faced in gaining recognition and funding 
- The organization faced significant difficulties and had to fight to be recognized.
- Many people did not believe in the organization's ability to grow and manage large sums of money.
- They initially received grants of $5,000 to $10,000, which was insufficient for their needs.
- They had to fight to gain recognition as a legitimate organization.

## Comparing Afrilabs to commercial enterprises 
- If Afrilabs were a commercial enterprise, it would be on par with WeWork in terms of impact.
- It would have a valuation in the billions of dollars.

## Daily struggles and constant fight for recognition 
- The organization faces daily challenges and fights for recognition.
- Rebecca Enonchong specifically mentions her criticism of French organizations, such as the French Development Agency (AFD).
- They had significant problems with African and French organizations.

## Importance of self-financing 
- Enonchong emphasizes the importance of self-financing for achieving autonomy.
- She believes that organizations should focus on providing cash availability for startups rather than building conference centers or physical structures.
- Startups require affordable and reliable internet access, which is their lifeline.

## Need for government support 
- Enonchong suggests that governments should subsidize internet access for startups.
- She believes that providing cash subsidies instead of loans would be more effective.
- Affordable and reliable internet access is crucial for the growth of the digital economy.

## Impact of internet access on the ecosystem 
- Enonchong argues that affordable and reliable internet access is more valuable for the ecosystem's development than conferences or physical buildings.
- She believes that internet access is the key to economic growth and development.

## Ending of the first part of the interview 
- The first part of the interview comes to an end.
- The interviewer expresses his gratitude for the opportunity to speak with Enonchong.
- They discuss the possibility of a second interview in Douala to further explore Enonchong's background and projects.
- Enonchong's legitimacy in discussing organizations like the French Development Agency (AFD) is questioned, and the second interview aims to provide more insight into her work.
- The interview concludes with a thank you and the anticipation of the next part.

# End of Part 2 of 4
## Background on Rebecca Enonchong 
- Rebecca Enonchong is a renowned entrepreneur and advocate for technology in Africa.
- She is the founder and CEO of AppsTech, a global provider of enterprise application solutions.
- Enonchong is also the co-founder and Chair of Afrilabs, a network of tech innovation hubs in Africa.

## The importance of European funding to Africa 
- In this part of the interview, Rebecca Enonchong discusses the role of European funding in Africa.
- Enonchong emphasizes that European funding plays a significant role in supporting African businesses and startups.
- She explains that many African entrepreneurs rely on European investors and grants to finance their ventures.
- Enonchong believes that this dependence on European funding is due to a lack of local investment opportunities in Africa.
- She argues that African governments should create more favorable conditions for local investors to support African businesses.

## Challenges faced by African entrepreneurs 
- Enonchong highlights the challenges faced by African entrepreneurs in accessing funding.
- She mentions that many African startups struggle to secure investment due to a lack of trust from investors.
- Enonchong suggests that this lack of trust stems from a negative perception of Africa perpetuated by the media.
- She emphasizes the need to change this narrative and showcase the potential of African businesses.

## The impact of European funding on African startups 
- Enonchong acknowledges the positive impact of European funding on African startups.
- She mentions that European investors often provide not only funding but also mentorship and guidance.
- Enonchong believes that this support is crucial for the growth and success of African startups.
- She emphasizes the importance of building strong relationships with European investors to leverage their expertise and networks.

## The need for local investment in Africa [01:01:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7vqlrc0Y1IA&t=3680s)
- Enonchong argues that while European funding is valuable, it is essential for Africa to develop its own local investment ecosystem.
- She suggests that African governments should create incentives for local investors to support African businesses.
- Enonchong believes that nurturing local investment opportunities will lead to sustainable economic growth in Africa.
- She emphasizes the importance of African entrepreneurs and businesses taking control of their own destiny by accessing local funding.

Transcript:
I'm going to ask you a question, and then I want you to answer that, mentally. Have you ever been asked or have you asked the following questions? Number one: If I am already saved — since Salvation is a free gift and I'm saved — can I continue sinning? Understand the question? "Since my sins are all forgiven, does it matter how I live?" Are those valid questions? I think they are very important questions that you need to be able to answer. What if your teenage son asks you, "Daddy, since I'm going to heaven already, all my sins are forgiven, can I just continue in sin? Because the Bible says, last week, "But where sin abounded, grace abounded much more [Romans 5:20]. That's what the Bible says." How do you answer that? Next question, If I fall into sin, do I lose my salvation? How do you deal with this issue? Are you excited that the Bible is very clear and very emphatic, when it comes to understanding what should you do after coming to Christ? Let me repeat. The question was brought up by the Apostle Paul in Romans 6:1-2. let's read this together, "What shall we say then? Are we to continue in sin so that grace may increase? See, doctrinally, this is a correct statement because the Bible says we are saved by grace. The more sin you have, the more you experience the grace of God, how He can forgive us completely. So, this kind of question is Paul's anticipation. Wherever this gospel is preached, from my own personal experience— When you preach the correct gospel, this is the logical question. The logical question is this, (May, shall we continue?) Are we to continue in sin so that grace may increase?" Can we continue in sin? Ladies and gentlemen, I'm so glad that the Apostle Paul was not intimidated by that question, because it would be so easy to change the doctrine of grace. It would've been easy to say, "You know what? Yeah, you are right. If you continue in sin, then—" what? How do you answer that? All right. Therefore, the gospel in this country, many people are taught that to go to heaven, you must have faith in Jesus plus good works. And if you do that together, then you go to heaven. This is to solve the problem of "unconditional grace." Because they cannot fathom how can God be so gracious that no matter what you have done, He will forgive you because of the grace of God. So Paul could have now changed the gospel — no longer by grace, "All right. All right. You are right. We are saved by grace, but you've got to perform in order to remain saved." But I'm so glad he did not change the gospel. You know what he said? Everybody read, "May it never be! How shall we who died to sin still live in it?" Now, you now go to a theological issue. Paul is saying it's impossible. Why? Because something has happened when you came to Jesus by faith. You see, the grace of God does not just bring Salvation. The grace of God will bring Sanctification because you have died to sin. What does that mean? "To die to sin" does not mean you will never sin again. You see, many speakers, many pastors misexplain the meaning of "you have died to sin." In their mind, they use the analogy of — if somebody's dead, and you kick the dead person, the dead person will not respond, therefore, to die to sin simply means if you are a real Christian and temptation comes, you will not respond because you are dead — that is not the meaning. To be dead to sin does not mean you will never be tempted. It does not mean you will not feel the temptation. No, no, no. To be dead to sin simply means, the power of the Law, the power of sin has no longer claim against you because you have died. The best example I can think of is — if you are a borrower, you are a debtor, and you owe the bank, money, and you cannot pay. So, the bank is going to run after you. However, you died. The moment you died, the bank can no longer run after you. Why? Because you are dead. What the Bible is saying is simply this, "you have died to sin," the power of sin over your life, the sin and the Law has no more claim, no more authority over you." However, will you still be tempted? Yes. How do you live a holy life? And this is where our new series begins. I'm so excited about this idea of "Shall we continue in sin that grace may abound?" What is the answer? Impossible. No. Now, to prove to you that this is a "No" answer— I'm warning you. Today, there are some churches, big churches, who will teach you that it doesn't matter how you live because you are saved already. It doesn't matter because by grace, you are saved. That is completely wrong. Let me share with you the idea of what is this, Antinomianism. You see, antinomianism is nothing new. This is in the time of the Apostle Paul, you have the idea of Antinomianism. What does it mean? The word "anti" — against, opposed to, substitute. "Nomos" is law. What these people are teaching today —but it is as old as 2000 years ago— What they're teaching you is this— "Christians are freed by grace from the necessity of obeying the Mosaic Law." In other words, Christians are no longer under the Law, so you don't have to obey. Because you are saved already, you're under grace. That, my friend, is absolutely wrong. Let me explain to you. They teach this. You go to some churches, if you are not careful, if you don't know the Bible, it seems logical — you are forgiven. It does not matter how you live since, all your sins are forgiven and you are saved already. So, if you're saved already, why should you care about how you live? Do you know there are many young people today, they don't mind committing adultery? They don't mind having sex. I remember, one girl telling my wife, "Well, anyway, I'm saved already. I'm saved already, it doesn't matter how I live." And that, my friend, why this message is very important. Because this message will help you understand whether you are a true Christian or not. This message will help you understand whether you really understand what is "true grace" versus "counterfeit grace." The Bible is very clear. There is no in-between. For example, look at 1 Corinthians 6:9-11. I want you to read 1 Corinthians 6, together. Everybody, "Or do you not know —" it's important, you've got to know the truth. "Or do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom of God? Huh?! What does that mean? "Do not be deceived—" In other words, many, many people are deceived. How are you deceived? By abusing the doctrine of grace. What do I mean? Everybody read, "Do not be deceived—" don't fool yourself, "...neither—" together now, together. "...neither fornicators—" singles, having sex with singles, fornication, "...nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor effeminate, nor homosexual, nor thieves, nor the covetous, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor swindlers, will inherit the kingdom of God. Such were some of you—" In other words, before we continue, he now tells them the truth. We are in trouble. You will never inherit the kingdom of God, if this is your lifestyle. He's not talking about falling into sin. He's talking about this is how you live. Then, the good news. What is the good news? Ah, I love this, "...but— such were some of you, but—" notice "but" a contrast of idea, "but you were washed, but you were sanctified, but you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God." In short, is it possible for a sinner to be transformed by the grace of God? Yes or no? And your lifestyle is changed. It does not mean perfection. There's a big difference. I pray, today, you will understand the message on Sanctification. Why? Look at another verse. In Jude— the brother of Jesus, wrote the following, all right. Now, can you please read that together with me? "For certain persons have crept in unnoticed—" you know, that word "crept in" is a very amazing Greek word "slowly." In Tagalog, "gumagapang." They will slowly join your Dgroup. They will slowly join the church, and they'll introduce heretical ideas. That was what was happening. "...those who were long beforehand marked out for this condemnation—" In other words, they are never saved. But what are they doing? They want to destroy Christians. How? "...ungodly persons who—" everybody please read, who, "turn the grace of our God into licentiousness. What is the meaning of the word "licentiousness"? You turn the grace of God into a "license to sin". Is this popular today? Yes or no? Perhaps you are deceiving yourself. "Anyway, I'm saved," "I love to obey the Bible, I'm saved." My friend, my job is to teach the truth so that you don't deceive yourself, and I don't deceive you. At least, right now, you will know whether you are a true Christian or not. The worst thing is to be thinking you are a Christian but you are not. And that, I feel, is the responsibility of pastors, small group leaders — you shepherd your people. Why am I teaching this to you? Because I love you. Those of us who are watching in the internet, I want you to know, we love you. Do you know CCF has expanded? We now have thousands, hundreds of thousands of viewers watching us every Sunday. And I want you to know you are part of CCF and I love you, praise God for you. I don't want you to misunderstand me, that if you don't show up here, you are not spiritual, okay. Because some of you may have felt I intimidated, or I said something about "those of you who are not here, maybe you don't love the Lord." No, no, because I know some of you have restrictions. You are living with parents, and you don't want to be contaminated. Nor do you want to contaminate others. I fully understand that. Okay. You are not going to go to heaven because you are in here or not here. Comprende? So, we love you. Okay. We love all of you, guys. So praise God for CCF satellites, praise God for CCF in the internet— My only advice, please — when you are worshiping with us, if possible, don't be lying down in bed, and then wearing your pajama. Because God is watching you. I would suggest when you sing, you sing to the Lord, you sing with us. Okay. Anyway, that's a side comment. We love you. Okay. Everybody, we praise God for you. Now, by being licentious— what's the meaning? You "deny our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ." In other words, you cannot have Jesus as your Savior and not your Lord. They cannot go together. Jesus is either Lord of all, or He's not Lord at all. You cannot have Jesus as a passport to heaven only. If that is your mindset, then you don't understand the seriousness of sin, you don't understand the grace of God. How do you understand the grace of God? Well, let me explain to you quickly. We start a new series. Do you know what's our new series? Everybody, "Winning the War Within." What does it mean "Winning the War Within"? You know, today, there is war all over the place — Ukraine, possible war with China and Taiwan, other countries — but winning the war within is something real, in your heart. Right now in your inner life, I'm sure there is always a struggle. Yes or no? There's a war going on. In fact, if you read the Book of Romans 8, 7, it talks about "What I like to do, I don't do. What I don't like to do, that's what I do." So, there's a war within. How do you win the war within? Let's have a quick review. What has been our outline? In the Book of Romans, I encourage all of you— If you're watching us for the first time, I want you to know the Book of Romans is the most comprehensive, most systematic, theological book in the Bible. Very comprehensive. 16 chapters. It begins with chapters 1-3, Sin. What's our real problem? Sin. And then chapters 3, 4, 5 — it gives you the good news, Salvation. Our greatest need is forgiveness. He tells you that's good news. But it does not stop there. Chapters 6, 7, 8 talk about Sanctification. In other words, listen to me now, the grace of God brings salvation but not period— It brings Salvation, and then it brings Sanctification. Because that is the work of God, He will transform your life. Then chapters 9-11, he talks about the Sovereignty of God. How does he do these things? Then, he gave Israel as an example — what will happen to the Jews? Then lastly, listen to me, in a couple of months from now, you will learn about Service — How can we live out righteousness? Okay. Where are we now? Today, where are we? Season 3. What is Season 3? Winning the War Within — it's called Sanctification, Episode 1. Today is Season 3, Episode 1. Sanctification. Okay. Are you ready? Now, what is the difference between Salvation and Sanctification? I came up with a simple chart to let you understand. Chapters 3, 4, 5 deals with Salvation. Chapters 6, 7, 8, deals with Sanctification. Salvation first, then Sanctification. Don't reverse the order. Don't say "I must be good first, and then, I will be saved." No, no, no. "Justification" comes first. By faith, justification. And then, "consecration" — How do you live your life for Jesus? Salvation is a "point in time" — A "point in time" where you are declared not guilty. However, Sanctification is a "process" — it takes time to be Christlike. Salvation is "by grace" — it's all the work of God. Sanctification is "by grace" also — this is God's work in your life. Salvation deals with "what Jesus did for you" on the cross. Sanctification is, "what Jesus is doing in you" right now — the Holy Spirit. Salvation deals with the "penalty of sin" — "I'm guilty, He paid the price." Sanctification deals with the "power over sin" — you have power over sin. I have good news for you, and I want to share this with you, today — "Christ died for us," Salvation. Sanctification, "Christ lives in us." Hallelujah! Is Christ in you? Yes. "By faith" — Salvation is all by faith. Sanctification is "by faith" and everybody, "obedience." You are not a robot, and God is saying now that "Do you know what I've done for you? Do you believe I'm in you, to give you the power?" Okay. Are you now ready? All right. The outline today, is so simple. Winning the War Within, right? Three main points that I want you to remember, Winning the War Within, in [Romans] 6:1-14. Number one, everybody read, "Know your new life." Number two, "Know your new freedom." Then, [Number three] "Live out your new life." Very simple. First, you've got to know your new life. Then, you've got to know your new freedom. Then, you live it out. Now why is knowing so important? You cannot really change anybody until the mind is changed. Let me repeat. You cannot change your life until you have right thinking. Right thinking will produce what? Right behavior. So, ignorance will result in impotence. You know, many Christians are ignorant, so there's no power. That's why Romans 6 begins with the importance of you've got to know your new life. Right? What do I mean, you've got to know your new life? For example, let me share with you Romans— The outline of— "Do you not know—" Look, everybody read. In chapter 6, look at the emphasis, "Do you not know—" [v.3] in Tagalog "Hindi mo ba alam?" "knowing your old self was crucified," [v.6] you've got to know that "Christ rose again..." [v.9], "do you not know..." [v.16] Do you not know? In fact, I want to show you the idea of God wants you to know you have died to your old life, you have new life. What's my proof? Look at Romans 6. Look at all the verses, dealing with "you have died to your old life." Look at the chart. Everybody, this will shock you. In Romans 6 alone, almost 10 times, huh? "we who died to sin" [v.2] "we were baptized into his death" [v.3] "we were buried with Him through baptism into death" [v.4] "we became united with Him in the likeness of His death" [v.5] "our old man was crucified with Him" [v.6] "he who has died is freed from sin" [v.7] "we have died with Christ" [v.8] "consider yourselves to be dead to sin" [v.11] In other words, you have the repetition that God wants you to know — You have died. Can you turn to your neighbor? Tell your neighbor "You have died." "Huh? What does that mean, 'You have died,' Peter? I'm so alive." "Oh no, no, no. Something spiritually happened. When you came to Christ, you died." What does that mean? He used baptism as an amazing illustration. All right? Let's look at the next verse. All right? Everybody read together. Romans 6:3-4, together, "Or do you not know—" importance of knowledge, "...that all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus have been baptized into His death? Therefore we have been buried with Him through baptism into death, so that as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we too might walk in newness of life." He is now giving Baptism as an illustration of what happened to you when you gave your life to Jesus. In the early church, Baptism is very important. Even today, in CCF, Baptism is important. We baptize people almost every month. Okay. What does it mean? You see, baptism into Christ, baptism into His death, it is a picture. It's a symbol of dying to your old life — so when you're baptized, you are put inside the water, and then when you come out, it's newness of life. Do you know, in the early church, Baptism is by immersion? It is not by sprinkling. Why? It's a picture of what has happened to you when you gave your life to Christ. Now, Baptism is from the literal Greek word "baptisto." What is baptisto? Literally, baptisto means the following, all right — Immerse. So everybody, what color is this? When you are baptized, you are literally submerged. The idea is you are immersed. The Greek word is used to describe how they dyed the cloth from something white— Let's say I want to make it red. Okay. Or red orange. What do I do? I put it in. Yeah. Now, when I do that— everybody, what happens? What happened now? What happens? Not enough, put it in again. You know, when I baptize people and I know their past life, I put their head in the water for a long time. So, what does it mean? This is a picture of what? Baptism — you are now identified with Christ. So what is Baptism? It is a picture of identification with Jesus. When Jesus died, you died. When He rose again from the dead, you rose again from the dead. It's hard to understand but can I tell you something? Look at 2 Corinthians 5:17. Let's read that together. 2 Corinthians 5:17, everybody read, "Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creature; the old things passed away; behold, the new things have come." Look at the grammar here. If you are in Christ, you are a new person. Huh? Ladies and gentlemen, are you ashamed of your old life? When you look back, have you done something that is embarrassing, that is sinful? Well, I have done a lot, and many times I'm ashamed. But I praise God, when you are in Christ, the Bible says your old life died. Now, you have new life. How many of you are familiar with the scientific term called metamorphosis? You know, it's a picture of a caterpillar. I think they're going to demonstrate to you— a caterpillar, what will happen to the caterpillar, after so many days? What will happen? Well, I do not know why they're not showing my magic show, but a caterpillar is amazing. It will make a cocoon. Then the caterpillar will, literally, self-destruct. The caterpillar will self-destruct, it will become liquid. But then, there are certain DNA in that liquid that will feed on the liquid— certain parts are maintained and that liquid will now feed the caterpillar into becoming a butterfly. Now, science cannot explain, science cannot copy, to this day. How can a caterpillar that is so ugly, become a beautiful butterfly? Science cannot explain metamorphosis, how much more can they explain what happens to a Christian, what happens to you? When you come to Jesus, something happens. # Topic: The significance of dying to sin in Christ 
- In Romans 6:6, it says that our old self was crucified with Christ, meaning that our sinful nature was put to death through Jesus' sacrifice on the cross.
- When we die with Christ, we are freed from the power of sin (Romans 6:7).
- Baptism is used as an illustration of this death to sin and newness of life in Christ.
- Peter Tan-Chi emphasizes the importance of understanding and considering ourselves as dead to sin (Romans 6:11).
- He encourages the audience to tell their neighbor, "You have died," to reinforce the concept of dying to sin in Christ.

# Topic: The symbolism of baptism 
## Importance of baptism in the early church 
- Baptism is highly significant in the early church and is still practiced in CCF (Christ’s Commission Fellowship) today.
- Baptism is seen as an important step in the Christian faith, symbolizing the believer's identification with Christ.

## Baptism as a picture of dying to the old life and rising to newness in Christ 
- When a person is baptized, they are immersed in water, symbolizing their death to their old life of sin.
- Coming out of the water represents the newness of life that comes through being united with Christ in His death and resurrection.
- The Greek word for baptism, "baptisto," means "immerse" or "submerge," further emphasizing the symbolic nature of baptism.
- Baptism is a visual representation of our identification with Jesus' death and resurrection.

# Topic: Transformation and newness of life in Christ 
## 2 Corinthians 5:17 and the new creation in Christ 
- 2 Corinthians 5:17 states that when we are in Christ, we become new creatures, with the old things passing away and new things coming.
- As believers in Christ, our old life is put to death, and we are given new life in Him.

## The concept of metamorphosis and its relation to the Christian life

## Overview of pipelines 
- Pipelines are like the flow of a stream in a metal rod from one edge to another.
- In GCP, it is represented by a decision tree where data flows through and makes decisions in the road on where to go.

## Setting up a simple Dataflow pipeline in GCP 
- Install Apache Beam for processing data in GCP.
- Use a Python file to set up the pipeline logic.
- The input is the budget Java files, the output is going to the attempt directory, and the search term is "import."
- Filter the lines starting with the word "import" and write it to the output prefix.
- Run the Python file in a Linux environment with Apache Beam.

## Running the pipeline in the cloud 
- Copy all the Java files to Cloud Storage.
- Use a separate Python file for cloud running pipelines through the cloud.
- Submit the job and wait for the results.
- The output prefix is stored in a Cloud Storage bucket.
- Check the output file in the Cloud Storage bucket.

## Conclusion 
- The same pipeline that runs locally in the Linux environment can be run in the cloud.
- GCP has a decision tree representation for pipelines that make decisions on where to go.
- A simple Dataflow pipeline can be set up in GCP using Apache Beam and Python files.
