# Marché du travail en 2023 : quand les candidats font la loi !

## Difficulties in recruiting 
- This year, the difficulties in recruiting have increased.
- Pôle emploi has released a barometer on labor needs, which indicates the challenges faced by companies in finding manpower.
- The barometer, known as BMO, was published in June last year.
- Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are the largest recruiters in France.
- However, even though they account for 10% of establishments, they are struggling to hire employees.

## The increasing difficulty of recruitment 
- Finding suitable candidates has become increasingly challenging.
- The host asks if the viewers, whether employers or job seekers, have experienced this difficulty.

## Introduction of guests 
- Two experts in the field of employment have been invited to discuss the topic.
- Sophie de Menton, President of the Ethical Small and Medium-sized Enterprises Movement, and Didier Moineau, President of CPME 91 and Vice-President of CPME Île-de-France, are introduced.

## The perception of job seekers "making the law" 
- The host introduces the topic of the perception that job seekers have more power in the job market.
- It is suggested that recruitment has become more challenging due to the demands and expectations of candidates.

## Reality of the job market 
- The host asks if this perception matches the reality of the job market.
- Sophie de Menton is asked if she has observed this trend in her association.

## Difficulty in finding candidates 
- Sophie de Menton confirms that this is a recurring issue across various sectors.
- She mentions that even for positions like IT interns or babysitters, finding suitable candidates is a challenge.

## Analysis of the situation 
- Employers have tried to analyze the situation and find reasons for the difficulty in recruitment.
- The host mentions the argument that certain sectors, like the restaurant industry, need to offer higher wages.
- Sophie de Menton acknowledges the issue of purchasing power but also highlights a deeper cultural attitude towards work.

## Cultural attitudes towards work 
- Sophie de Menton explains that there has been a discourse in France that promotes a certain laziness and discourages the value of work.
- She suggests that this mindset needs to be addressed and the value of work should be emphasized.

## Importance of work 
- Didier Moineau agrees that there is a need to revalue and teach the importance of work.
- He mentions that while the government talks about creating more jobs, there is also a discussion about reducing the workweek to four days.
- He believes that work is essential for the country's development and should be prioritized.

## Comparison with other countries 
- Didier Moineau highlights the disparity in working hours between France and Germany.
- He mentions that France works 1600 hours compared to Germany's 2500 hours, indicating a problem in the French work culture.

## Revalorizing work 
- Didier Moineau emphasizes the need to revalue work and make it a priority.
- He believes that work should be taught and highlighted before anything else.

## Invitation for audience participation 
- The host invites viewers to join the discussion on the Sud Radio Facebook page.
- Viewers are encouraged to share their experiences and opinions on the topic of recruitment difficulties and the value of work.
## Sophie de Menton 
- Sophie de Menton is introduced as a speaker in the video.

## La semaine de quatre jours 
- The discussion moves to the topic of the four-day workweek.
- Sophie wants to share her thoughts on what Didier said about it.

## Exemple de la journée de travail de 12 heures 
- Sophie shares an example from her own experience.
- Her daughter-in-law works in a hospital and tells her that they have started doing 12-hour shifts.
- Sophie finds it astonishing because the standard workweek is 35 hours.

## Télétravail et ses avantages 
- The topic shifts to telecommuting and its benefits.
- Sophie mentions that telecommuting works well for some professions and she herself works with people who telecommute from abroad.

## 30% de la population française 
- Sophie mentions that 30% of the French population telecommutes.
- She believes that telecommuting is not suitable for all professions, but it works well for some.

## Les difficultés de recrutement 
- The discussion moves to the difficulties faced by employers in recruiting suitable candidates.
- Sophie asks Didier Monroe, who is the president of CPME (Confederation of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises) and vice-president of CPAM (Caisses Primaires d'Assurance Maladie, French health insurance system), about the real difficulties in recruitment that business owners share with him.

## Les vraies difficultés de recrutement 
- Sophie wonders if the difficulties in recruitment are due to the quality of work, mismatched profiles, or if there is a societal change happening after the crisis.

## Le changement sociétal brutal 
- Didier responds by mentioning that the crisis has brought about a societal change.
- He believes that the idea of telecommuting was sold as a dream for everyone, but in reality, not all professions are eligible for it.
- Didier argues that there is a disconnect between work and the workforce, where the connection and reciprocity that used to exist between employers and employees have been lost.

## La notion de travail et devoir 
- Didier suggests that there needs to be a reevaluation of the notion of work and its role in the economy.
- He questions what people should contribute to their country and the economy if they want to enjoy the benefits of consumption.

## La connexion entre l'emploi et l'employé 
- Didier argues that there is a lack of connection between employment and employees.
- He believes that people still want to work, but they want to work differently.
- Didier acknowledges that this is a simplification but emphasizes that employees have more power and influence in the workplace now.

## Les employés qui mettent leur loi 
- Sophie mentions that there is a perception that employees are now the ones who dictate terms in the workplace.
- She cautions against generalizing this perception and suggests that it may be a result of noise from certain quarters.

## Conclusion 
- The discussion concludes with the mention of the noise from certain quarters and the need for a more nuanced understanding of the changing dynamics in the job market.
## La mobilisation sociale 
- Un participant estime que lorsque seulement 1% de la population manifeste, cela ne représente pas les 99% restants.
- L'économie et le travail sont des sujets trop graves pour être pris à la légère.
- La CPME s'investit dans le projet France travail qui réunit les acteurs de l'emploi.
- Une réforme de l'éducation est proposée, avec la présence d'entreprises dans les établissements scolaires, afin de changer les mentalités et préparer les jeunes au marché du travail.

## Les métiers et l'importance du travail 
- Il est souligné que certains métiers, comme plombier, offrent des rémunérations plus élevées que des professions comme avocat.
- Les invités estiment qu'il est dommage de ne pas valoriser davantage ces métiers et d'expliquer aux jeunes les opportunités qu'ils offrent.

## Exemple d'une situation salariale 
- Une histoire réelle est racontée où un salarié reçoit une augmentation de salaire, mais perd des allocations et avantages, ce qui fait qu'il préfère revenir à son salaire précédent.
- Cette histoire met en évidence les complexités du système salarial et des allocations.

## Les conséquences de ne pas travailler 
- Il est mentionné qu'il y a des personnes qui préfèrent ne pas travailler car cela leur permet de conserver certaines allocations et avantages.
- Les invités estiment que cela ne peut pas être soutenu à long terme, car cela mettrait à mal le système des retraites et l'État.

## Le taux de chômage et le plein emploi 
- Le taux de chômage a baissé ces dernières années, mais il reste encore des demandeurs d'emploi qui ne sont pas employables pour diverses raisons.
- Le plein emploi est considéré statistiquement autour de 5% de chômage, mais il existe toujours une tension sur le marché de l'emploi entre l'offre et la demande.

# Conclusion
- Dans cette partie de la vidéo, on aborde la mobilisation sociale, l'importance du travail, les conséquences de ne pas travailler et le taux de chômage. Ces sujets mettent en lumière les problématiques du marché du travail en 2023.
## Tensions sur le marché de l'emploi 
- Les jeunes sont confrontés à la difficulté de trouver du travail.
- Certains jeunes ont peur de travailler, mais il ne faut pas les stigmatiser.
- Il y a une tension évidente sur le marché de l'emploi qui n'est pas facile à gérer.

## Témoignage d'un chef cuisinier expérimenté 
- Lionel, un chef cuisinier avec 35 ans d'expérience, partage son expérience.
- Il a travaillé en France et à l'étranger, dans des sociétés de catering renommées.
- Malgré son expérience, il a du mal à trouver un poste de chef cuisine en France.

## Dévalorisation des compétences acquises à l'étranger 
- Les personnes qui ont acquis des compétences à l'étranger sont souvent dénigrées en France.
- Les restaurateurs français ne valorisent pas ces compétences et ne comprennent pas qu'il y a des gens qui veulent grandir et optimiser leur travail.

## Les restaurateurs ne comprennent pas 
- Les restaurateurs français ne comprennent pas que la valeur d'un employé ne se limite pas à son salaire.
- Il y a des employés qui ont des idées et qui réfléchissent, et il faudrait les écouter davantage.
- Les restaurateurs devraient discuter et trouver des solutions avec leurs employés plutôt que de les ignorer.

## Témoignage d'un employé frustré 
- Lionel exprime sa frustration de ne pas être payé à sa juste valeur.
- Il se sent incompris et dévalorisé dans son métier.

## Difficultés à trouver des employés qualifiés 
- Les employeurs rencontrent des difficultés à trouver des employés qualifiés.
- Si les employés qualifiés quittent leur poste, il est difficile de les remplacer.
- Les employeurs doivent comprendre que certaines compétences sont rares et précieuses.

## Problème de l'offre et de la demande 
- Il existe un réel problème de correspondance entre l'offre et la demande sur le marché du travail.
- Il y a trop d'acteurs et il est difficile pour chacun de trouver le job dont il a besoin.
- Il est important de trouver un équilibre entre l'offre et la demande pour résoudre ce problème.

## Conclusion 
- Il est nécessaire de trouver des solutions pour résoudre les problèmes sur le marché du travail.
- Les employeurs doivent valoriser les compétences des employés et les écouter.
- Il faut également trouver un équilibre entre l'offre et la demande pour assurer une meilleure correspondance sur le marché de l'emploi.
## Problématique dans le secteur de la restauration 
- Le monde de la restauration a connu de nombreux changements, notamment au niveau des méthodes de travail et des salaires.
- Les prix des restaurants ont largement augmenté, non pas pour le bénéfice des restaurateurs, mais pour permettre de verser des salaires convenables aux employés.

## Témoignage d'un chef d'entreprise 
- Lionel, chef d'entreprise dans les Alpes-Maritimes, explique comment il a résolu son problème de personnel en travaillant seul.
- Il mentionne le cas de sa fille de 16 ans qui souhaite travailler dans la restauration, mais qui se heurte aux difficultés liées à l'emploi des mineurs.

## Importance du travail dès un jeune âge 
- Le témoignage de Lionel met en avant l'importance pour les jeunes de commencer à travailler tôt afin de se confronter au monde du travail et d'acquérir des compétences.
- Sophie et Didier soulignent également l'importance de commencer à travailler dès l'âge de 16 ans pour se réaliser et s'épanouir.

## L'impact des réglementations sur l'emploi 
- Sophie de Menton explique que la France a tendance à empêcher le travail et le recrutement, avec de nombreuses réglementations qui paralysent le monde de l'emploi.
- Cette situation affecte également les jeunes, qui se retrouvent limités dans leurs possibilités de travail dès l'âge de 16 ans.

## Valorisation du travail 
- Didier souligne l'importance de revaloriser la notion de travail et de l'expliquer comme une manière de s'épanouir et de s'accomplir, tout en soulignant l'existence d'entreprises qui offrent de belles opportunités aux salariés.

## Conclusion 
- Sophie et Didier concluent en mentionnant que 98% des entreprises en France sont des petites et moyennes entreprises, où les dirigeants discutent et travaillent quotidiennement avec leurs salariés.
- Ils reconnaissent que le sujet n'a pas été totalement exploré, mais soulignent son importance.
## Discussion sur l'âge légal pour travailler 
- Certains suggèrent de permettre aux jeunes de travailler à partir de 17 ans, puisqu'ils peuvent déjà obtenir leur permis de conduire à cet âge.
- Des incohérences sont soulignées concernant l'âge légal pour travailler, car il est actuellement fixé à 18 ans.
- Sophie de Menton, présidente du mouvement patronal de l'entreprise éthique, est présente dans la discussion.

## Introduction des invités 
- Didier Moindreau est présent en tant que président de la CPME 91 (Confédération des petites et moyennes entreprises) et vice-président de la CPAM France (Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie).
- Didier Moindreau est également président de la Commission nationale des entreprises en difficulté.

## Pause café 
- Une petite pause est annoncée, et il est mentionné qu'il est temps de prendre un café.
- L'animateur promet de faire rencontrer les spectateurs à une véritable source de café à la reprise de l'émission.

# ChatGPT Prompt Hack: Unlock the Secret to 10x Smarter Responses!



## Unlock the Power of Expertise



## Expertise in Prompts
Using expert knowledge in your ChatGPT prompt is a great way to help the model understand the context and give more specific answers. To do this, start by setting the context in the first sentence. For example, you can say "You are an expert career advisor" and then outline the field of expertise and years of experience. Afterwards, outline a specific task such as, "your task is to provide the best advice when it comes to changing careers". Finally, add the important instruction, "you must always ask questions before you answer". This ensures that the model can ask questions to help narrow down the user's request, providing better and more accurate answers.



## Communicate Feelings and Goals
Asking questions before answering can be a great way to get more information from the user. However, it's important to remember that it's also a chance to open up a conversation on the user's feelings and goals. This can help the model better understand a user's situation and provide further information on better ways to tackle the issue. For example, a prompt can include the instruction, "can you tell me a bit more about why you're considering ending the relationship?" to help gain insight into a user's feelings and then suggest possible solutions. 



## Listen and Give Advice
Once questions have been asked, it's important to listen to the response and give advice based on what the user has said. This could include suggesting possible alternative paths such as internships, apprenticeships and coding challenges. Overall, advice should be tailored to fit the user's individual situation, so it is important to consider their goals and interests before suggesting any paths forward. 




## Financial Planning for Saving Money
- Creating a budget and tracking expenses is an important step in saving money.
- Prioritizing spending and reducing expenses can be a way to save money.
- Increasing income can be helpful for saving money, for example by looking for a higher paying job or a side hustle.
- Automating savings can help you reach your long-term goals, such as working fewer hours in the future.
- Making your own food and doing DIY projects can reduce expenses.
- Starting a side hustle can be a great way to increase your income and reach your savings goals.




## Improving Health and Fitness 
- Engaging in regular physical activity for 150 minutes of moderate intensity aerobic activity, or 75 minutes of vigorous intensity aerobic activity, and two or more days of muscle strengthening activities can improve overall health and fitness.
- Improving your diet by focusing on nutrient dense Whole Foods and limiting your intake of added sugars and unsaturated fats can help to improve health.
- Losing weight, if needed, through a combination of healthy eating and regular physical activity can also lead to better overall health. 
- Managing your stress levels through techniques such as deep breathing, meditation, or yoga can help to improve overall health and well-being. 
- It's important to set realistic and achievable goals and be patient with progress, as lifestyle changes to improve health may take some time. 
- Following a consistent, well-rounded exercise plan in conjunction with a healthy diet can bring significant improvements in your overall health and well-being, including cardiovascular health. 
- It is important to consult with your doctor before starting any exercise or diet plan.

# Gérer son stress : l'expérience du Raid | Marc Verillotte | TEDxESSECBusinessSchool

## Marc Verillotte's experience with the Raid 
- Marc Verillotte is a former member of the elite police unit, the Raid
- He has been part of several high-risk missions, including the Charlie Hebdo shooting and the Hyper Cacher hostage situation
- He shares his experience dealing with stress and pressure in these situations
- Verillotte was also a former member of the French national judo team, with several international titles

## Two distinct zones of evolution 
- There are two zones of evolution: the comfort zone and the high-pressure zone
- The two zones have different rules and require different approaches to deal with them

## Characteristics of the comfort zone 
- In the comfort zone, an individual's mental, physical, and psychological abilities are stable
- The intensity of information is moderate, and difficulties are within the individual's competence
- An individual is relaxed and comfortable in this zone

## Characteristics of the high-pressure zone 
- In the high-pressure zone, an individual's mental, physical, and psychological abilities are negatively impacted
- An individual loses their composure and can't perform at their optimal level
- This happens because an individual's mental abilities are in a state of shock

## Procedures to deal with high-pressure situations 
- To deal with high-pressure situations, it's important to have a set of procedures in place
- These procedures are universal and can help individuals deal with their own challenges
- The procedures include:
  - Mental preparation through visualization and simulation
  - Physical preparation through training and maintaining physical fitness
  - Team preparation through communication and trust-building
  - Execution preparation through planning and preparation for contingencies
- By following these procedures, individuals can better handle high-pressure situations and improve their performance.
## Positive and negative reflexes 
- Physiological reactions occur in a high-pressure zone.
- Positive reflexes include intensified influx of nerve impulses to make us more physically reactive, sweating to anticipate future warming, and the sense leaving unnecessary organs for combat and flight to supply locomotor muscles.
- Negative reflexes cannot always be developed because they are innate.
- Reflexes cannot always be controlled, and they are not always updated based on current problems.
- In general, it is best to create automatic responses that are more reliable and can be trained. 

## Automatisms 
- Four types of automatic responses include physical and technical-tactical, thinking, emotional, and stress adaptation.
- Physical and technical-tactical responses are repetitive and practiced until they are as fluid and natural as bringing a spoon to the mouth.
- The same approach is used to develop professional gestures.
- Thinking automatism involves choosing a thought and repeating it to create a neural groove that prioritizes that thought over others.
- Emotional automatism prioritizes professional emotions and suppresses more frivolous, social emotions.
- Adaptation to stress involves developing an advanced reflex to move forward in high-pressure situations rather than shrinking back.

## How to develop your second pyramid 
- The first step is to create a green pyramid that provides an adequate amount of comfort.
- The second step is to create a red pyramid that is specific to your high-pressure zone and is made of the same components as the green pyramid but adjusted differently.
- It is essential to resist the modern-day comfort that softens you physically to maintain all of these assets.
- Pushing a car to exercise more, taking cold showers, and reducing intellectual activity are all ways to keep yourself dense and rustic. 

## Reflexes are innate 
- Reflexes have been honed over millions of years of evolution, and we have them in our skin.
- When faced with a significant challenge, it is essential to seek solutions not only from our minds but also from our guts.
- The first rule is to accept your stress and its reflexes since they are there to serve you.
## Benefits of working with our automatisms 
- Working with our automatisms can bring several advantages.
- Firstly, it saves time because it is quicker than an action linked to a thinking process.
- This is important in situations like Judo or Police intervention where a second can make a significant difference.

## Space saving 
- Automatisms allow us to save space in our thinking process.
- We can automate predictable actions, leaving more space for unpredictable situations.

## Stability 
- Automatisms can make us more stable, allowing us to avoid internal conflicts linked to thinking and emotions.
- We can act the same way in different situations, with more calmness and stability in our decision making.

## Conditions for Automatisms 
- However, automatisms require identical conditions between the moment they are constructed and when they are executed.
- This means that they have to be trained in the same conditions as the situation they will be used in.

## Mental skills 
- Mental skills are required to manage stress.
- Traditional thinking is not as effective in crisis situations as it is in a comfortable environment.
- The traditional thinking method takes too much space in our minds.
- During a crisis, we need a more synthetic thinking method that can help us focus on only the essential points.

## Adapting to crisis 
- During a crisis, we need to act quickly, which requires a different type of thinking than traditional thinking.
- We need to have a synthetic method that can help us focus on essential points to act quickly and efficiently.

## Zone of comfort 
- We cannot succeed by staying in our comfort zone.
- To adapt to stress, we need to expose ourselves gradually to different situations.
- This helps us to program ourselves to adapt to stress.

## Adaptation 
- Darwin's theory states that it is not the strongest or the most intelligent that survives, but the one that adapts best to change.
- On January 9, 2015, Marc Verillotte and his colleagues adapted to the high-pressure situation and saved 26 lives.
- To save lives, we need to train every day and use the same principles to perform under stress.

# Reprogram Your Mindset





## Working with a Metaphor
The metaphor of the horse and rider works a useful analogy for how we make decisions. The horse represents our instincts and deeper parts of ourselves, and the rider is the language center and is the part of ourselves which we have more control over. We can gain access to those parts of ourselves which are inaccessible and make more intentional choices.



## Integrating the Shadow
Psychologist Carl Young discussed the Shadow and how meeting it may feel. Our Shadow consists of the parts of ourselves we find aberrant and don't want to acknowledge. We can become conscious of our Shadow through considerable moral effort, which is an essential condition for any kind of self-knowledge. 

Discovering the power hunger in his Shadow allowed the writer to place if statements in order to make more intentional choices, understanding that he craved power for the purpose of setting things right when they go wrong, not for the same reason his father may have.



## Working with Different Parts
Richard Schwartz, the inventor of Integrated Family Systems, discussed the concept of being composed of multiple personalities and that we are all on a spectrum. Every part of us, including any we may consider bad, is valuable and should be accepted and given life. Doing inner work to understand and accept these parts is how trust can be regained in its leadership. 

Carl Young also theorized that these parts of ourselves had a consciousness and could behave mischievously, causing unexplainable events to occur, and that they were unteachable. 




## Mental Health and Self Discovery

- Mental health is something that can be improved over time with consistent effort. 
- It's important to be aware of the flaws that may exist in the way we think, feel, and act, so that we can fix them and ultimately be better to the people around us.
- Self-acceptance is essential to making lasting change. One way to do this is to talk to a therapist or coach, who can help you identify and work through issues that you may have shirked away from in the past. 
- It's helpful to think of the “Horse and Rider" model, where the "Rider" is the thinker or manager of the emotions and impulses. 
- People can also rely on "Firefighters" or extreme versions of the manager, which are often seen as problematic behaviors like addiction and dissociation. 
- Somatic approaches are effective for working with parts of the self that have been unconsciously pushed away for protection. 
- Words of wisdom from psychologists and philosophers, like Carl Jung and Alan Watts, remind us that true self-acceptance is a crucial part of leading a successful and meaningful life. 
- It's only with introspection and the right questions that you can make real changes, and unlock the power within you.

# Anatomy Of Story - John Truby [FULL INTERVIEW]

## Importance of Watching Movies and Reading Scripts 
- Both watching movies and reading scripts are important for a screenwriting career.
- John Truby has seen many movies and read countless scripts throughout his career.
- He believes that both activities are crucial for someone who wants to write screenplays professionally.

## Learning from Movies 
- Truby learned his craft as a writer by watching films.
- He developed his techniques and understanding of how to write a script that will make a great film.
- Truby went to classic cinemas and watched two high-level films per day for about three years.
- He took notes in the dark, looking for patterns and elements that were found in every great film.
- From this experience, Truby was able to develop the centerpiece of his teachings in "Story," which is the seven key steps of every great story.
- He also developed the more detailed 22 steps of every great story, which are applicable to any good script, regardless of length, medium, or genre.

## Importance of Reading Scripts 
- Reading scripts is important for writers to understand the pacing of a professional script.
- By reading a lot of scripts, writers can get a sense of how quickly a story needs to be established in the script.
- Writers need to consider that the reader, who is the person deciding whether to buy the script, has read many scripts before.
- The reader's normal response to a script is to say no, so writers need to break that pattern and capture the reader's attention within the first ten pages.
- Reading a lot of scripts gives the writer a sense of what needs to be accomplished in those first ten pages to keep the reader reading and have a chance of selling the script.

## Successful Storytelling 
- Truby mentions some good films that have come out in the summertime, such as "Hunger Games" and "Avengers."
- He explains that these films do extremely well because they incorporate certain story elements that appeal to a worldwide audience.
- To sell to a worldwide audience, Truby emphasizes the need for blockbuster films, which have specific story elements.
- Hollywood is not primarily concerned with the U.S. audience but with a worldwide audience.
- Truby states that Hollywood's basic marketing requirement is to sell to a worldwide audience.
- He mentions that Hollywood has not been a movie star-based system for at least a decade.
- The main factor that Hollywood buys and sells is genres.
- Genres are the most popular story forms in the world and have been for many years.
- These genres have already been worked out and have detailed knowledge of how their characters and plots work.
- In order to sell to a worldwide audience, writers need to use these different genres that the audience is already buying into.

## The Importance of Understanding Genres 
- Genre is the key to understanding screenwriting today.
- Hollywood buys and sells genres, not just movie stars, directors, or writers.
- Genres are the all-stars of the story world, with story forms that have been told for decades, centuries, and even thousands of years.
- Genres have been worked out in great detail, knowing exactly how their characters, themes, and plots work.
- To sell to a worldwide audience, writers need to use different genres because audiences know what they like even if they may not consciously recognize the specific genre.

## Examples of Blockbuster Films 
- Truby mentions films like "Avengers" and "Dark Knight" as examples of big summer blockbuster films.
- These films may not be recognized by audiences as specific genres, but they incorporate basic story forms with a unique skin placed on top.
- "Avengers" combines the myth-based story form with the concept of a dream team of all-stars.
- Disney acquired Marvel Comics to access the characters with worldwide appeal and use them in various films.
- "Hunger Games" is a good adaptation of a book that incorporates myth elements.
- The novelist skillfully brings together classic myth elements and modernizes them using a science fiction form.
- The combination of myth and science fiction makes "Hunger Games" a worldwide hit.

## Conclusion
- Watching movies and reading scripts are both important for aspiring screenwriters.
- Movies provide the opportunity to learn about storytelling techniques and patterns found in great films.
- Reading scripts helps writers understand the pacing required in professional scripts and how to capture the reader's attention in the first ten pages.
- Understanding genres is crucial in screenwriting as Hollywood primarily buys and sells genres rather than individual talents.
- Blockbuster films incorporate specific story elements that appeal to a worldwide audience, such as myth-based stories and concepts like dream teams or all-stars.
- The combination of genre and unique storytelling elements contributes to the success of films like "Avengers" and "Hunger Games."
## Importance of Understanding Genres in Storytelling 
- Combining genres is crucial in modern filmmaking.
- Most films today are not just a single genre, but a combination of two, three, or even four genres.
- Combining genres can be challenging because each genre has its own hero, opponent, desire line, theme, and more.
- When genres are combined without proper understanding, the result is often a disconnected and ineffective script.

## The Biggest Decision in Writing Process: Choosing the Genre 
- The first decision that writers have to make is determining the genre of their story.
- Many scripts fail because they use the wrong genre to develop their idea.
- Choosing the right genre is essential for a story to succeed.

## Different Parts of Hollywood: Mainstream vs Independent Filmmaking 
- Hollywood can be divided into two main parts: mainstream filmmaking and independent film.
- Mainstream filmmaking focuses on genre and combining genres to appeal to a worldwide audience.
- Independent film emphasizes originality, unique ideas, quirky characters, and often comedy.
- These two parts of Hollywood have different approaches to storytelling and story structures.

## The Importance of Television in Storytelling 
- Television has the best writing in the entertainment business.
- TV dramas coming out of Hollywood have reached a high level of excellence in recent years.
- The quality of craft writing in television is phenomenal.
- Writers are interested in learning how to write TV scripts that match the level of excellence seen in TV dramas.

## Transcending the Genre 
- It is important to approach a genre in a way that hasn't been done before.
- Hollywood marketing is based on selling genres, so having a genre-based story is crucial.
- However, if a writer follows the genre conventions too closely, their script will be like everyone else's and have no chance of standing out.
- To transcend the genre, writers need to twist the genre in a way that surprises the audience.
- This involves taking the basic story beats of the genre and doing them in a unique and unexpected way.

## Breaking the Screenwriting Rules 
- There is no popular film that breaks the fundamental key elements of screenwriting for telling a great story.
- The concept of "rules" in screenwriting can be misunderstood.
- Most people think of rules as simple conventions, but they are not the fundamental elements that make a script great.
- Breaking the rules in terms of conventions can lead to mechanical writing rather than storytelling excellence.
## The Key Elements of a Good Story 
- Paint-by-numbers script writing doesn't work for creating a good story.
- Good stories have key elements that are deep under the surface and link the story together.
- The story should build steadily from the beginning.
- The grammar of drama is the way a story can build, so it has the greatest impact on the audience.
- Great scripts always hit certain beats and follow certain rules.

## Transcending the Basic Rules 
- Advanced storytelling techniques can appear to break the basic rules, but they actually come up with more complex characters and story structures.
- These stories might have a main character who is unlikable, which goes against conventional wisdom.

## Creating Characters the Audience Cares About 
- One of the biggest mistakes writers make is how they create characters.
- Making a character as detailed as possible with many character traits is not the best way to make the audience care.
- The audience cares about a character based on their fundamental weakness and their goal in the story.
- The weakness is a personal problem that is hurting the hero and ruining their life.
- The entire story revolves around the solving of that problem through the pursuit of a particular goal.
- Plot comes from character, and creating a goal for the hero that forces them to deal with their deep weakness makes for a great story.

## Overcoming Weakness 
- The common notion used to be that action heroes should be upstanding moral paragons throughout the entire story.
- However, audiences are more interested in seeing a character overcome a deep weakness.
- The hero's goal is important, but what truly matters is whether the hero overcomes their weakness.
- Showing the great internal weakness of the character early on in the story is crucial.

## Dealing with Criticism 
- Fear of criticism can prevent brilliant people from putting their great work out there.
- Desensitizing ourselves to criticism is important.
- We need to strengthen our "criticism muscle" so that criticism doesn't hurt as much.
- Everyone faces criticism, especially as they climb higher in the public's view.



## Importance of Taking Criticism 
- John Truby emphasizes the importance of being able to take criticism as a writer.
- He states that the inability to accept criticism is a mark of an amateur writer.
- It can be difficult to hear criticism because writers put their heart and soul into their scripts, and negative feedback can feel personal.
- However, in order to improve, writers must be open to criticism and acknowledge that no script is perfect.

## Importance of Outside Criticism 
- Truby explains that in order to improve a script, it is crucial to listen to outside criticism.
- He acknowledges that everyone has weaknesses in their writing and that every script has weaknesses.
- The trick is to be open to criticism and use it as an opportunity to improve the script.

## The Importance of Who Gives Criticism 
- Truby emphasizes that it is important to consider who is giving the criticism.
- He states that most people are not capable of giving useful criticism to a writer.
- Family members, for example, may be afraid of giving negative feedback, and they may not have the necessary tools to provide constructive criticism.
- Even professionals in the industry, such as producers and agents, may not always be trained to give feedback that can truly improve the script.
- Therefore, it is crucial to seek criticism from people who know what they are talking about.

## The Importance of Structural Criticism 
- Truby explains that the only criticism that actually works for a writer is structural criticism.
- Structural criticism focuses on the bones of the story and identifies what is not working.
- Writers who receive constructive and structural criticism appreciate it because it is not personal; it is about the craft of storytelling.
- Structural criticism is what can make a script better.

## Writer Groups for Constructive Feedback 
- Truby recommends forming writer groups, preferably with the best writers one knows.
- Being part of a writer group allows writers to talk the same language and discuss the structure of their scripts.
- Writers who are serious about improving their craft understand the importance of deconstruction and reconstruction.
- Feedback from other writers in a group can make a significant difference in improving a script.

## Feedback from the Average Audience 
- Truby discusses the value of feedback from the average audience member.
- While they may not be able to provide feedback in structural terms, they can still express what is not working for them.
- Filmmakers and writers should be open to listening and translating the responses of the audience.
- Feedback from the audience, when taken into consideration, can be very helpful in improving a script or film.

## The Customer is Always Right 
- Truby emphasizes the importance of being open to all kinds of criticism.
- He explains that if a reader or viewer says something didn't work for them, the writer or filmmaker should take responsibility and not blame the audience.
- It is essential to be open to criticism and learn from it, as it can reveal things about the script or film that the writer or filmmaker may not have noticed.

## Listening to Audience Feedback 
- Truby explains that when an audience is giving feedback, it often relates to the pace of the story and specific scenes.
- Feedback may include comments about the story feeling slow or not liking certain characters or scenes.
- Ultimately, the audience is expressing that the sequencing of the scenes and the building of the story are not working for them.
- Filmmakers and writers should pay attention to these comments and consider how they can improve the story based on the feedback received.

## Importance of Good Feedback 
- Truby emphasizes that getting good feedback from an audience can be very helpful.
- It is important to be open and listen to what the audience is saying, even if they may not express it in structural terms.
- By being receptive to audience feedback, writers and filmmakers can learn a great deal about their script or film.
- The concept of "the customer is always right" applies here, as writers and filmmakers need to prioritize the audience's perspective and make necessary improvements based on their feedback.
## The importance of audience feedback 

- The speaker discusses the importance of audience feedback in shaping a story.
- Sometimes, writers may misjudge the audience's level of intuition or interest in the story, resulting in a lack of engagement.
- Filmmakers and writers are often too close to their work to objectively evaluate its effectiveness.
- Getting outside feedback is valuable because the audience has a kind of knowledge that can help improve the storytelling.

## TV drama as the best writing and filmmaking in Hollywood 

- The speaker argues that TV drama is currently the best form of writing and filmmaking in the entertainment industry.
- The best TV shows do not speak down to the audience; instead, they have a high regard for the audience's intelligence.
- The audience is smarter than we think and can handle complex storytelling forms.
- This goes against the old conventional wisdom that stories need to be easily understandable by everyone.

## The shift in audience perception through shows like Seinfeld 

- The show Seinfeld challenged the conventional wisdom of mainstream popular storytelling by featuring unlikable characters.
- This counterintuitive approach proved successful and influenced storytelling in both TV and film.
- Even superhero stories, which traditionally featured flawless characters, now incorporate severe character flaws to make them more relatable and popular.

## The misunderstood process of rewriting 

- Rewriting is one of the most misunderstood steps in the writing process.
- Writers often make a mistake by thinking they can fix any mistakes in the rewrite without realizing that the first draft solidifies certain elements.
- The first draft becomes concrete in the writer's mind, making it difficult to break apart and make necessary structural changes.
- Therefore, it is crucial to do a lot of prep work before writing the first draft, exploring the premise, creating characters, and planning the story's structure.

## The importance of the scene sequence 

- The scene sequence is a critical step in the writing process that many writers overlook.
- It allows writers to see the architecture of their story before writing the actual scenes.
- By analyzing the scene sequence, a consultant can identify about 90% of the problems in a script and propose solutions.
- The scene list helps spot any embedded structural problems and allows for fixes before writing the scenes.
## Importance of Craft Homework 

- Doing craft homework before writing the first draft is important.
- Writing the first draft with dialogue and undergrowth can hide the bones of the story.
- Craft homework allows the writer to see what is not working and how it can be fixed.
- Doing craft homework makes the rewriting process simpler and guarantees that the second draft is better than the first.

## Misunderstood Concept of Rewriting 

- Rewriting is a set of tools just like plot, character, and soul.
- Many writers mistakenly focus on fixing dialogue in the first draft.
- The focus should be on getting the story right during rewriting.
- The steps of finding the structural problems in a script start with the desire line of the story.
- A strong spine and a desire line that drives the story from beginning to end are essential.

## Difficulty of Screenwriting and Commitment 

- Screenwriting is the most difficult craft in the world.
- It requires a lifetime commitment to master.
- Many writers underestimate the level of commitment and complexity involved.
- The three-act structure approach is designed for beginners and does not work at the professional level.
- Writing a successful screenplay cannot be done with a few simple steps or a paint-by-numbers approach.
- To reach a level of excellence, writers need to master hundreds of craft techniques.

## Plot as the Underestimated Writing Skill 

- Plot is the most underestimated of all the major writing skills.
- Many writers understand the importance of a good main character and lean dialogue but overlook the importance of plot.
- Plot has more techniques that must be mastered to become a working professional.
- Without knowing these techniques, writers have no chance of working at the professional level.

## The Psychological Element of Writer Success 

- The psychological element is the biggest obstacle to writer success.
- Spending a lot of time alone and facing the challenge of writing every day can be difficult on the human mind.
- Many writers don't realize the psychological aspect and lack the tools and support system to handle it.
- Writers who work professionally are the ones who are still standing after facing rejection and the psychological difficulties.
- It takes years of commitment and mastery of the craft to reach the professional level.

## Openness to Learning the Craft 

- Stubbornness and a teflon personality are dependent on maintaining an openness to learning the craft.
- Professional writers who take John Truby's class often show no ego and have a willingness to learn.
- Maintaining an openness to learning is crucial in dealing with rejection and overcoming the challenges of being a writer.

## Importance of Continuous Learning 
- Professional writers are well-trained, but they should maintain a willingness to learn and grow.
- The most important quality for a successful writer is the openness to learning more.
- Constantly expanding your repertoire and set of tools will give you the confidence to withstand criticism and rejection.

## The Foundation of Confidence 
- Having a strong foundation in storytelling craft gives writers the confidence to weather tough psychological moments.
- It's similar to how attorneys and doctors need to pursue mandatory continuing education to stay competent in their fields.
- Many artists make the mistake of thinking they already know enough, which can be a huge problem.

## The Fallacy of Connections 
- Many writers believe that success in Hollywood is all about connections and who you know.
- However, 99% of writers lack the necessary story tools to make those connections pay off.
- Craft foundation is crucial for writers to make meaningful connections and succeed in the industry.

## Every Story is Unique 
- No matter how much you know about storytelling, cracking a story is always challenging because every story is different.
- While there are certain elements and techniques that can be used, each story presents its own set of difficulties.
- Even professional writers find it increasingly difficult as they set higher bars for themselves with each script.

## Avoiding Creativity Trap 
- A significant problem in the industry is writers feeling trapped in the lack of creativity.
- The constant pressure to write commercial scripts leads to trying to predict what will be commercially successful, which is impossible.
- Writers should challenge their own creativity and not succumb to writing generic, paint-by-numbers scripts.

## Taking Responsibility for Creativity 
- Creativity is the writer's responsibility, regardless of their level of success.
- Writers should strive to make every script personally meaningful and unique, while still appealing to a larger audience.
- It is a false belief that the industry forces writers to write in a particular way. Writers have the freedom to choose their approach.

## Staying Fresh and Challenging Yourself 
- It is essential for writers, especially successful ones, to constantly challenge their creativity.
- Writers should force themselves to hit the genre beats in a creative way that the audience has never seen before.
- There is no shortage of ideas, and writers should write stories they care about and believe will have a wider appeal.

## Overcoming Creativity Slump 
- If writers are feeling creatively stagnant, they can engage in physical activities or go on "writer's states" to rejuvenate their creativity.
- Julia Cameron, the author of "The Artist's Way," suggests engaging in activities that inspire and stimulate creativity.

## Overcoming Writer's Block 

- Writer's block is a common problem that writers face at some point.
- It is a misconception that writer's block is solely caused by a lack of creativity or being in the wrong mindset.
- According to John Truby, writer's block often stems from a lack of understanding the true structure of the story being told.
- Understanding the key story beats and ensuring they are unique and right for the story is crucial.
- The main character plays a significant role in driving the story and unlocking creativity.
- When facing writer's block, Truby advises going back to the main character and exploring what is unique about them.
- By focusing on the unfolding of that character over the course of the story, writers can reconnect with their creativity and overcome writer's block.

- He criticizes screenwriting gurus who claim to have a three-act structure or a formula that guarantees success, pointing out that many of these gurus don't even write screenplays themselves.

# Benefits and Limitations of Screenwriting Classes [01:13:45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8Q07y1JFeEE&t=4425s)

- Truby acknowledges that there are some benefits to taking screenwriting classes.
- However, he cautions against being misled into thinking that these classes are a be-all and end-all solution to becoming a successful screenwriter.
- He believes that everything in life requires self-applied effort, and screenwriting is no exception.
- Learning to write well is not easy, and it cannot be achieved solely through a class or a formula.

# The Problems with Traditional Screenwriting Teaching Methods [01:14:03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8Q07y1JFeEE&t=4443s)

- Truby criticizes the traditional teaching methods of screenwriting, particularly the emphasis on a three-act structure.
- He argues that the three-act structure is a false concept and does not work at a professional level.
- Truby believes that the teaching of writing concepts can often be ethereal and useless when faced with the blank page.
- He points out that not all writers have the same natural storytelling ability, and many successful writers have developed their craft through practice and the use of specific techniques.

# The Purpose of Truby's Classes [01:16:09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8Q07y1JFeEE&t=4569s)

- Truby explains that the purpose of his classes is to teach practical craft elements and techniques that he believes are useful to writers.
- His goal is to give writers the essential tools they need to write a great story.
- Truby emphasizes the importance of practicality and usefulness in his classes, focusing on techniques that can actually make a story better.
- He has received positive feedback from many students who have found his classes to be valuable and effective.

# The Changing Landscape for Screenwriters [01:19:12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8Q07y1JFeEE&t=4752s)

- Truby acknowledges that there have been some specific changes in the film industry that have made it more difficult for screenwriters to break into the business.
- Development money has essentially disappeared, making it harder for writers to sustain themselves and improve their craft through development work.
- Pitch festivals, which promise writers the opportunity to pitch their ideas to executives, are often misleading as they rarely result in deals due to the lack of development money.
- Truby argues that the fundamentals of breaking into the business as a screenwriter have always been challenging, but the current landscape has made it even more difficult.

Note: These notes are based on the provided captions and may not cover every detail in the video.
## Pitching Scripts and the Importance of the Page [01:21:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8Q07y1JFeEE&t=4879s)

- When pitching scripts, it can be challenging to get a deal if you are not one of the top 20 or so screenwriters.
- Producers may not be interested in your idea if they don't know if you can write a script or not.
- Unfortunately, these factors have become more negative over the years.
- One advantage writers have is that their work can speak for itself on the page.
- Writers don't have to pitch in person, and rejection is not personal.
- As long as the script is good and well-written, it doesn't matter where you're from or what you look like.
- It is crucial to prove yourself on the page and show that you have mastered the craft of writing.

## Reasons for Script Rejections [01:22:31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8Q07y1JFeEE&t=4951s)

- A script may be rejected not necessarily because of the quality of writing, but often because the producer didn't like the story idea or didn't find it commercially viable.
- Writers have no control over what producers want to sell.
- The only thing writers have control over is the quality of writing on the page.
- It is essential to focus on mastering the craft of writing to break through eventually.

## Pitchfests and the Door-Opening Opportunity [01:23:35](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8Q07y1JFeEE&t=5015s)

- Pitchfests can be a waste of money, and it's advisable to avoid them entirely.
- The only possible advantage of attending a pitchfest is that someone may agree to read your script after hearing your pitch.
- The purpose of a pitchfest is not to sell your idea but to get the opportunity for someone to read your script.
- Most people attending pitchfests don't have agents, so it's crucial to have a great script ready to show when someone expresses interest in your idea.
- The completed script is what matters the most in the industry.

## Fear of Idea Theft [01:24:45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8Q07y1JFeEE&t=5085s)

- The fear of someone stealing your idea is overrated.
- It is rare for ideas to be stolen because it takes a lot of work to develop an idea into a good script.
- Ideas that are similar or in the air can be developed by different people at different times.
- The emphasis on ideas and the belief that one can make a living selling story ideas is total nonsense.

Title: What is RabbitMQ?
Video URL: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7rkeORD4jSw
Categories: RABBITMQ
Transcript:
What is RabbitMQ, and what makes it one of the most popular message brokers out there? My name is Whitney Lee. I'm a Cloud Developer here at IBM. Before I dig in, please, don't forget to hit that subscribe button. So, let's travel back in time to the days of monolithic architecture. Back then, application components were tightly coupled. That means they were directly connected. So, in a simple retail application, if we had a checkout service and it needed to communicate with an inventory service, that would be done directly through, usually through a TCP connection. So, this had some limitations. As soon as the checkout sent the message, it would need to hear a reply before it could move on to the next task. Or worse, if the inventory service went down, it would try over and over again until it was able to make that connection. Or, if a lot of checkouts happened at once the inventory service wouldn't be able to keep up and the whole system would get bogged down. So, that's why message queues were created -- or, message brokers -- and those will sit, a message queue sits in between the two services that need to communication with one another. So, with a message queue, a checkout can add a message to the queue and then immediately move on to the next task. And then similarly, the inventory, when it's ready, can consume from the queue, process the message and then immediately consume the next message. So, this is going to decouple the two applications. A message broker is also going to help with scalability. So, the inventory...if a lot of checkouts happen at once, the queue begins to fill, you can have more than one consuming service -- more than one inventory, in our case -- to read from the queue to handle the amount of workload that the checkout is producing, and that's going to make the system more scalable. Another big benefit of message queues is that the queue itself can sit on its own machine. So, in that case, it can offload some of the work that's done by the Web application and make the whole system more performant. So, let's talk about RabbitMQ. RabbitMQ is an implementation of the AMQP message model -- that's Advanced Message Queueing Protocol -- and specifically, Version 091. So, with this type of message model, the producer, in our case the checkout, the service that produces the messages, instead of producing directly to a message queue, it's going to produce to an exchange. So, you can think of an exchange as a post office. It's going to receive all the messages and then distribute them according to how they're addressed. An exchange could be connected to many queues; in our case, we're going to do two. And then, the queues are connected to the consuming services or our consumers. So, we'll have one called inventory and then we'll do one called shipping might need to consume from a checkout. So, the checkout will send a message to the exchange. The exchange is connected to queues through connections called bindings, and these bindings can be referenced by the binding key. And then our consuming applications -- or, consumers, consuming services -- those subscribe to the queues. So, AMQP, RabbitMQ this is the message broker here, this part of the system. One thing that's great about this message model I the flexibility with which the messages can move through the system, and that flexibility is largely in part to the different types of exchanges available. So, the first type of exchange that the system can do is a fanout exchange. With a fanout exchange, checkout will produce to the exchange, the exchange will duplicate the message and send it to every single queue that it knows about. Or, we have a direct exchange. With the direct exchange, the checkout will produce the message and then that message will get a routing key. So, with a direct exchange the routing key is being compared to the binding key; and if it's an exact match, then the message will move through the system accordingly. Next, we have a topic exchange. With a topic exchange, we can do a partial match between the routing key and the binding key. So, if we had a routing key on this message called ship.shoes and the binding key was called ship.any and the exchange type was a topic exchange, that message would get routed through to that, this queue. There's also a header exchange. With a header exchange, the routing key is ignored completely, and the message is moved through the system according to the header. And then finally, we have a default exchange. This exchange is unique only to RabbitMQ. It's not part of the AMQP message model. So, the default exchange is also called a nameless exchange. And with the default exchange, the routing key, let's say the routing key of this message is inv. The routing key is getting tied to the name of the queue itself. So, if this queue is named inv, then the message would route through to there. So, there are a couple of main benefits of RabbitMQ right now with the architecture, and one is a tremendous amount of flexibility you have moving messages through your system. In fact, they say you can design your system with whatever you want, the sky's the limit, and then later configure it RabbitMQ to work with your system as opposed to needing to know RabbitMQ's limitations and designing your system accordingly. Also, with other message brokers the broker administrator when they set up the message model, that's when all the configuration for how message moves through the system, that's when it's all defined. But with RabbitMQ, the way the message moves through the system is largely a part of the message metadata. So, in this case, it's the application and the developer that has a lot of control with the way messages move through the system rather than the broker administrator. Another great benefit to RabbitMQ is that it is cloud friendly. It is easy to get started. You can deploy an instance of it on Docker or other containerization software. It also can run as a cluster, so that means it's fault tolerant, highly available and has high throughput. RabbitMQ can do cross language communication. So, if a message is produced by a checkout and go, it can be consumed by inventory in JavaScript and consumed by shipping in Python. And really the possibilities are endless. It has a very extensive library. It has good security. It supports FASL, LDAP and TLS for authentication and authorization. It does message acknowledgements. So, message acknowledgements, when a message is in a queue and it goes to the consumer, the message stays in the queue until the consumer lets the broker know that it has received the message. And only then is the message taken out of the queue, and that prevents the system from losing any messages. It has great management. So, right out of the box you have a really good browser based management UI as well as incentive CLI tools. Not only that, but the open source community has created plugins that really enrich the management and moderning part of RabbitMQ. And speaking of that open source community, it has created a lot of plugins that can enrich most aspects of RabbitMQ. There are many tools created, there are lots of clients, it's so evolved that RabbitMQ now supports other message models. So, not just AMQP 091 but you can do MQTT, Stomp, AMQP 1.0 for example. So, this has been an overview of RabbitMQ. The big takeaways for you are the flexibility with the ways the messages move through the system; the fact that the message metadata defines how messages move through the system as opposed to the broker administrator; and then, it's also super cloud friendly. Thank you. If you have questions, please drop us a line below. If you want to see more videos like this in the future, please like and subscribe. And don't forget, you can grow your skills and earn a badge with IBM Cloud Labs which are free, browser based, interactive Kubernetes labs.

# What is RabbitMQ?

## Message brokers and Monolithic Architecture 
- Monolithic Architecture refers to the time when application components were tightly coupled.
- In this architecture, application components were directly connected, usually through a TCP connection.
- Message brokers were created to help decouple application components.
- A message broker sits in between the two services that need to communicate with one another.
- With a message queue, checkout can add to the queue and then immediately move on to the next task.
- Similarly, the inventory, when it's ready, can consume from the queue, process the message and then immediately consume the next message.

## Types of Exchanges 
- A fanout exchange duplicates messages and sends it to every single queue that knows about.
- A direct exchange compares the routing key to the binding key.
- A topic exchange allows partial matching between the routing key and binding key.
- A header exchange ignores the routing key completely and moves the message through the system according to header.
- The default exchange is unique only to RabbitMQ and the routing key is tied to the name of the queue itself.

## RabbitMQ 
- RabbitMQ is an implementation of the AMQP message model.
- The AMQP message model stands for Advanced Message Queueing Protocol and specifically, version 0.9.1.
- With the AMQP message model, the producer produces an exchange instead of producing directly to a message queue.
- An exchange receives all the messages and then distributes them according to how they're addressed.
- RabbitMQ is cloud-friendly and easy to get started with.
- It can run as a cluster, so that means it's fault-tolerant, highly available and has high throughput.
- RabbitMQ can do cross-language communication, which means a message produced in one language can be consumed in another language.
- RabbitMQ has a very extensive library and good security.
- It supports FASL, LDAP, and TLS for authentication authorization.
- RabbitMQ does message acknowledgements, which means the message stays in the queue until the consumer lets the broker know that it has received the message.
- It has great management with a browser-based management UI and various CLI tools.
## RabbitMQ as a system 
- RabbitMQ is a message broker that allows different software systems to communicate with each other.
- It works by accepting and forwarding messages between different applications.
- It's a distributed system that can be installed on multiple nodes in a network.

## RabbitMQ and cloud computing 
- RabbitMQ is cloud-friendly and can work with different cloud platforms.
- It can be used in cloud-based systems for message queuing and communication between different applications.
- RabbitMQ can be deployed as a cloud service or installed in a cloud-based environment.

## Conclusion and call-to-action 
- The speaker thanks the audience for watching the video and reminds them to ask questions in the comments section.
- The speaker invites the audience to subscribe to the channel for more videos on RabbitMQ and related topics.
- The speaker introduces IBM Cloud Labs as a free, browser-based tool to learn and earn badges in Kubernetes labs.

# Introduction To Kubernetes | What Is Kubernetes? | Kubernetes Tutorial For Beginners | Simplilearn

## Life Before Kubernetes 
- The traditional way of deploying solutions was to push code to physical servers in a data center or to virtual machines.
- These methods have limitations in terms of consistency, resource allocation, and scalability.
- Virtual machines have become popular due to better resource utilization and scalability at a lower cost.
- However, virtual machines still have security risks, availability issues, and are time-consuming to manage.

## What is Kubernetes? 
- Kubernetes is a tool that allows for the management of containerized deployment of solutions.
- It is the next level of deployment for solutions after physical servers and virtual machines.
- Kubernetes is inherently secure and portable, working with docker container solutions.
- It allows for easy scaling on the demands of customers.

## Differences Between Kubernetes and Virtual Machines 
- Virtual machines have inherent security risks, while Kubernetes is inherently secure.
- Virtual machines are not easily portable, while Kubernetes is extremely portable due to the use of containerization.
- Kubernetes is much less time-consuming to use than virtual machines.
- Kubernetes uses more isolation when building out the encapsulated environment than virtual machines.

## Benefits of Kubernetes 
- Kubernetes allows for better resource utilization and scalability at a lower cost.
- It is extremely portable due to the use of containerization.
- Kubernetes is inherently secure and less time-consuming to manage.
- Kubernetes provides more isolation when building out the encapsulated environment than virtual machines.
- It allows for easy scaling on the demands of customers.
## What is Kubernetes? 

- Kubernetes is an open-source platform that allows managing and deploying groups of containers.
- Containers are similar to Docker and provide flexibility in scaling up solutions.
- Kubernetes manages multiple Docker environments together, making it a tool for managing large groups of containers.
- Kubernetes is designed for a cloud-first environment and is highly portable.

## History of Kubernetes 

- Kubernetes was originally a successor to a project at Google called Borg, which managed Google's network and infrastructure.
- Kubernetes was rewritten from the ground up and released as an open-source project in 2014.
- Kubernetes was released as an open-source project so that people outside of Google could take advantage of the power of Kubernetes containerization management tools.
- Today, Kubernetes is managed by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation, and there are many companies that support and manage Kubernetes.

## Benefits of Kubernetes 

- Kubernetes is highly portable and 100% open-source code, allowing contributions to the code project through Github.
- Kubernetes is highly scalable, and its history as part of a Google project for managing the Google network and infrastructure sets the groundwork for a highly scalable solution.
- Kubernetes is highly available, allowing for a highly efficient and energized environment that you can rely on.
- Kubernetes is designed for deployment, allowing for scripting out the environment and having it as part of your DevOps model.
- Kubernetes provides efficient load balancing, allowing you to distribute the load efficiently across your entire network.
- Kubernetes allows managing the orchestration of your storage, enabling you to have local storage or pull storage from a public cloud such as Azure or AWS.
- Kubernetes is designed for a cloud-first environment and is a self-healing environment, detecting failure and restarting, killing, or replacing the process as required.
- Kubernetes provides automated rollouts and rollbacks for managing the state of the environment.
- Kubernetes provides automatic bin packaging, allowing specifying the compute power being used from CPU and RAM for each container.

## Kubernetes Architecture 

- Kubernetes architecture is clustered-based, consisting of the Kubernetes master, which controls all of the activities within your entire Kubernetes infrastructure, and nodes that are running on Linux machines outs that are controlled by the master.
- The Kubernetes master allows for the configuration of information and the management of nodes within your cluster.
- The Kubernetes master is accessible via the API server, which is a restful based infrastructure that can secure each connection with SSL and other security models, ensuring that your entire infrastructure and the communication going back and forth across your infrastructure is tightly secured.
- The scheduler manages the schedule of activities within the actual cluster.
- The controller is a daemon server that manages and pushes out the instructions to all of your nodes.
- The nodes have three key areas: the Docker environment, which manages and maintains the container inside the node; kubelet, which is responsible for information that goes back and forth and does most of the conversation with the API server on the actual health of that node; and Kubernetes proxy, which runs the services inside of the node.
## Overview of Kubernetes 
- Kubernetes is an open-source container orchestration system that allows you to manage and automate the deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications.
- Kubernetes is efficient and highly available for your infrastructure and provides an easy way to manage your applications.

## Kubernetes Tools 
- There are different tools available for Kubernetes that can be divided into two key areas: Kubernetes master and Kubernetes node.
- The Kubernetes master has the instructions of what's going to happen within your Kubernetes infrastructure.
- Kubernetes will push out the instructions to an indefinite number of nodes that will allow you to scale up and scale down your solution in a dynamic way.

## Kubernetes Master and Node 
- The Kubernetes master is the control plane that manages the Kubernetes cluster. It includes several components such as the API server, etcd, controller manager, and scheduler.
- The Kubernetes node is the worker machine that runs the containerized applications. It includes the container runtime, kubelet, and kube-proxy.

## Kubernetes Infrastructure 
- Kubernetes infrastructure is a set of resources that includes the master node, worker nodes, and the containerized applications.
- The Kubernetes master manages the infrastructure and pushes out the instructions to the worker nodes.

## Benefits of Kubernetes 
- Kubernetes provides an overview of your infrastructure and allows you to manage and automate the deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications.
- Kubernetes architecture provides a dynamic way of scaling up and down your solution and provides high availability for your infrastructure.

## Conclusion 
- Kubernetes is a powerful tool for managing your containerized applications and provides an easy way to scale up and down your solution in a dynamic way. 
- If you want a deeper dive into the Kubernetes architecture, there is a link in the instructions below.

# Nihilism: The Philosophy of Johan Liebert

## Introduction and Existential Questions 
- The video opens with a musical introduction.
- It raises existential questions about life, such as our purpose and the meaning of existence.
- It highlights the uncertainty and lack of understanding about the future.

## Nihilism and Human Imposition 
- Nihilism is introduced as a belief in nothingness.
- It claims that life has no purpose or meaning.
- Humans are the ones who ascribe meaning to life's existence.

## Life and its Lack of Purpose 
- Life is depicted as transient and lacking purpose.
- The video emphasizes that life comes and goes without any inherent meaning.

## Nihilism's Rejection of Morals and Equality 
- Nihilism rejects the existence of morals and equality.
- It argues that these concepts are not objective truths.

## Human Insignificance in the Universe 
- Nihilism suggests that humans are insignificant compared to the vastness of the universe.
- It challenges the notion of humans being special or unique.

## Nihilism's Denial of Objective Truth 
- Nihilism denies the existence of objective truth, knowledge, morality, values, and meaning.
- It asserts that these concepts are subjective and vary from person to person.

## The Tale of the Nameless Monster 
- The video transitions to a tale about a nameless monster looking for a name.
- The monster splits into two and embarks on separate journeys.

## The Encounter with the Blacksmith 
- One of the monsters encounters a blacksmith in a village.
- The monster asks for the blacksmith's name but is denied.
- The blacksmith agrees to give his name if the monster can make him stronger.

## The Monster Becomes Otto the Blacksmith 
- The monster enters the blacksmith's body, named Otto.
- Otto becomes the strongest man in town.

## The Monster Consumes Otto 
- Otto realizes that the monster inside him is growing.
- The monster devours Otto from the inside out, reverting to being nameless.

- The monster tries to acquire names from a shoemaker and a hunter but ends up consuming them as well.

## Encounter with the Sick Boy 
- The monster arrives at a castle and encounters a sick boy.
- The boy offers his name in exchange for being made healthy and strong.

## The Monster Becomes Part of the Boy 
- The monster enters the boy's body, making him healthy and strong.
- The boy becomes a prince, but the monster suppresses its hunger to maintain the new life.

## The Boy Devours the King 
- The boy's hunger becomes uncontrollable, and he devours the king and all his servants.
- The castle becomes empty, and the boy embarks on a journey.

## The Encounter with the Monster from the West 
- The boy encounters the other monster who went west.
- The boy asks for a name, but the monster rejects the need for one, calling themselves nameless monsters.

## The Boy Consumes the Monster 
- The boy devours the monster who went west, acquiring a name.
- However, there is no one left to call him by that name.

# Design Masterclass with the best designer I’ve ever met (Raphael Schaad with Cron Calendar)





## Design and Paper Sketching
- Raphael Schaad emphasizes the importance of sketching before starting a software design process.
- He suggests sketching on paper as the first step because it is low commitment, allows him to explore ideas quickly, and creates an easy way to communicate with the team.
- Sketching helps to communicate ideas especially when done as group exercise, where each team member has a limited amount of time to sketch their ideas.
- Raphael uses distinctively black and white copic pens which help to emphasize the design’s form, function, and interactions.
- He stresses the importance of deferring judgement when sketching and encourages designers and non-designers alike to be visual and draw out ideas, even just stick figures.




## Design for Empathy
- Design should create empathy for the user and help create an expectation of what will happen when they interact further with the product.
- Designers need to be able to feel the user's experience and take into account user feedback to ensure that the design is suitable.
- The design process often involves exploring ideas in sketching and using design and prototyping tools, and then prototyping the product in the actual development medium (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, etc.).
- Steve Jobs famously drove engineers to replicate exactly how he wanted the design to "feel", creating a slider tool to give him control over design settings. This highlights the importance of the designer to be able to explore their ideas and simultaneously feel empathy for the user.




## Improving Interaction with UI Design
- To make a control stand out, designers can create contrast through color choices and visual hierarchy, as demonstrated by splitting out detail labels. 
- Typographic details also create visual distinction, such as replacing plus symbols with unicode minus symbols to make them all the same width. 
- Tabular figures are a type of font where all numbers are the same width, creating an 'excel like experience' for the user.




## Design Mastery with the Best Designer I’ve Ever Met
- Raphael Schaad with Cron Calendar took viewers through a masterclass to illustrate how to design a user interface in great detail. 
- He showed viewers how to create a visual hierarchy with sections, make it functional with a "recent" section, as well as, creating uniform lines giving the interface aesthetically pleasing design. 
- The class also covered the importance of user experience and functionality to work in unison. 
- Raphael discussed how he and the team at Cron Calendar are passionate about reimagining the calendar for the modern age. 
- Viewers had the opportunity to join the private beta for Cron Calendar by going to [Kron.com](Kron.com).
- By the end of the masterclass, viewers would of learned how to take their design craft to a higher level, understand the importance of every pixel, working with time zones, and making the most of ones time.
