# Kafka in 100 Seconds

## Apache Kafka
Apache Kafka is a distributed event streaming platform that can scale massive pipelines of real-time data. Developed in 2011 at LinkedIn, it is written in Java and Scala and was named after the German author Franz Kafka.

- It is used for building a dashboard like Google analytics, where when an event occurs (like a website visit), the producer API creates a new record that is stored to disk in an ordered, immutable log called a topic.
- Topics are distributed and replicated in clusters which contains multiple servers called Brokers, making Kafka fault tolerant and able to scale to any workload.
- Multiple consumers can subscribe to this data, being able to read the most recent message like a queue, read the entire topic log and listen to updates in real time.
- It provides a very powerful streams API that can transform and aggregate these topics before they ever reach the consumer.
- Kafka is more efficient than similar message brokers such as RabbitMQ and is ideal for streaming data applications. It is used today by companies like Lyft to collect and process geolocation data, Spotify and Netflix for log processing and Cloudflare for real-time analytics.



## Setting Up Apache Kafka
- Download Apache Kafka and use a tool like Zookeeper or K-Raft to manage the cluster.
- Start Zookeeper in one terminal and the Kafka server in another.
- Create your first topic - an event will have a key value, a timestamp, and optional metadata and headers.
- Use a command to publish an event to the topic, and this event is written to the log which is stored durably and partitioned in the cluster.
- Kafka guarantees that any consumer of a given topic will always read the events in the exact same order.
- Use a command to consume the topic, providing an offset to read a subset of records and from beginning flag to read the entire log.



## Kafka Streams API
- The Kafka Streams API is most well supported for Java.
- It allows for stateless transformation such as filtering out a subset of events.
- It also allows for stateful transformation such as an aggregation that combines multiple events into a single value over a window of time. 
- It enables you to manage real-time streams of data at virtually any scale.

- GPT-4 can evaluate its response to a task and create an even better one.

- GPT-4's success without reflection is linear compared to the success with reflection.

- Auto GPT can run its own code and execute Python scripts, allowing it to work independently.
- Auto GPT can evaluate its code for syntax errors and logic issues, then improve the code based on evaluation suggestions.
- Auto GPT adds tests for the functions in basic math.pi and executes the basic math.pi file to test the code.

- Auto GPT can perform tasks such as searching the internet and finding information.

And in case you're that person who has not yet made Jesus the foundation of your life, let Him know that's what you want Him to be and tell Him, Lord Jesus, I am just so awed by who You are, the God of this universe, willing to dwell within me and transform me and give me the power to change. You are the master of my life, the savior of my soul, the forgiver of my sin, the master of my destiny, and I will be in Your eternal presence forever, someday, because You paid for all my sin on the cross. But for today and for all of the days, You'll give me on earth, Lord Jesus, by your power, by your presence within me,  I will follow You all the days of my life, I will hear Your word, and I will put it into practice because You are my rock, my savior, and my Lord. # Walk On The Right Path | Ricky Sarthou | Run Through

## Importance of Foundation 

- Paul talks about the importance of having a solid foundation in our lives.
- Jesus should be the foundation of our lives.
- Jesus is the forgiver of our sins, the savior of our souls, and the master of our lives.
- We must be careful how we build on this foundation.

## Building on Jesus as the Foundation 

- We need to make sure that Jesus is the foundation of our lives.
- This is the first step in living an opposite life and making a difference in the world.
- We need to have a conviction that Jesus is the foundation of our lives.

## Proof of Foundation 

- Having Jesus as our foundation is not just about going to heaven.
- Faith in Jesus and obedience to His words go hand in hand.
- Obedience is the fruit or proof of our salvation.
- Jesus said that those who hear His words and act on them are like a wise man who built his house on the rock.
- The proof that Jesus is our foundation is seen in our daily obedience to Him.

## Practicing Obedience 

- When Jesus is our foundation, we practice obedience to His words.
- We need to obey Him in the calm seasons of life so that we continue to obey Him in the storms of life.
- Obedience should be a lifestyle of joyful obedience.
- The power of the Holy Spirit helps us change and obey Jesus in all circumstances.

## Building on the Right Foundation 

- Jesus warns that those who hear His words but do not act on them are like a foolish man who built his house on the sand.
- There is a lapse of time between building the house and the storm coming.
- Sometimes we realize that we have been building on the wrong foundation and need to make a change.
- If someone claims to be a follower of Jesus but lives in habitual disobedience and sin, they need to question their faith.

## Jesus as the Cornerstone 

- Jesus is not only the foundation but also the cornerstone of our lives.
- The cornerstone is the chief stone of an edifice and all other stones align with it.
- Our lives should be aligned with Jesus in our thoughts, emotions, and actions.
- Hearing and putting His word into practice is the proof that Jesus is our foundation.

## Building for Eternity 

- After establishing Jesus as our foundation, we need to build for eternity.
- This means living with an eternal perspective.
- We need to go back to 1 Corinthians to learn how to build for eternity.

# Walk On The Right Path | Ricky Sarthou | Run Through
Part 3 of 4
# Building Our Lives on Jesus 
- Paul talks about building our lives on the foundation of Jesus.
- There are two categories of materials we can use to build: gold, silver, and precious stones, and wood, hay, and straw.
- Gold, silver, and precious stones are of high value and do not burn up easily, while wood, hay, and straw are of low value and burn up quickly.
- Paul says that each person's work will be tested by fire on the day of judgment to determine its quality.
- This judgment is not about salvation but about how we lived our lives on earth.

# The Judgment Seat of Christ 
- Believers will stand before Jesus for judgment, where we will give an account of our lives.
- This judgment is based on how we lived our lives, not on the quantity of our works.
- The quality and motive of our hearts in serving Jesus is what matters.
- We will be recompensed for our deeds, whether good or bad, and receive rewards or suffer loss.
- This judgment is a time of evaluation, not for determining our salvation.

# Building with Gold, Silver, and Precious Stones 
- Gold, silver, and precious stones represent things with eternal value.
- Examples include studying God's word, daily obedience, sharing the gospel, making disciples, genuine worship, loving family, forgiving and reconciling, practicing the Spirit-filled life, serving with spiritual gifts, giving to God's work, staying morally pure, and doing all things for the glory of God.
- These are actions and attitudes that honor God and have a lasting impact.

# Building with Wood, Hay, and Straw 
- Wood, hay, and straw represent things of low value and temporary nature.
- Examples include materialism, making money our god, self-centeredness, giving in to lust and fleshly desires, hatred, bitterness, unforgiveness, causing division, exalting oneself, ignoring the convictions of the Holy Spirit, living to please others, and idolizing ourselves.
- These are actions and attitudes that do not honor God and have no lasting value.

# The Testing and Fire 
- The testing and fire mentioned by Paul are symbolic and represent the evaluation of our works.
- The exact nature of this testing is unknown, but God knows.
- Our job is to live our lives in a way that is contrary to the ways of the world.
- The outcome of this testing will determine whether our works remain and we receive a reward or our works are burned up and we suffer loss.

# God's Reward and Blessings 
- God is the author of the reward system and desires to bless His children.
- He wants us to live a life that we will not regret.
- The word "reward" reminds the speaker of his late wife and how she would surprise their grandchildren with gifts.
- Likewise, God wants to bless us and reward us for our faithfulness.
## Living the Opposite Life 
- Ricky Sarthou talks about the joy and brightness in the eyes of those who open their eyes to meet Jesus.
- He encourages the audience to live the opposite life and be prepared for the surprises that God has prepared for those who love Him.
- Ricky shares that following Jesus may cost everything, but not following Jesus also comes with a high price known as opportunity cost.
- He urges the audience not to waste their lives and to build with gold, silver, and precious stones for the glory of God.

## We Are the Temple of God 
- Ricky emphasizes that believers are the temple of God.
- He refers to 1 Corinthians 3:16-17, where the Apostle Paul reminds the Corinthians that they are the temple of God and the Spirit of God dwells in them.
- Ricky explains that although the Corinthians didn't have a physical building like Solomon's temple, they were the temple of God.
- He highlights the importance of knowing that believers are set apart for a purpose and a person, Jesus Christ.

## Personal Holiness and the Toothbrush Illustration 
- Ricky uses the illustration of a toothbrush to describe personal holiness.
- He explains that holiness means being set apart for a purpose and a person.
- Ricky asks the audience if they brushed their teeth that morning and relates it to the toothbrush being set apart for the purpose of brushing their own teeth.
- He connects this to believers being set apart for a purpose and for Jesus Christ.

## The Temple of Solomon 
- Ricky shows a visual representation of Solomon's temple and mentions its estimated cost in today's currency.
- He highlights that the most amazing aspect of the temple was not its appearance but what took place inside.
- Ricky refers to 2 Chronicles 7, where fire came down from heaven and the glory of the Lord filled the temple.
- He asks the audience to imagine if the same were to happen in their current worship setting, with everyone being overwhelmed by the presence of God.

# Conclusion
Ricky Sarthou continues to encourage the audience to live the opposite life and be prepared for the surprises that God has in store for those who love Him. He emphasizes that believers are the temple of God and should strive for personal holiness. Ricky also draws inspiration from Solomon's temple to illustrate the awe and reverence that comes with being in the presence of God.
## Living a Life that Shines with God's Glory 

- We have the privilege of being in God's temple every day.
- Our lives should reflect the glory of God.
- People should be able to see God in us.
- We are set apart for a purpose and a person.

## Proclaiming the Excellencies of God 

- We are chosen, holy, and set apart for God's own possession.
- Our purpose is to proclaim the excellencies of God to the world.
- We are called to talk about Him, shout out His praise, and live out His character.

## Called Out of Darkness into Light 

- We have been called out of darkness into God's marvelous light.
- We were once living independently, pursuing the emptiness of the world.
- But now, we are the people of God and have received His mercy.

## Bringing God's Presence Everywhere 

- When we go back to our homes, workplaces, and schools, people should sense the presence of the Lord.
- We bring His presence with us wherever we go.
- We should constantly ask ourselves how we can glorify God in every situation.

## Being a Fool for Christ 

- Apostle Paul says that if we think we are wise in the ways of the world, we must become foolish to become truly wise.
- The wisdom of this world is foolishness before God.
- We don't want to be called fools, especially by God on the last day of our lives.
- We need to live as fools for Jesus in opposition to the wisdom of the world.

## Unity in the Church 

- Paul addresses the issue of division within the church.
- He emphasizes the importance of unity among believers.
- Division goes against the principles of God.

## Conclusion 

- Ricky Sarthou concludes his message by encouraging the audience to walk on the right path, live with God's glory shining through them, and be fools for Christ.
- He urges them to embrace unity and avoid division in the church.
## Living for Eternity 
- Ricky Sarthou emphasizes the importance of living for eternity.
- He suggests that if someone is truly built on Jesus and living for eternity, they will realize that they are God's temple.
- Living for eternity means being willing to be a fool for Christ by living the opposite life.

## The Uselessness of Boasting in Men 
- Ricky Sarthou criticizes the division among believers who boast in different leaders like Cephas or Apollo.
- He states that this kind of division is totally useless.
- According to him, when someone has Jesus, they have everything and there is no need to boast in men.

## All Things Belong to You 
- Ricky Sarthou quotes from the Bible, emphasizing that all things belong to believers.
- Whether it is Paul, Apollos, Cephas, the world, life, death, or things present or to come, all things belong to believers.
- Ultimately, believers belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God.

## Having Jesus Means Having Everything 
- Ricky Sarthou summarizes the previous points by stating that when someone has Jesus, they have everything.
- He questions what else believers are pursuing when they already have Jesus.

## Living the Opposite Life 
- Ricky Sarthou introduces the main theme of the message, which is living the opposite life.
- He challenges the audience to be the opposite light in this dark world.
- He invites those who have not made a commitment to Jesus to do so, and assures them that they will be prayed for.

## Making Jesus the Foundation of Life 
- Ricky Sarthou addresses those who have not made Jesus the foundation of their life.
- He invites them to make the first step of accepting Jesus and making Him the foundation.
- He offers to pray for and with those who want to make this commitment.

## Repenting and Living for God 
- Ricky Sarthou leads a prayer of repentance for those who have been living in-sync with the world instead of being opposite to it.
- He encourages believers to repent of their selfish ways and ask God for forgiveness.
- He prays for believers to be filled with the Holy Spirit and to live for God, representing Him as His temple.

## Making a Decision for Jesus 
- Ricky Sarthou addresses those who have not yet made Jesus the foundation of their life.
- He encourages them to tell Jesus that they want Him to be the foundation of their life.
- He leads a prayer where the person gives their life to Jesus and acknowledges Him as the master, savior, forgiver of sin, and master of destiny.

## Following Jesus 
- Ricky Sarthou encourages believers to follow Jesus all the days of their life.
- He emphasizes the importance of hearing God's word and putting it into practice.
- He assures believers that they can do this through the power and presence of Jesus within them.

## Closing Prayer 
- Ricky Sarthou thanks God for His presence during the message.
- He acknowledges that even though they may not have seen a bright cloud of glory, they know that God is present.
- He prays in the name of Jesus and asks for blessings for everyone.

# End of Part 2

# Elon wants GPT-5 stopped NOW… 5 reasons AI kinda sucks

## AI and the Future of Work 

- OpenAI has released a paper that lists all the occupations that will be affected by large language models.
- The report concluded that up to 49% of workers could have at least half of their job functions enhanced by AI.
- This is why over 1,000 people just signed a petition asking all AI labs to immediately pause training for AI systems more powerful than GPT-4 until we can be confident that it's not going to kill everybody.
- Prominent people like Steve Wozniak, Victoria Krakovna, and Elon Musk have signed the petition.
- However, most degrees, including history, math, gender studies, and business, will be affected just as much.

## AI and Computer Science Degrees 

- AI is forcing many people to question whether or not they should get a degree in computer science because what's the point if AI can write and debug its own code or build an app based on a design on a napkin.
- Almost every other degree is also likely to be affected in the future.
- However, computer science provides a solid foundation for problem-solving and critical thinking, which are the skills that will not be impacted by GPTs.
- Computer science graduates will be the ones most well-positioned to snatch up new cutting-edge jobs that will emerge.

## GPT's Limitations 

- GPT-4 is not as great of a program when it comes to things like LeeCo questions that have already been solved.
- Large language models mostly just regurgitate information from the internet in clever ways. If information has never been "gurgitated" before, it'll struggle.
- AI executing its own code can be done with the new Chat GPT plugin. If requirements for a problem are well-defined, it won't just generate one solution that might be correct; it can generate tens of thousands of solutions and test all of them to figure out which one is optimal.
- It's possible that technology like this will make writing source code by hand obsolete.

## The Hype Behind AI 

- A lot of AI is just marketing hype.
- Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, knows how to accelerate growth using all kinds of Jedi mind tricks.
- AI regulation is needed ASAP before artificial general intelligence emerges and completely takes over.
- Altman has also attended Bilderberg, which conspiracy theories speculate is a meeting where powerful people conspire to create a One World Government.
- This is all just optics for marketing, and the hype is hugely beneficial to OpenAI.

## AI and the Internet 

- AI is making the internet boring.
- It's almost impossible to know if a social media account or image is human-crafted or not.
- The internet of 2023 is entirely different and awesome in its way, but sometimes it's hard to determine if anybody out there is real.
- The dead internet theory suggests that these big tech companies have used AI to inhabit the internet with a bunch of fake accounts that provide engagement to boost advertising revenue, while also motivating creators to continue on the hamster wheel.
## Background on GPT and Deep Learning 
- GPT refers to Generative Pre-trained Transformer, an AI language model developed by OpenAI.
- Deep learning is a subset of machine learning that involves training artificial neural networks to learn from data.
- The transformer in deep learning was first introduced by Google in 2017.
- OpenAI was the first company to build a product based on this idea.

## Building an AI language model 
- It is possible to build your own GPT using Python in a day.
- However, building a high-quality language model takes a massive amount of computing power and time.

## Limitations of AI 
- There is something special about being human that we cannot replicate on a silicon chip.
- Science has never been able to fully explain concepts like consciousness and the soul.
- It is highly likely that we are missing some kind of "secret sauce" required to create AGI (Artificial General Intelligence).
- AI will be extremely good at mimicking humans but will never surpass human intellect.

## AGI and the future 
- There may come a day where AGI emerges and we must worship it, implement a one-world government, and eat bugs.
- However, this video is just a joke, and the speaker is excited to be working together with AI in the future.

## Conclusion 
- This has been the Code Report, and thank you for watching.

# The biggest predictor of divorce | Shannon Curry and Lex Fridman

## Contempt - the biggest predictor of a split 
- Contempt is criticism on steroids and the biggest predictor of a split in a relationship.
- It is when you look down on your partner and make them feel pathetic and ridiculous.
- Contempt can be abusive and takes the legs out from your partner.
- People engage in contempt at some point in their relationship.
- Eye-rolling is a lower level of contempt but it's the biggest predictor of a split.
- If you allow yourself to think of contempt, it's like a weird slippery slope.

## Importance of wearing rose-colored glasses in a relationship 
- Wearing rose-colored glasses is important and healthy in a relationship.
- It's a choice you make in seeing the beauty in your partner.
- Getting married is choosing one person's faults over another.
- As human beings, love is an emotion and attraction is an emotion.
- Even if you're in a committed relationship, you might see the beauty in another person who seems novel.
- If you can remember that they too have problems that you would be marrying, it helps you see the beauty in your partner again.

## Differences in a relationship 
- Fundamentally, all humans have flaws or unique flaws.
- Relationships are just the way to figure out how two people can fit together.
- We all have differences because we are raised differently, have different stories, and experiences that shaped our value systems.
- We are going to have differences, so it's important to determine if these are dealbreaker differences or if their benefits and strengths make it worth it.

# NEW RAG Framework: Canopy

## Introduction to Canopy 

- Canopy is a new framework developed by the Geni team at Pine Cone.
- The framework aims to help build better RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) pipelines.
- Canopy simplifies the process of building RAG pipelines and offers additional features.
- One notable feature is the ability to compare RAG output with non-RAG output in the terminal.
- Canopy is designed to be easy to use and is wrapped up in a user-friendly framework.

## Overview of Canopy 

- The video introduces the Canopy framework and provides a visual representation of its components.
- The focus of the video will be on the Canopy CLI (Command Line Interface) for getting started.

## Setting up Canopy 

- To set up Canopy, it is recommended to create a virtual environment.
- The package can be installed using the command `pip install --upgrade canopy`.
- After installation, running the command `canopy` will initially result in an error message.
- This error is due to missing environment variables that need to be set.

## Setting Environment Variables 

- To resolve the error, the video demonstrates setting up the required environment variables.
- The required environment variables are the Pine Cone API key, Pine environment, and the Open AI API key.
- The video shows how to set these environment variables using the `export` command and the specific variable names.
- The Pine Cone API key and environment can be obtained from the Pine Cone app, while the Open AI API key can be obtained from the Open AI platform.

## Running Canopy 

- Once the environment variables are set, running the `canopy` command again should result in a proper response.
- The video demonstrates creating a new index using the command `canopy new` followed by the desired index name.
- Adding data to the index is shown using the command `canopy upsert` and specifying the file or directory containing the data.

## Creating Data for Canopy 

- The video briefly mentions creating data in the correct format for Canopy.
- It refers to a notebook that demonstrates how to create data in the required format.
- The notebook uses a dataset scraped from the AI archive and showcases the necessary columns and metadata.
- The data is converted into a JSON lines file format for use with Canopy.

## Conclusion 

- The video concludes by summarizing the steps covered, including setting up Canopy, creating an index, and adding data.
- It encourages viewers to follow along with the notebook provided to gain a better understanding of creating data for Canopy.
## Setting up the Index 

- Canopy allows you to set up an index using the command line interface (CLI).
- You can also set the index name within the command, but in this video, the index name will be set via the "Via" command.
- A quick check is done to confirm that everything is correct.

## Starting Canopy 

- Canopy is started by using the command "canopy start" in the CLI.
- This command starts up the API or Canopy server.
- Once the server is running, you can access the documentation by going to "localhost:8000" in your browser.

## Using the CLI 

- The CLI allows you to interact with Canopy using commands in the command line.
- To use the CLI, the Canopy server needs to be running in the background.
- The command "canopy chat" is used to run the CLI and interact with the language model (LM).
- By running "canopy chat" without any arguments, you can chat with the LM and get responses.
- Running "canopy chat --no-rag" will show a comparison of the LM response with and without the RAG framework.

## Testing with Context 

- The RAG framework allows for context-aware responses from the LM.
- The conversation starts with a general query that doesn't require context.
- The LM responds similarly with and without RAG for this type of query.
- The data set used behind Canopy contains information about "Lama 2," a large language model.
- Asking about "Lama 2" with context results in the LM providing specific details about it.
- Without context, the LM is not aware of "Lama 2" as it was trained on data only up until September 2012.

## Asking More Specific Questions 

- Asking about when to use "Lama" allows the LM to provide information about its use cases and optimizations.
- The RAG framework helps provide a more tailored response based on the context given.
- Without context, the LM provides a generic response that it is not aware of any specific entity called "LL 2."

## Comparing Llama 2 and Distill Bird 

- Asking about the comparison between "Lama 2" and "Distill Bird" is a more complex question.
- The RAG framework splits the query into multiple searches to provide results from different papers.
- With context, the LM provides a detailed comparison of the two models.
- Without context, the LM is not aware of "Lama 2" but can provide information about "Distill Bird" as a specific model architecture used in various NLP tasks.

## Introduction to Canopy 

- Canopy is a framework that enhances the language model's responses by incorporating context.
- It provides a CLI for interacting with the LM and a server for running the Canopy API.
- The Canopy server can be used to access the documentation and explore the available endpoints.
- The CLI allows for chat-like interactions with the LM, and the "--no-rag" option shows a comparison of LM responses with and without RAG.

## Conclusion 

- Canopy is a powerful framework for improving LM responses by considering context.
- It offers a CLI and a server for interacting with the LM.
- The video concludes by thanking the audience for watching and mentioning that the next video will be coming soon.

## How to use ChatGPT for Tax Documentation

In this video, Harry Jmg demonstrates how to utilize the chatbot ChatGPT for streamlining the process of collecting and managing tax documentation.

- He begins by explaining the challenges associated with collecting multiple invoices for his tax audit. 
- He then describes how the Rebrandly application streamlines URLs to make them easier to remember.
- He goes on to explain that he needs to use a program to automatically extract HTML pages into PDF documents so he can send them to his bank easily.
- He then describes his plan of action which includes two steps. The first step will be to use code to extract all the links to his bills as HTML pages.
- He then goes on to explain that he will then use ChatGPT to help create a script which will go through each of these links and extract the bills in PDF form. 
- He then shows how to copy the code from the HTML page and paste it into the ChatGPT console.
- He explains that he must simplify his question to make it fit the character limit, and that he is using ChatGPT in order to avoid writing too much code. 
- He then demonstrates how a simple question can be used to generate the desired script which will ultimately provide the data he needs.




## Use of ChatGPT
ChatGPT is a powerful tool that can be used to automate certain tedious tasks, such as tax filing in this case. It is capable of writing code based on a specific question.

- Harry Jmg demonstrates how he uses ChatGPT to create a code that can generate a list of 33 links by asking a specific question. 
- He then copies the provided response and uses it to access the list of links. 
- He modifies the provided code to create a Ruby script, which takes the list of links and extracts HTML pages in PDF format.
- He then tests the script to debug and fix any issues before using it to finish the task.



## How to use ChatGPT for tax auditing
- With ChatGPT, the uploading of invoices can be automated to facilitate the tax audit and save time.
- To do this, a small terminal can be opened and a Ruby script can be run.
- If the codes are correct, the invoices can be uploaded without any problems.
- If the error is displayed, a script to resolve the error must be installed. On a Mac, this can be done by writing `defol script wave from error resolved hoop`.
- A hoop is always necessary ;-)
- A final script must be run to generate the logs and ensure that the invoices have been downloaded.
- For best results, it is important to understand the code and have some basic development knowledge.


## Using ChatGPT for Tax Preparations 
- ChatGPT can be used by software developers to automate certain tasks, such as tax preparaion. 
- This video shows how Harry Jmg uses ChatGPT to decrease the amount of time spent manually updating records and files. 
- As a software developer, he is able to move quickly from one task to another without having to manually click, print, drag and drop files on each website. 
- He highlighted the extra effort that would go into the task for someone who is not skilled in programming. 
- He proposed Cody Accelerator as a solution for people who would like to gain coding skills and use ChatGPT to their advantage.


## Conclusion
- `Harry Jmg` concludes the video by emphasizing the simplicty of using `ChatGPT` to perform one's taxes. 
- He states that there's plenty to explore with ChatGPT and he looks forward to seeing the viewer as part of the team.

# Web Scraping with ChatGPT Code Interpreter is Mind-Blowing!

## Introduction to web scraping with ChatGPT Code Interpreter 
- The video will demonstrate how to perform web scraping using the ChatGPT Code Interpreter.
- The method shown is straightforward and does not require any plugins or additional tools.

## Saving the website as an HTML file 
- To begin, navigate to the website you want to scrape. In this example, the website is Amazon.
- Use the search function on the website to find the desired information, such as TVs.
- Press "Ctrl + S" (or "Command + S" on Mac) to save the webpage as an HTML file.
- Choose a name for the file, e.g., "amazon.com_TVs.html", and save it to your computer.

## Uploading the HTML file to ChatGPT Code Interpreter 
- Go to the ChatGPT Code Interpreter website.
- Select the "Code Interpreter" option.
- Upload the HTML file that was saved earlier by clicking the upload button.
- Choose the HTML file, and it will be displayed in the code interpreter.

## Providing instructions for data extraction 
- In the code prompt, specify the desired data extraction instructions.
- In this example, the prompt asks ChatGPT to extract the name and price of the product, put the data into a table, and export it to a CSV file.
- The prompt also includes information about handling missing data, ensuring that it is not duplicated from other products.

## Extracting data and generating a CSV file 
- After sending the instructions, ChatGPT starts extracting the product names and prices from the HTML file.
- It creates a table with two columns: product name and price.
- Finally, ChatGPT generates a CSV file containing all the extracted data.
- The CSV file can be downloaded and opened to view the scraped data.

## Verifying the extracted data 
- The extracted data is displayed in the CSV file.
- Each row represents a different product, and the corresponding name and price are correctly extracted.
- If any data is incorrect, additional prompting can be done to guide ChatGPT in getting the right data.

## Scraping data from multiple pages 
- To scrape data from multiple pages, repeat the process for each page.
- Save each page as a separate HTML file.
- Upload the HTML file for each page to the Code Interpreter.
- Provide instructions for each page, specifying that it is a different part of the website.
- ChatGPT will extract the data from each page and combine it into a single CSV file.

## Conclusion 
- Web scraping with the ChatGPT Code Interpreter provides a powerful and efficient way to extract data from websites.
- The process involves saving the website as an HTML file, uploading it to the Code Interpreter, providing instructions for data extraction, and generating a CSV file.
- The extracted data can be verified and, if necessary, further prompting can be used to ensure accuracy.
- Multiple pages can be scraped by repeating the process for each page and combining the extracted data into a single CSV file.
## Scraping Data from Amazon 
- The presenter demonstrates how to scrape data from Amazon using a code interpreter.
- They show an example of scraping product data from Amazon's website.
- The product they scrape is a 55-inch D series full HD TV, priced at $168.
- They successfully scrape not only the first page but also the second page of the search results.
- They mention that you can continue this process to scrape as many pages as you want from Amazon.

## Scraping Data from Glassdoor 
- The presenter now demonstrates how to scrape data from the Glassdoor website.
- They want to extract job data for data scientists.
- They show a slightly different approach compared to the Amazon example.
- They save the Glassdoor job search page as an HTML file.
- They upload the HTML file to the code interpreter.

## Extracting Data from Glassdoor 
- The presenter explains the process of extracting specific elements from the HTML file.
- They use IDs as identifiers to extract the desired data.
- The elements they want to extract include the company name, job title, location, and job salary.
- They demonstrate how to identify the IDs of these elements using the right-click inspect feature on the webpage.
- They mention that if the ID approach doesn't work, you can try using other attributes like data-test or class.

## Matching IDs with Regular Expressions 
- The presenter encounters an issue where the code interpreter doesn't find elements with the specified IDs.
- They explain that it's because they deleted part of the IDs and only left specific words.
- To solve this, they introduce the use of regular expressions with brackets to match the missing parts of the IDs.
- By using this approach, the code interpreter will be able to extract the data even if the full ID name is not matched.

## Exporting Data to CSV 
- The presenter mentions that they want to put the extracted data into a table and export it to a CSV file.
- They explain that there might be missing data, such as companies not providing a job salary.
- In case of missing data, they instruct the code interpreter to treat it as "new data" instead of duplicating existing data.
- They press enter to execute the code and the code interpreter successfully extracts and exports the data.

## Verifying Extracted Data 
- The presenter downloads the CSV file and opens it to verify the extracted data.
- They compare the data in the CSV file with the Glassdoor website to ensure accuracy.
- They show examples of extracted data, such as a job at UCLA Health for a data scientist in LA with a salary of $26.20 per hour.
- They confirm that all the data has been successfully extracted and exported.
- They mention that if there were any duplicated rows, it could be handled by instructing the code interpreter accordingly.

## Conclusion 
- The presenter asks the viewers if they found this approach to web scraping using the code interpreter easy.
- They encourage viewers to leave comments about their experiences with web scraping using the code interpreter.
- The presenter concludes the video and mentions that they will see the viewers in the next video.

# How to Stand Out (without getting shot down)



## Finding the Right Path
- When pursuing something new, break free from traditional conventions and try something unique.
- Ricky Rubin, a producer of early hip-hop, wanted to create music that replicated the vibrancy of the clubs, pulled away from the conventions of traditional R&B.
- Aikido martial-arts master Endo Sheshiro Shihan emphasizes the importance of the Shu Ha Re cycle: Shu (following the given conventions), Ha (breaking with the conventions and experimenting), Re (creating something completely new without overstepping laws).
- Creative rebellion is essential in being able to make something unique, however it is important that this rebellion is backed by thorough research and study of the Forebears.
- True creativity and innovation comes from understanding what has been done before, but also the willingness to be different.
 


## The Rules of Mastery
- Mastery is not a function of genius or talent, but of time and intense focus given to a particular field of knowledge.
- Learning is a constant process of discovery that never ends.
- Iteration is the key to improving mastery, where the journey is as important as the destination.
- Don't purely try to be different for different's sake, but take what exists and build upon it.

# The founder mindset you need - (Bill Gates’s lesson on time frame)



## Short-Term Pessimism, Long-Term Optimism
- Bill Gates learned that true founders need to adopt this approach to succeed in business.
- This might feel counter-intuitive but is key to avoiding self-fulfilling prophecy.
- Overactive super egos can be used to channel anxiety productively if translated into taking preventive action.
- Andy Grove's book, "Only the Paranoid Survive" is quoted in this video as an example of the value of paranoia in areas like product quality and competition.
- The Stockdale Paradox refers to finding the balance between having faith in eventual success with the discipline to confront the facts of current reality - a link to the video about this is found in the description of this video.
- The London School of Economics did a study in 2019 that showed founders with above-average optimism earned less than their pessimistic counterparts when they started their own businesses.
- Charlie Munger's famous quote: "All I want to know is where I'm going to die, so I'll never go there" reaffirms the need for short-term pessimism.
- Product feedback is key to testing the viability of a business idea and preventing failure.
- It is important to pay attention to criticisms and incorporate them into strategy and design.




## Short Term Pessimism and Long Term Optimism
- Success in any venture requires being a long term optimist and being prepared to be in it for the long haul. 
- 80% of new businesses fail in the first 5 years and another 80% fail after 10 years.
- Most people underestimate just how much can be achieved in 10 years. 
- The founders journey is often characterized by an initial launch, followed by a long trough of sorrow, and eventually leading to success. 
- To stay committed for the long haul and make impossible things possible, one must resist their natural inclinations and apply conscious attention and focus.

# How to Build An MVP | Startup School

## Introduction and MVP 
- The speaker talks about how to build an MVP (Minimum Viable Product).
- MVP is a meme that is popular among founders.
- The speaker talks about the midwit meme - the super intelligent founder, and the first-time founder who has no idea what's going on.
- The best advice is to launch something quickly and iterate.

## Importance of an MVP 
- The best way to start a conversation with the user is to get a product into the hands of your customers.
- You only really start learning about your user when you put a product in front of them.
- The wrong answer is to do 100 surveys and 600 user interviews. It is better to launch something quickly and iterate.

## Building an MVP 
- The goal you should have as an early stage founder is to get a product out into the world quickly.
- You should be talking to some initial customers and trying to figure out what you can do to make that product useful for them.
- You should care about how to help them accomplish their goals and try to figure out how to change and iterate your product so that it actually helps them.

## Importance of iteration 
- Talk to more users, iterate your product.
- More often than not, after three, four, five, six iterations, your MVP is going to be very different.
- You have learned so much by having that conversation with users and by letting them see your product evolve.

## Fear of an MVP 
- Fear is the biggest that founders have.
- It's a non-specific fear of, "Oh my God, if I give people my product and they don't like it, boom, my company dies."
- Fear is not bad, but it is bad to act on it.
- You don't have to worry about losing people who are interested in talking to a startup. They are early adopters and are used to using products that don't work very well.

## Fake Steve Jobs 
- There are some people who think they know what the perfect product is and that it's going to take a year to build.
- The speaker calls these people fake Steve Jobs.
- It is a misconception of what great product people do.
- Most of the time, when people think about products that Steve Jobs is most known for, they don't take enough time to look at all of the different iterations those products went through over time.
## Importance of Iteration and MVP 

- Iteration is essential for building a successful product.
- Even Steve Jobs iterated his products to make them better.
- Building an MVP (Minimum Viable Product) is a great way to get started.

## Characteristics of Successful MVPs 

- Successful MVPs are fast to build and can get to the market quickly.
- They have limited functionality.
- They appeal to a small set of users.

## Examples of Successful MVPs



## Airbnb 

- The first version of Airbnb had no payment system, no map view, and only worked for conferences.
- Users could only rent an air bed, not a room or an entire house.
- Despite these limitations, the MVP was successful because it solved a specific pain point for a small set of users.



## Twitch 

- Twitch started as a site named Justin TV where the co-founder Justin had a camera on his head that broadcasted 24/7.
- The first version of Twitch had only one page with one streamer named Justin and was costly to stream.
- Even though it had limited features, it was successful because it solved a specific pain point for a small set of users.



## Stripe 

- The first version of Stripe was called Slash Depth Payments and had no fancy bank deal or direct APIs with the bank.
- It was so basic that even Twitch couldn't use it, but it solved a specific pain point for a small set of users.

## Building for Customers with Hair on Fire 

- Building an MVP is all about building for customers with a pressing need.
- Customers with hair on fire are willing to accept non-perfect solutions to solve their immediate problems.
- Don't try to build for customers who are not desperate yet.

## Surveys are Not a Shortcut 

- Surveys might help you understand the pain that your customer is going through.
- However, they will never help you figure out how to solve that pain.
- The only time you start having a conversation with customers is when you can put your MVP in front of them and ask if it solves their problem.
## Introduction 
- Building a successful startup requires starting with the minimum viable product (MVP).
- MVP is the minimum set of features required to satisfy early customers.
- MVP is not perfect, but it is the starting point for any startup.

## Importance of Learning in Startup 
- Building a startup is all about learning.
- The first phase of building a startup is pre-product market fit.
- You start with some insights, and then you bring them to the market to learn.
- Most of the best products to use today were discovered after the products were launched.
- Founders learn from their users, and building, launching MVP is the fastest way to start the process of learning.
- The faster you learn, the more likely you are to build something that people love before anyone else.

## Tricks to Quickly Build an MVP 
- Give yourself a very specific deadline to build the MVP.
- Write down the specifications required for the MVP.
- Cut back on the features required for the MVP.
- Don't fall in love with your MVP.

## Give Yourself a Very Specific Deadline 
- It's a lot easier to make sure that you're building something that's the minimum viable product if you give yourself two weeks or a month and a half to complete it.
- If you don't give yourself a deadline, it will be difficult to determine what features to include in the MVP.

## Write Down the Specifications Required for the MVP 
- If you think that there are five or ten features required in order to launch an MVP, write them all down.
- It will help you focus on building instead of continuously debating what should be built.

## Cut Back on the Features Required for the MVP 
- Go through each item on the specifications list and ask yourself if there's a truly desperate customer need for that feature.
- You may be surprised at how many features you can leave off for the second, third, or fourth version of your product.
- Just get the basic stuff out first.

## Don't Fall in Love with Your MVP 
- Your MVP is going to change, and you're going to iterate it.
- It's going to get very, very different over time.
- You want to do it fast and not fall in love with it.
- You want to fall in love with your customer/user, not with the crappy initial product that you're building to start learning from that user.

## Importance of Initial Customers 
- It's far better to have a hundred people love your product than a hundred thousand who kind of like it.
- When you're releasing that MVP, it's totally okay to do things that don't scale and recruit those initial customers one at a time.
- If you care about those customers, they will talk to you, and you can work with them to help figure out how to solve their problems.
- As a result, you can help figure out how to build a great product for them.

## Conclusion 
- Building a successful startup requires starting with the minimum viable product (MVP).
- MVP is the minimum set of features required to satisfy early customers.
- Building an MVP is all about learning from your customers and iterating your product to build something that people love.

# Transformer Neural Networks, ChatGPT's foundation, Clearly Explained!!!

## Introduction and Background 
- The video starts with an introduction to the topic of Transformer neural networks.
- The host, Josh Starmer, mentions the popularity of something called ChatGPT and its foundation in Transformer networks.
- Word embedding is introduced as a commonly used method to convert words into numbers for neural networks.
- A simple vocabulary is used as an example to explain word embedding.
- The concept of tokens is introduced, where each input (word, word fragment, or symbol) is considered a token.
- Tokens are connected to activation functions, and the connections are assigned weights.
- The concept of weight values is briefly mentioned, and their origin is left for later explanation.

## Word Embedding and Activation Functions 
- Word embedding is further explained as a process of converting input words into numbers by multiplying them with weights determined by the connections to activation functions.
- An example is given to demonstrate how the word "let's" is converted into numbers.
- The process is illustrated with multiplication of input values and weights, leading to output values.
- The activation functions are described as identity functions, where the output values are the same as the input values.
- The conversion of the word "go" into numbers is also explained using the same process.

## Back Propagation and Training 
- Back propagation is introduced as a method to optimize the weights in the word embedding network.
- The analogy of fitting a line to data is used to explain how back propagation iteratively adjusts the weights until optimal values are found.
- The optimization of weights is referred to as training the Transformer.
- The final weights obtained through back propagation are considered the optimized values for the network.

## Positional Encoding and Word Order 
- The importance of word order in conveying different meanings is highlighted with an example.
- Positional encoding is introduced as a technique used by Transformers to keep track of word order.
- The addition of positional encoding to a phrase is explained.
- The video concludes by showing an example of adding positional encoding to the first phrase.

# Notes continued in the next part.
## Word Embeddings and Positional Encoding 
- Word embeddings convert words into numbers.
- Each word has multiple embedding values.
- The number of embedding values per word can vary.
- Positional encoding adds numbers that correspond to word order.
- One popular method of positional encoding is using sine and cosine squiggles.
- Each squiggle represents a specific position and provides values for each word's embeddings.
- The y-axis values on the squiggles give position encoding values for the embeddings of each word.
- Position values for the first word come from the corresponding y-axis coordinates on the squiggles.
- Position values for the second and third words come from the y-axis coordinates that correspond to the x-axis coordinates for those words.
- The repetitive nature of the squiggles means that some words might have the same position or y-axis values.
- However, with a larger number of embedding values, the squiggles become wider, resulting in a unique sequence of position values for each word.
- By adding the position values to the embeddings, we obtain the word embeddings with positional encoding for the whole sentence.

## Reverse Word Order and Positional Encoding 
- If we reverse the order of the input words, the embeddings for the first and third words get swapped.
- However, the positional values for the first, second, and third words remain the same.
- When we add positional values to the embeddings, we end up with new positional encoding for the first and third words.
- The second word's positional encoding stays the same because it didn't change position.
- Positional encoding allows a Transformer to keep track of word order.

## Self-Attention for Word Relationships 
- Transformers use self-attention to correctly associate words with their intended meaning.
- Self-attention calculates the similarity between each word and all other words in the sentence, including itself.
- These similarities are used to determine how the Transformer encodes each word.
- If a word is more commonly associated with a certain context, it will have a larger impact on how it is encoded by the Transformer.

## Detailed Explanation of Self-Attention 
- Self-attention works by multiplying the positional encoded values for each word by pairs of weights and summing the products.
- This is done multiple times to create query values that represent the word.
- The reason for using multiple values to represent a word will be explained later.

## Next Steps 
- The video will continue to explain the details of self-attention and how it is used in Transformer neural networks.
## Introduction to Self-Attention 
- Self-attention is a key component of transformer neural networks.
- It helps the model understand the relationships between different words in a sentence.
- This is done by calculating the similarity between words using queries, keys, and values.

## Calculating Similarity 
- To calculate similarity, two new values are created for each word: key values.
- The dot product similarity between the query and keys is calculated by multiplying each pair of numbers together and adding the products.
- This process is illustrated using the example of the word "let's" and its similarity to itself and the word "go".

## Importance of Similarity 
- The similarity values obtained indicate how similar a word is to itself and other words.
- A higher similarity value for a word relative to itself indicates a stronger connection.
- In the example, "let's" has a larger similarity value with itself compared to the word "go".

## Softmax Function 
- To determine the influence of each word's encoding, the similarity scores are passed through a softmax function.
- The softmax function preserves the order of input values and translates them into numbers between 0 and 1 that add up to one.
- In this case, since "let's" is more similar to itself than the word "go", it will have a higher percentage used for its encoding.

## Generating Self-Attention Values 
- Two values are created to represent each word: let's and go.
- The values representing "let's" are scaled by 1.0, while the values representing "go" are scaled by 0.0.
- The scaled values are then added together to obtain the self-attention values for "let's".

## Calculating Self-Attention for Other Words 
- The process of calculating self-attention values for other words, like "go", involves creating a new query and performing similar calculations.
- The weights used for calculating self-attention queries, keys, and values are the same for all words.
- This allows for parallel computing and faster processing in transformers.

## Benefits of Self-Attention 
- Self-attention helps establish context and relationships between words in the input.
- By stacking multiple self-attention cells, transformers can capture different relationships among words in complex sentences and paragraphs.
- The original Transformer model used eight stacked self-attention cells for this purpose.

## Residual Connections 
- To encode the input, the position encoded values are added to the self-attention values.
- These bypasses, called residual connections, facilitate the training of complex neural networks.

Note: This is just a partial set of notes for Part 2 of the video. Please refer to other batches for complete coverage.
## Encoder and Decoder Introduction 

- The transformer neural network consists of two main components: the encoder and the decoder.
- The encoder is responsible for processing the input sequence, typically a sentence, and encoding it into a numerical representation.
- The decoder takes the encoded representation from the encoder and generates the output sequence, which in this case is a translated version of the input sentence.
- The encoder and decoder work together to establish relationships among the input words and preserve important information for the translation process.

## Encoding the Input 

- The input sentence is encoded using word embeddings and positional encoding, among other techniques.
- Word embeddings convert each word in the sentence into a numerical representation.
- Positional encoding adds information about the position of each word in the sentence.
- These encoding techniques allow the transformer to capture the relationships among words and train efficiently.

## Encoder Components 

- The encoder consists of four main components: word embedding, positional encoding, self-attention, and residual connections.
- Word embedding converts each word in the input sentence into a numerical vector.
- Positional encoding adds information about the position of each word in the sentence using sine and cosine functions.
- Self-attention allows the encoder to focus on different words in the input sentence simultaneously.
- Residual connections help preserve the original information from the input sentence during the encoding process.

## Decoding the Output 

- The decoder takes the encoded representation from the encoder and generates the output sequence, which is the translated version of the input sentence.
- The decoder also uses word embeddings and positional encoding, similar to the encoder.
- However, the word embeddings and positional encoding values are specific to the output vocabulary, which consists of the Spanish words in this case.

## Initializing the Decoding Process 

- The decoder starts the decoding process by initializing the word embeddings and positional encoding for the EOS (end of sequence) token.
- The EOS token represents the start of the decoding process and is commonly used as the initial input for translation.
- The decoder calculates the numerical values representing the EOS token using the embedding values and positional encoding.

## Encoder-Decoder Attention 

- Encoding the input sentence is not enough for accurate translation. The decoder also needs to consider the relationships between the input sentence and the output sequence.
- Encoder-decoder attention allows the decoder to focus on significant words in the input sentence while generating the output.
- This attention mechanism helps ensure that important words and concepts from the input are properly translated.

## Encoder-Decoder Attention Details 

- Encoder-decoder attention involves creating query and key vectors for the EOS token in the decoder and the words in the encoder.
- Similarities between the EOS token and the words in the encoder are calculated using dot products.
- The similarities are then passed through a softmax function to determine the importance of each word in the encoder for generating the first translated word.
- This attention mechanism helps the decoder keep track of significant words in the input sentence during translation.

# Stay tuned for the next batch of notes!
## Introduction to Transformers 

- Transformers are a type of neural network architecture that has revolutionized natural language processing tasks such as translation, chatbots, and text generation.
- They were introduced in 2017 and have become the foundation for various language models, including ChatGPT.
- Transformers use a combination of word embeddings, positional encoding, self-attention, and encoder-decoder attention mechanisms to process and generate text.

## Encoder-Decoder Attention 

- In the Transformer architecture, encoder-decoder attention is a mechanism that allows the decoder to focus on relevant parts of the input sequence (encoder output) while generating the output sequence.
- The encoder-decoder attention values are calculated by scaling the values obtained through self-attention by the softmax of the maximum percentages.
- These scaled values are then added together to get the encoder-decoder attention values.
- The sets of weights used for encoder-decoder attention are different from those used for self-attention.
- However, like self-attention, the sets of weights for encoder-decoder attention are copied and reused for each word, allowing the Transformer to be flexible with the length of inputs and outputs.

## Residual Connections 

- Residual connections are additional connections in the Transformer architecture that allow information to flow directly from one layer to another.
- In the case of encoder-decoder attention, residual connections enable the attention mechanism to focus on the relationships between the output words and the input sequence without having to preserve the self-attention or word and position encoding that happened earlier.
- These residual connections help in capturing important information and maintaining the flow of information throughout the network.

## Decoding Process 

- To select the output word from the decoder, the values representing the end-of-sentence (EOS) token and the translated word are passed through a fully connected layer.
- The fully connected layer has one input for each value representing the current token and one output for each token in the output vocabulary.
- The inputs are multiplied by weights and added biases, and the resulting values are passed through a softmax function to select the first output word.

## Example Translation 

- The video demonstrates the translation process using the example phrase "Let's Go" translated to "Vamos" in Spanish.
- The translation is done step by step, starting with word embeddings, positional encoding, self-attention, encoder-decoder attention, and finally, the decoding process.
- The video shows how the values representing the EOS token and the translated word are processed through the layers to generate the translated output.

## Summary of Transformer Components 

- Transformers use various components to process and generate text:
  - Word embeddings: Convert words into numerical representations.
  - Positional encoding: Keep track of word order.
  - Self-attention: Capture word relationships within the input and output phrases.
  - Encoder-decoder attention: Maintain important connections between the input and output phrases during translation.
  - Residual connections: Allow each subunit to focus on solving one part of the problem.
- These components work together to enable Transformers to effectively process and generate text.

## Additional Features 

- The video mentions a few additional features that can be added to Transformers to handle larger vocabularies and more complex data:
  - Normalization: Scaling the values after each step to improve the encoding and decoding of long and complicated phrases.
  - Different similarity functions: Instead of the dot product, other similarity functions can be used to calculate attention values.
  - Additional neural networks: Hidden layers can be added to both the encoder and decoder to provide more weights and biases, enabling the model to fit more complex data.

## Conclusion and Self-Promotion 

- The video concludes by summarizing the main ideas behind Transformers and their components.
- The presenter mentions that the video is part of a series and invites viewers to check out the study guides and book available on the presenter's website.
- The video ends with a call to action for viewers to subscribe, support the presenter's Patreon campaign, or purchase merchandise to support the channel.

# IMPACT OF CHATGPT ON SOCIETY

## The Unreliability of AI 
- AI models are unreliable and not trustworthy.
- We don't fully understand how they work or their reasoning.
- They don't provide their thinking or reasoning.
- They lack certain cognitive capacities.

## The Need for Research on AI 
- Calls for intense research on AI's abilities, limitations, trustworthiness, and interpretability.
- The investigation and results should be open to anyone.
- Melanie Mitchell spoke about this in her recent piece.

## The Dangers of AI on Society 
- Over-reliance on AI has negative societal impacts.
- We may lose all intelligible frameworks of understanding.
- People are becoming detached from basic understanding of things that are now dominating their world.
- AI's pernicious enmeshment in society leads to erosion of autonomy.
- When many things are controlled by the infosphere, people lose control.

## The Two Groups Running the World 
- The two groups interested in AI are those who can understand it and create it, and those who can use it effectively to control.
- The technical and political spheres are the two groups running the world.
- Politicians and bureaucrats want to control more, and that gives them more power and self-actualization.

## The Virtualization and Abstraction of Everything 
- There is a pernicious virtualization and abstraction of everything.
- Generative arts can produce an abstract image that is a confection of the work of thousands of artists.
- Personal identity is being diffused in ways that no one can currently understand.
- The real problem is the re-antologization of identity.
## Information Abstraction and Misinformation 

- Our society is increasingly abstract, and information is the best way to understand its functioning.
- However, information becomes so abstract and divorced from any intelligible understanding that it becomes impossible to do anything useful.
- Misinformation is a term used in the field of politics and society, which implies making a large collection of people believe a certain thing.
- Misinformation can be distinguished from disinformation based on malicious intent.
- The real threat is not the misinformation per se but its effect on our cognitive apparatus.

## Preventing the Impact of AI on Autonomy 

- Two things that are being eroded are agency and understanding.
- It means we've become a society of automatons.
- The extreme version of this is paternalism, which is worse than the outcome probably.
- It's not about preventing the AI as much is the precedent that you'd be setting what you can dictate to individuals and society.
- The problem is technologies become so democratized that anyone at home in their bedroom with a powerful machine can start to build this technology so that you would have to tell people that no, you can't use your computer anymore.
- We can say that isn't as Superior an outcome to the explosion risk of AI.
- The AI will basically seek to kill all of us, and they think this is possible.

## Existential Threat Posed by AI 

- People who advocate for the explosion are called doomers and think that AI will become an existential threat within 10-50 years.
- Can a machine have intentionality, can it will, seek to deceive us, and preserve itself?
- The machine or AI can differentiate between taking over and not taking over, and this is the problem.
## The limitations of understanding GPT 
- The speaker notes that there are limitations to human understanding of GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer).
- It is difficult for humans to comprehend what GPT thinks or how it processes information.

## The Pandora's Box analogy 
- The speaker compares GPT to Pandora's Box, a metaphor for a source of endless complications.
- The speaker implies that GPT is like Pandora's Box because it is a powerful tool that, if not used carefully, could have unforeseen negative consequences.

## The danger of relying on GPT 
- The speaker notes that GPT could be dangerous because relying too heavily on it could lead to negative consequences.
- The speaker suggests that by the time people realize they are in trouble, it might be too late to prevent the negative outcome.
- The speaker implies that people need to be careful when using GPT to avoid negative consequences.

## The need for caution when using GPT 
- The speaker suggests that much of the hype around GPT is based on fanciful ideas.
- The speaker seems to suggest that people need to be cautious when using GPT and not rely too heavily on it without fully understanding its limitations.

# 7 better ways to create a React app

## Overview
- Create React App (CRA) is the official tool for getting started with react.js, but there are 7 better ways to create a react app.
- We will be looking at 7 ways to create a react app without create react app and the trade-offs so you can choose the optimal tool for the type of app you're building. 

## Stack Blitz and Code Sandbox 
- Drastically simplifies the process of setting up a development environment 
- Click a button and you can create a react app 
- You can even run back-end code like node.js and next.js thanks to web containers
- Great for learning and prototyping, but not suitable for building a serious app


## Veil 
- Closest thing to a one-for-one replacement for CRA 
- Way faster and more scalable for bigger projects 
- Supports Tailwind and Typescript out of the box
- May require installing a bunch of extra dependencies 
- Mainly suitable for single-page applications 



## Next
- Building a react app without using a react-rendering framework
- Comes with a low-level API for server rendering
- Uses Roll-up for module bundling suggesting fast program execution
- Easily shareable from any device
- Typescript template by default to support modern libraries 



## Nx 
- Builds standalone react apps
- Builds with webpack, RS Pack, or any other bundler 
- Uses TypeScript by default and CSS preprocessor 
- Comes with task caching and cloud computing features for scaling 
- Has generators for adding dependencies and scaffolding boilerplate code 
- Provides baseline for CI automation by generating a CI workflow 



## React-Rendering Frameworks 
- Meta-frameworks for multi-page applications 
- Support Server-Side Rendering (SSR) and Advanced Routing 
- Prominent example is Next.js which optimizes performance and search engine optimization (SEO) 
- Server-side data fetching with React server components 
- Minimal external dependencies 
- Universal React code support (runs on both client-side and server-side)
 



## NexT.js vs. Remix
- NexT.js provides **server-side components** while Remix **does not** 
- NexT.js features **nested layouts** and **streaming** are in **beta** while Remix's versions are **fully stable**. 
- **Competition** between the two is **beneficial** to React developers, as they have access to two excellent Frameworks. 



## Gatsby 
- Gatsby is a popular choice for **static content heavy sites** though it also supports server side rendering. 
- Gatsby is unique in that it uses **Graphql** to provide a data layer for the application, with **Walhalla content Hub** providing a unified API for data sources.
- Gatsby has **many tools** to quickly migrate content-driven apps to React, including **CMS selection** during initial setup. 



## Astro 🧠
- An alternative framework for content-heavy sites is **Astro**, which is **not exclusive to React** and also supports Vue and Solid. 
- Its **'Islands' architecture** simplifies code and increases performance by **eliminating JavaScript** needing to be shipped to the browser.
- Astro's **Content Collections** feature enables sites to scale up securely, with markdown content adhering to a schema. 



## Create react app
- There are **seven different ways** to create a React app **without using create react app**, including NexT.js, Remix, Gatsby and Astro. 
- The future of Create React App is unknown, with the potential for it to become an app launcher pointing to one of the aforementioned Frameworks. 
- Another possibility is that Create React App will integrate **generative AI** to automatically generate starter projects.

And you can look under the hood and see that what it actually did was write a prompt just like a human could. And so you sort of have this ability to inspect how the machine is using these tools, which allows us to provide feedback to them. Now it's saved for later, and let me show you what it's like to use that information and to integrate with other applications too. You can say, “Now make a shopping list for the tasty thing I was suggesting earlier.” And make it a little tricky for the AI. "And tweet it out for all the TED viewers out there." (Laughter) So if you do make this wonderful, wonderful meal, I definitely want to know how it tastes. But you can see that ChatGPT is selecting all these different tools without me having to tell it explicitly which ones to use in any situation. And this, I think, shows a new way of thinking about the user interface. Like, we are so used to thinking of, well, we have these apps, we click between them, we copy/paste between them, and usually it's a great experience within an app as long as you kind of know the menus and know all the options. Yes, I would like you to. Yes, please. Always good to be polite. (Laughter) And by having this unified language interface on top of tools, the AI is able to sort of take away all those details from you. So you don't have to be the one who spells out every single sort of little piece of what's supposed to happen. And as I said, this is a live demo, so sometimes the unexpected will happen to us. But let's take a look at the Instacart shopping list while we're at it. And you can see we sent a list of ingredients to Instacart. Here's everything you need. And the thing that's really interesting is that the traditional UI is still very valuable, right? If you look at this, you still can click through it and sort of modify the actual quantities. And that's something that I think shows that they're not going away, traditional UIs. It's just we have a new, augmented way to build them. And now we have a tweet that's been drafted for our review, which is also a very important thing. We can click “run,” and there we are, we’re the manager, we’re able to inspect, we're able to change the work of the AI if we want to. And so after this talk, you will be able to access this yourself. And there we go. Cool. Thank you, everyone. (Applause) So we’ll cut back to the slides. Now, the important thing about how we build this, it's not just about building these tools. It's about teaching the AI how to use them. If you go back to Alan Turing's 1950 paper on the Turing test, he says, you'll never program an answer to this. Instead, you can learn it. - People are given time to input before the machines are perfect and super powerful.
- GPT-3 is an example. The team was afraid that the number one use would be to generate misinformation and try to tip elections, but it was only used to generate Viagra spam.
- This approach is the only other path to building AGI that would benefit all of humanity.

## The Pandora's box thought experiment 
- Suppose you are sitting in a room with a box on the table.
- You believe that the box contains something that could be absolutely glorious and give beautiful gifts to your family and everyone.
- However, there is a one percent chance that the box contains something that could unleash unimaginable evils on the world.
- Do you open the box?

## The need for incremental development 
- The development of every technology has been incremental.
- The history of capability has been quite smooth over time.
- Each moment that capability is increased, it is important to figure out how to manage it.
- Development of other technologies like nuclear weapons has been incremental.
- It is important to take each step as we encounter it.

## Responsibility for the future of AI 
- We have birthed an extraordinary child that may have superpowers that take humanity to a whole new place.
- It is our collective responsibility to provide the guardrails for this child.
- It is important to collectively teach it to be wise and not tear us all down.
- We need to get literate in this technology, figure out how to provide feedback, and decide what we want from it.

# I built a react app… but with a visual editor

## Introduction to Codex 
- Codex is a new visual IDE created by Wix that brings drag and drop productivity to React apps.
- It is a tool that complements VS Code but not a replacement.
- It works in tandem with VS Code while providing a robust visual layer on top of your code.
- It is entirely free and requires typescript and CSS module SAS or stylable for styling.

## Overview of Codex Interface 
- Codex has a home tab that shows file explorer, git integration, and other icons.
- Yes we can 
- It has a main editor that shows the code for the board component.
- Boards allow isolating your own components.
- A board contains a component that in this case renders the app component.
- It has a component editor that provides a hierarchy of elements in the Dom.
- It has a properties panel where properties on any element can be modified.
- It has a style editor that allows adding new styles and modifying existing ones.

## Creating a React Component in Codex 
- To create a new project, you need to download React from the website and create a new project.
- Codex only supports React, and it's necessary to use typescript and CSS module SAS or stylable for styling.
- You can create a new component by clicking on the plus icon and giving it a name.
- Creating a new component will create a new board for us, which allows us to develop this component in isolation.
- Clicking on the pencil icon in the components panel brings up its code.
- Props can be added to the component interface and used in Codex from the properties panel.

## Building a BNB Card Component 
- For each BNB card, we'll need a title, price, and an array of image URLs.
- The main card will have two other divs, one for the carousel and one for the main content below the images.
- Dummy data can be added to the component props in the board properties panel.
- The divs can be structured, and elements can be added by dragging and dropping them.
- The style editor can be used to add new styles and modify existing ones.
## Styling with CSS Editor 
- The CSS Editor is a visual tool that allows filtering of CSS properties and enables visual editing.
- It has advanced features like shadow editor, which simplifies editing different shadow properties.

## Making the component interactive 
- To make the component interactive, we add a div and a couple of buttons inside the carousel.
- The buttons should rotate between the images in the carousel.
- We can write all the code in codecs but we can switch over to vs code for that. 

## Implementing Dynamic Data 
- We can destructure the props from our interface and use that to interpolate dynamic data like the title and price.
- We can add some state for the current index of the image that we want to show in the carousel.
- We can define a couple of functions like previous image and next to change the index in a specific direction.

## Adding functionality to buttons 
- We can bind carousel functions to the buttons by selecting a button from the elements tab and finding the on click property in the properties panel.
- We can then add the appropriate function name in the code.

## Updating the Default Image 
- We update the default image with the current index of the images array.

## Using the component 
- We can put the component to use in other places in the app application by dragging and dropping it to the desired location.
- It may show an error initially because it's missing the required props.
- In the full demo, the presenter took some dummy data and looped over it to show multiple carousels and then styled them with CSS grid.

## Codex 
- Codex is a new tool with features that any developer can take advantage of, whether you're a beginner or highly experienced.
- It won't replace your main editor but it has some unique features like changing the size of the canvas to check its responsiveness without leaving the IDE.
- It's a tool that allows visual editing and helps to speed up the development process.
