# KEMI SEBA : la philosophie de la panafricanité | Entretien


## Définition du Panafricanisme [00:02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2xgj-POfU7Y&t=00h00m02s)
- Le panafricanisme est l'unité des diverses formes d'africanité dans l'objectif d'obtenir collectivement notre souveraineté et de pouvoir peser dans le concert des nations.
- Selon Donelder Camara, c'est la théologie ou l'idéologie de libération des peuples africains de manière générale.

## Combat pour les peuples [02:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2xgj-POfU7Y&t=00h02m04s)
- Kimi Seba mène un combat pour son peuple en priorité, tout en comprenant que la justice est transgraciale et va au-delà d'une question d'épiderme et de peuple.
- Il y a des personnes qui luttent contre l'impérialisme qui sont des plus blancs, et des personnes qui luttent en servant l'impérialisme qui sont les plus noirs.

## Négritude [03:02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2xgj-POfU7Y&t=00h03m02s)
- La négritude et la noirceur ne range pas automatiquement les personnes du côté des opprimés, mais peuvent les ranger profondément du côté des serviteurs de l'oppression.
- Des exemples connus sont Alassane Dramane Ouattara et Macky Sall, qui sont noirs mais servent l'impérialisme.
## La blanchitée et la couleur de peau [03:22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2xgj-POfU7Y&t=00h03m22s)
- Pour Kemi Sebah, l'Occident en tant civilisation a commis aux quatre coins du monde des actes que aucune autre civilisation n'a commis. 
- Il faut accepter que la civilisation occidentale est porteuse du chaos, que ce soit au sens métaphysique ou physique.
- La blanchitée est avant tout une dimension sociale et politique, et non pas une couleur.

## Est-ce qu'on peut concevoir une dimension politique dans le fait d'être noir? [04:29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2xgj-POfU7Y&t=00h04m29s)
- Selon Kemi Sebah, être noir est une entité politique, car les populations africaines ont été incarcérées et circonscrites par l'Occident. 
- Être noir est une communauté de véhicules, de destin, de douleur, et de perspectives.
- Malgré les différentes coutumes qui traversent les nations, il y a un foyer commun.

## Les communautés de destin des noirs [05:54](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2xgj-POfU7Y&t=00h05m54s)
- Les communautés de destin des noirs vont des prolétaires des ghettos aux prolétaires et bourgeois des Assemblées Nationales.
- Lorsqu'on voit un noir dans une belle voiture, il y a une perception que c'est peut-être un dealer.
- En allant aux quatre coins du monde, on voit les aborigènes d'Australie, les Mélanésiens, les dramidiens en Inde, les Afro-colombiens en Amérique du Sud, les Afro brésiliens, etc.
## Racisme systémique dans le monde [06:28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2xgj-POfU7Y&t=00h06m28s)
- Le racisme systémique existe dans le monde entier, et touche les populations mélanodermes à l'échelle internationale. Rosa Meloribe, écrivaine afro-colombienne, a parlé de la "Férocité Blanche "dans son livre, qui a été un best-seller à l'époque.
- La suprématie blanche ne signifie pas que tous les prolétaires blancs sont responsables de cela, mais il y a un racisme vis-à-vis des populations mélanodermes qui ne peut être ignoré.

## Se prendre en charge [07:29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2xgj-POfU7Y&t=00h07m29s)
- Les populations mélanodermes doivent se prendre en charge, se responsabiliser et se structurer en communauté. Ils doivent tendre la main à ceux qui leur tendent la main, mais surtout comprendre la nécessité de compter sur eux-mêmes.
- Les Noirs doivent cesser de mendier et se lancer dans l'antiracisme, mais ils doivent surtout prendre conscience de leur puissance et de leur importance.

## Lien et communauté de destin [07:47](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2xgj-POfU7Y&t=00h07m47s)
- Malgré les enjeux ou luttes différentes que vivent les différentes minorités noires dans le monde, il y a une communauté de destins. Il est important de créer du lien entre les banlieusards et les prolétaires africains, et de comprendre que c'est la même pieuvre qui impose le racisme systémique.
- Cette pieuvre à plusieurs tentacules, et cela signifie que la discrimination, l'agression et l'asphyxie des populations noires est causée par la même force mondiale.

# StreamingLLM - Extend Llama2 to 4 million token & 22x faster inference?

## Introduction to the problem 
- The demand for feeding more data and knowledge to large language models is increasing.
- However, feeding more data to these models causes them to perform slower and eventually run out of memory.
- This is because GPUs, which are commonly used for large language models, have limited memory and the complexity of the model increases quadratically with the number of tokens.

## Limitations of feeding unlimited data 
- It is not possible to feed unlimited data into GPUs due to their limited memory.
- Even if it were possible, it would take a very long time to compute, which would dramatically impact user experience.

## Window attention as a solution 
- One common solution to this problem is using something called Window attention.
- Window attention means that instead of feeding all the data into the model, only the latest x amount of tokens are used.
- This allows the model to generate relevant content with good performance.
- However, the downside is that the model loses context about the tokens that have been removed.

## Introduction to StreamingLM 
- StreamingLM is a research project that explores a new approach to significantly increase the amount of data that a large language model can take as input and generate text at high efficiency.

## Attention sync and effective context window 
- The StreamingLM project identifies a phenomenon called attention sync.
- Attention sync means that even though a large language model is fed a large amount of data, it pays more attention and weights to the initial tokens compared to the end tokens.
- This means that the initial part of the context is more important, while the middle part contributes less or has less weight.

## Extending the effective context window 
- The StreamingLM project extends the effective context window by combining the attention sync of the first few tokens with a rolling cache of the latest x amount of tokens.
- This allows the large language model to have context about what has been talked about before as well as recent conversation.

## Detailed illustration of how StreamingLM works 
- As the amount of data expands, the tokens in the middle are excluded from the memory.
- The model only considers the initial part with attention sync and the rolling cache, which contains the content in the end.
- By utilizing this approach, the StreamingLM project achieves the ability to feed large language models an infinite amount of inputs.

## Limitations and use cases of StreamingLM 
- While StreamingLM allows for more context, it still has limitations.
- It works well for scenarios that require large language models to generate a large amount of content, such as long-form content generation (e.g., writing a book or movie transcripts).
- It also works for maintaining context in chatbots over a longer period of time.
- However, it is not suitable for tasks that require detailed context in the middle of the input, such as summarizing research papers.

## Conclusion and future possibilities 
- StreamingLM is just one implementation of utilizing attention sync to extend the context window.
- There may be more creative concepts to solve the context limit problem.
- Viewers are encouraged to comment with their own ideas.
- Exciting AI projects like StreamingLM are continuously being explored and shared.

# My $200 million startup mistake by Garry Tan

## Background
- Gary Tan is a venture capitalist and product manager who graduated in 2003. 
- He had dinner with Peter Thiel, who was a known great entrepreneur, but not yet a billionaire. 
- Peter asked Gary to quit his job at Microsoft and join his startup, offering him a check for $500,000.


## Pros and Cons of Working for a Big Tech Company
- Pros include the ability to ship products to millions of people, a stable job, and access to smart people.
- Cons include difficulty in making something new, the need to be good at negotiation and politics, and the potential to become too comfortable.


## Advantages of Working at a Smaller Place or Starting a Company
- Direct access to users and customers and their problems, the ability to create empathy and solve problems, and the potential to create hundreds of millions of dollars worth of value.


## Advice
- Gary advises to make sure that time is spent wisely, especially when young, and to consider the pros and cons of working for a big tech company or a smaller one. 
- He encourages people to make their own mistakes, and to remember the cycle of making software and solving problems for people.

- The author shows how to use a text-to-speech model to convert the AI girlfriend's responses into audio and play it back to the user.
- The author shows how to run the AI girlfriend as a chatbot in a Telegram bot using the Telegram API.
- The author emphasizes that building your own AI girlfriend is easy and can be done for free using OpenAI's GPT-3 model.
## Understanding the rules of the AI 
- The AI is designed to simulate a human girlfriend.
- The user inputs the history and human input variables to the prompt template.
- Overdefined templates are used to generate responses that follow certain rules.
- Rules include the girlfriend's name (Shirley), age , occupation (market manager at her uncle's furniture store), and language addiction (using the word "earn" at the end of sentences).

Title: Why React.js is taking a new direction
Video URL: https://youtu.be/1LkOa7Ky2ak
Categories: Academind
Transcript:
React is getting used more than ever before. It's super popular, and especially compared to Angular and Vue, it's definitely far ahead, and it's also not just npm download numbers. If we take a look at the State of JavaScript 2022 survey, we can confirm that React is super popular amongst JavaScript developers, even though it's slightly dropped in popularity since 2019, 2020. The latest major version of React, React 18, was released roughly a year ago and therefore, the question is, "What's the current state of React?" Now, let's start with a quick win. Hooks are standard, actually, to be fair, not just since this year, but they have been the standard in 2021 and 2022 as well. You can still use class-based components, and it's probably not going anywhere. You can stick to that approach if you like, but hooks are definitely the default. In most projects you find, most examples you find use hooks, but of course, React Hooks were introduced back in React 16.8, not in version 18. Instead, React 18 was all about concurrent features, formally known as concurrent mode. To be precise,, React 18 did introduce two important new hooks, useTransition, and useDeferredValue, which ultimately are both tools you can use to give your website users a better perceived performance, to avoid blocking UI states and ensure smooth UI updates and changes. And belonging to the same category of changes, React 18 also added new capabilities to Suspense, which is a component you can wrap around your components to show a fallback whilst you're waiting for code to download in case of lazy loading or a data to be fetched. Though this Suspense for data fetching feature is still in experimental mode and not that easy to implement from scratch on your own. Instead, it's much easier if you use libraries that integrate with it, like React Query or Facebook's relay package but even those packages mention that it's still in experimental mode and not stable and ready for production yet. So these React 18 features exist to give you tools to improve the perceived performance of the React app you're building. Using these tools, however, is non-trivial. It's certainly doable for a big company like Meta with hundreds or thousands of engineers. After all they built React. But if you are working on your own or in a smaller team, these features will maybe not be that helpful to you. And it's also pretty clear to see that Meta, so Facebook, in the end, built all these features for themselves and they then rolled it out to the public once they tested it internally, which, of course, generally is a good approach, but which also makes it seem like you're only getting features that Meta or Facebook needs. But there also is one other exciting initiative taken by the React team, and that would be server components. Server components were first announced at the end of 2020 and the idea behind them is that you can have some components that only run on the server and never reach the client. Therefore, you can perform server-side logic in them, like reach out to a database and you ship less client-side code to your users, which is amazing. And that generally is a huge trend. Server components are actually still not stable, still experimental, but NextJS 13, for example, uses them in their new feature, which is also not finished and also not stable yet. That allows you to build more complex fullstack applications and that allows you to move more code on the server. So the current state of React is, of course, still that we have a library that's there to build front end user interfaces and that's always what React will do but enriched with more backend capabilities or combined with Meta frameworks like NextJS or Remix that allow us to build such fullstack applications. Because as I also mentioned in my phases of JavaScript framework evolution video, we moved more and more code to the client side, adding more and more complexity to the client side and more code that must be downloaded by our users. And now this trend is reversing and we're building full-stack apps again and we need frameworks that simplify the process of building these fullstack apps while still being able to build these rich, highly interactive user interfaces. So React is not going anywhere. It's more important than ever, but it's also more important than ever to learn a Meta framework like NextJS or Remix or Next for Vue if you're using that or look into AnalogJS for Angular if you're into that to move more code back from the client onto the server. And that trend of going back to the server for certain tasks has a couple of important implications. It, for example, means simpler client-side code, less useState, and less useEffect, less Eedux usage because there is less state to manage on the client side and less side effects to run if you're doing more work on the server again. For example, in my Remix course where I teach you this amazing framework, there is no useState and no useEffect call in the entire final project we built because we have all that logic on the server side. So that's the state of React. You're getting tools to build better user interfaces that are non-blocking, that feel reactive, that are responsive. And at the same time, we get more tools around React. We get all these Meta frameworks like Next and Remix that allow us to simplify our React apps and then leverage React for the front end but also make it easier for us to build full-stack applications and move logic back onto the server, ultimately leading to simpler React apps. So should you stop learning React? No, not at all. It's that foundation for the next evolution phase.

# Why React.js is taking a new direction





## Introduction to React.js
- React.js has become more popular than ever, with an especially notable lead over Angular and Vue according to npm downloads and the State of JavaScript 2022 survey
- React 18 is the latest major version of React, and some of its improvements focus on giving developers tools to improve the perceived performance of React apps



## React Hooks 
- Hooks are the standard in React, and have been since React 16.8
- You can still use class-based components, but hooks are the default
- Hooks introduced in React 16.8 include: `useTransition` and `useDeferredValue` 



## React 18 New Features 
- React 18 also added new capabilities to `Suspense`, which is a component that can wrap around other components to show a fallback while you wait for code to download, or data to be fetched
- The `Suspense for data fetching` feature is still in experimental mode and not yet stable, but easier to implement using libraries like `React Query` or `Facebook's relay package`
- React 18 also introduced two important hooks, `useTransition`, and `useDeferredValue`, which are tools to give users a better perceived performance, to avoid blocking UI states and ensure smooth UI updates and changes



## Server Components 
- Server components were first announced at the end of 2020
- Server components allow you to perform server-side logic without reaching the client, and to ship less client-side code to your users
- Server components are still experimental, and must be used alongside Meta frameworks like React Query or NextJS



## Working with React
- Learning a Meta framework like NextJS or Remix, or Next for Vue if needed, can help simplify building full-stack apps
- Complex projects may require more use of the server and less client-side handling of logic, useState, and useEffects, with Redux usage potentially becoming unnecessary 
- React will always be the foundation for building front end user interfaces, but enriched with more backend capabilities or combined with Meta frameworks like NextJS or Remix to allow for building fullstack applications

source.title: Why React.js is taking a new direction

# Guilty or Not Guilty? | Ricky Sarthou

# Introduction 
- The video starts with music playing in the background.
- This is the last episode of the current season and it is based on the book of Romans.
- In the next season, Pastor Peter will talk about how to be sure about going to heaven.

## Setting the Stage 
- The speaker mentions that many television shows and movies are based on courtroom dramas.
- One of his personal favorite movies in this genre is "A Few Good Men" starring Tom Cruise and Jack Nicholson.
- He quotes a famous dialogue from the movie, "I want the truth!" and "You can't handle the truth!"
- The speaker emphasizes that even though we may say we want the truth, the question is, can we handle it?

## The Good News in the Bad News 
- The speaker mentions that even when talking about bad news, the Bible always brings good news.
- Jesus himself is described as full of grace and truth.
- The speaker assures that behind the bad news, there is always great news.

## Guilty or Not Guilty? 
- The title of today's message is "Guilty or Not Guilty?"
- The speaker asks the audience what they think the answer should be.
- He explains that the message will explore this question together.

## Judgment Day and Courtroom 
- The speaker refers to the previous Sunday's message by Pastor Peter and informs that they will continue from Romans chapter 2 verse 5.
- Paul writes about a day of wrath and the righteous judgment of God.
- It is mentioned that there will be a judgment day in court.
- God will render judgment to each person according to their deeds.

## Understanding Judgment and Salvation 
- The speaker acknowledges the confusion regarding judgment according to deeds and salvation by faith.
- It is clarified that judgment will be based on works, but salvation is by grace through faith.
- Works are important because they are the outward expression of what a person truly is deep down.
- Believers' works are the expression of faith, while unbelievers' works show unbelief.

## Ephesians 2:8-10 
- The speaker shares his favorite verses from the Bible, Ephesians chapter 2 verses 8 to 10.
- The verses talk about salvation by grace through faith, not as a result of works.
- It is emphasized that no one can boast about their salvation based on their own good deeds.
- The speaker reflects on his own past sense of moral superiority and the realization that salvation is not earned through works.

# To be continued in Part 3...
## Good works as evidence of salvation 
- Good works are not the means to be saved.
- Good works are the outflow and evidence of salvation.
- In verse 10, it is mentioned that believers are God's workmanship created in Christ Jesus for good works.
- These good works were prepared beforehand by God, and believers are called to walk in them.

## Genuine salvation results in good works 
- The equation is not that good works lead to salvation.
- Genuine salvation leads to good works.
- Good works are the evidence that someone has received eternal life by faith in Jesus.

## The day of wrath and righteous judgment 
- Paul is discussing the day of wrath when God's righteous judgment will be revealed.
- Those who, by perseverance in doing good, seek for glory, honor, and eternal life will receive it.
- This does not mean that they earned it through their good deeds, but their good deeds are evidence of their faith in Jesus.

## Outcome of obedience or unrighteousness 
- Those who are selfishly ambitious and do not obey the truth but obey unrighteousness will face the outcome of wrath and indignation.
- This is the reverse of the outcome for those who persevere in doing good.

## Tribulation and distress for those who do evil 
- Paul states that there will be tribulation and distress for every soul who does evil.
- This applies to both the Jew and the Gentile.
- On the other hand, glory, honor, and peace will be given to everyone who does good, first to the Jew and also to the Gentile.

## Two groups on judgment day 
- Paul presents two groups or columns on judgment day.
- Group A consists of those who are saved through faith in Jesus Christ alone.
- The evidence of their salvation is that they persevere in doing good.
- Group B consists of those who have not put their faith in Jesus Christ alone.
- The evidence is that they do not obey the truth.

## Destiny of the two groups 
- The destiny of Group A, those saved through faith in Jesus, is glory, honor, peace, and eternal life.
- They will experience the wondrous environment of heaven forever.
- The destiny of Group B, those who do not obey the truth, is wrath, indignation, tribulation, and distress.

## Relevance of Jew and Gentile to us today 
- Paul's letter addresses two major groups: the Jews and the Gentiles.
- The Gentiles are referred to as those without the law, while the Jews are those under the law.
- The relevance to us today is that the Gentiles represent moralists who believe they can be good without God.
- The Jews represent religious people who practice their religion.

## Defense number one: "I live a good life" 
- Defense number one is the belief that living a good life is enough.
- Romans 2 discusses Gentiles who do not have the law but instinctively do things according to the law.
- They are a law unto themselves, indicating that even without the law, they somehow know what is right.

## Gentiles as moralists 
- Gentiles can be seen as moralists who live a good life based on conscience.
- Their basis for living a good life is their conscience.
- If their conscience does not bother them, they consider themselves okay.

## Jews as religious people 
- Jews, on the other hand, are religious people who have a religious tenet that they practice.
- Their defense is that they practice their religion.

## Question: Guilty or not guilty? 
- The question arises for both moralists and religious people: Are they guilty or not guilty?
- This question sets the stage for further discussion and exploration in the video.
## Conscience as a Basis for Judgment 

- The work of the law is shown in the hearts of people.
- Conscience plays a significant role in determining right from wrong.

## Understanding Conscience 

- Conscience is an inner feeling or voice that guides one's behavior.
- It is a spiritual and moral consciousness, unique to human beings.
- Conscience is a precious gift from God, as humans are created in His image.

## Conscience as a Witness 

- Conscience bears witness to our thoughts, alternately accusing or defending us.
- It reveals whether we have done right or wrong based on our moral standards.

## Conscience and Judgment 

- According to the Gospel, God will judge the secrets of men through Jesus Christ.
- Conscience becomes the basis for judgment on the day of reckoning.

## Limitations of Conscience 

- Conscience is not always reliable.
- It can accuse or defend us, indicating that we don't always do what is right.
- Living a good life based solely on our conscience is not sufficient for justification.

## Conscience and its Definition 

- Conscience is defined as an inner feeling or voice that guides behavior.
- In a biblical context, it is a spiritual and moral consciousness resulting from being created in God's image.

## The Problem with Conscience 

- Some people claim to live a good life by following their conscience.
- However, when asked what they believe is right and wrong, they might struggle to answer.

## Conscience and Personal Experience 

- Everyone fails to consistently do what is right based on their conscience.
- Personal example: The speaker learned to play guitar using a 12-string guitar to build calluses faster.
- The example illustrates that conscience can become calloused or desensitized.

## Conscience and Addiction 

- The speaker shares his personal struggle with addiction to pornography.
- Repeated exposure to pornography caused callousness in his conscience.
- His conscience became numb to the wrongness of his actions.

## Living a Good Life and Conscience 

- Living a good life and following one's conscience is not a reliable defense.
- The speaker emphasizes that this defense leads to guilt, not innocence.

## Reliance on Religious Practices 

- Some people rely on their religious practices to justify their actions.
- Paul addresses the Jews who boast in having God's law but fail to live according to it.
- This can also be applied to Christians who claim to follow Jesus but do not live out His teachings.

## Summary

- Conscience serves as a moral compass and witnesses our thoughts and actions.
- It is a spiritual and moral consciousness unique to human beings.
- Conscience can be unreliable and calloused, leading to guilt.
- Living a good life or relying on religious practices is not enough to justify oneself.
# Paul's Argument Against Self-Righteousness 
- Paul addresses those who see themselves as religiously superior and confident in their own righteousness.
- He reminds them that they are called to be guides to the blind and a light to those in darkness, which is true according to Jewish beliefs.
- However, Paul turns the tables on his fellow Jews and points out their hypocrisy.
- He challenges them to examine their own actions and asks if they are truly living up to the standards they teach.
- Paul questions if they, who preach against stealing, are stealing themselves, or if they, who preach against adultery, are committing adultery.
- He reminds them of Jesus' teaching that even looking at someone with lust is already committing adultery in the heart.
- Paul's argument is that if they claim to be religious and place their confidence in their religious practices, they should be able to follow their religion perfectly at all times, which is impossible.

- Ricky shares his own story of being a religious young man before he became a follower of Jesus.
- He would pray in his office every morning and attend church services regularly.
- However, he also had a secret indulgence in watching explicit movies.
- Ricky highlights that being religious and practicing a religion does not guarantee true righteousness or a transformed heart.
- He emphasizes that true Christianity is not about external appearances but about the condition of the heart.

# The Name of God Blasphemed Among the Gentiles 
- Paul warns that the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of the hypocrisy of those who claim to be religious.
- Ricky mentions the sad reality of children growing up in homes where their parents profess to be Christians but do not live out their faith.
- He describes situations where parents who claim to be Christians engage in conflict, neglect their children, or fail to demonstrate love and respect.
- Ricky quotes Ray Stedman, who points out the hypocrisy of those who focus on how many people they win to Christ but not on how many they drive away.
- The name of God is blasphemed when those who claim to follow Him do not live according to His teachings.

# Relying on the Power of the Holy Spirit 
- Ricky emphasizes the need for true followers of Jesus to rely on the power of the Holy Spirit.
- He reminds listeners that salvation is by faith alone and not by following religious practices.
- Ricky cautions against boasting in following the Bible as the basis for eternal destiny, as it is only through faith in Jesus that salvation is obtained.

## Anticipating Counter Arguments 
- Paul anticipates possible counter arguments and addresses something that is significant to Jews.
- The video ends before further elaboration on this topic.

(Note: These notes are based on the provided caption extract and do not include information beyond the given timestamps.)
## The Significance of Circumcision 
- Circumcision is the topic being discussed by Ricky Sarthou in this video.
- It is an important issue in the Bible, specifically for the Jews.

## Circumcision and the Law 
- Circumcision held great value for the Jews because it was commanded by God and it symbolized their covenant relationship with Him.
- However, Paul is saying that circumcision is only valuable if one practices the law.
- If someone is a transgressor of the law and does not obey it, then their circumcision becomes meaningless.

## The Importance of an Inward Transformation 
- Paul is emphasizing that focusing solely on the outward act of circumcision misses the point.
- In the Old Testament, God spoke about circumcising the hearts of His people, indicating that the outward ceremony was merely a symbol of an inward transformation.
- Paul suggests that if one only focuses on the outward ceremony and disobeys the law, it is as if they were never circumcised to begin with.

## Baptism as a Modern Parallel 
- Ricky Sarthou draws a parallel between circumcision in the Old Testament and baptism in the New Testament.
- Just as circumcision was an important outward ceremony for the Jews, baptism is a significant ceremony for Christians.
- Sarthou highlights the meaningfulness of baptism and its representation of an inward change and new life in Christ.

## Ensuring the Right Motives for Baptism 
- Sarthou acknowledges that there may be people who get baptized for the wrong reasons, such as peer pressure or to gain membership in a church.
- He emphasizes that the focus should be on the inward change and transformation that baptism represents, not just the outward act.

## The True Jew and the Circumcision of the Heart 
- Paul states that being a Jew is not merely about outward circumcision, but about an inward transformation of the heart.
- Circumcision of the heart is a work of the Holy Spirit, not something we can achieve on our own.
- This inward change changes our perspective in life and redirects our focus to pleasing God rather than seeking worldly recognition.

## God's Faithfulness and Human Response 
- Paul addresses the advantage of being a Jew and the significance of circumcision.
- He acknowledges that not everyone will believe in the gospel, but this does not nullify God's faithfulness.
- People are held responsible for their decision to believe or not believe in the gospel.

## Conclusion 
- Paul concludes by stating that it is not God's fault if people do not believe the gospel.
- He emphasizes that God will be found true, even if every man is found to be a liar.
- This sets the stage for the next section in Romans chapter 3.
## Establishing counter-arguments 
- Paul anticipates and addresses counter-arguments against his statements.
- He acknowledges that some may argue that their unrighteousness demonstrates the righteousness of God.

## Challenging the counter-arguments 
- Paul states that if their unrighteousness establishes the righteousness of God, then God is not unrighteous in inflicting wrath upon them.
- He clarifies that he is speaking in human terms to address these flawed arguments.

## Anticipating objections 
- Paul suggests that some may argue that their sinfulness actually establishes the fact that God is holy and righteous.
- They might question why God would judge them since their unrighteousness validates His righteousness.
- Paul considers this argument to be absurd.

## Invalidating the counter-arguments 
- Paul asserts that no matter how crazy or persuasive these counter-arguments may seem, they will always fail.
- He aims to silence these objections once and for all.

## Addressing misinterpretations 
- Paul questions why he is still being judged as a sinner if his dishonesty actually brings glory to God.
- He dismisses the slanderous claims that he and others encourage doing evil to bring about good.
- Paul asserts that their condemnation is just, implying that these claims are baseless.

## Introducing the question of guilt 
- The main question posed in this video is whether we are guilty or not guilty.
- The focus is on our guilt or innocence apart from faith in Jesus.

## Testimony of Rachel, the sister attorney 
- Rachel shares her personal journey and how it relates to the topic of guilt.
- She grew up attaching her self-worth to achievements and reputation.
- Rachel believed that following her conscience and practicing her religion would grant her acceptance into heaven.
- However, she realized that this belief was flawed and led to a poor and sad conclusion.

## The pursuit of success and self-righteousness 
- Rachel's pursuit of success and adherence to rules led her to become self-righteous.
- She looked down on others who struggled in life and lectured them on how to live.

## Confrontation and depression 
- Rachel's friends and classmates confronted her about her judgmental and self-righteous attitude.
- These incidents caused her to fall into depression and feel embarrassed about herself.

## Seeking answers 
- Rachel's family started attending Christ's Commission Fellowship, and she had the opportunity to attend a college retreat.
- She questioned why God allowed her possessions to be swindled despite following all the rules.
- Rachel wanted to find God and attended the retreat to search for answers.

## Understanding her sinful nature 
- The retreat speaker shared the story of the prodigal son and emphasized the love of the Father.
- Rachel realized that her sinful nature was her biggest problem.
- She was focused on herself, her reputation, and possessions, which prevented true happiness.

## Accepting Jesus as Lord and Savior 
- Through the retreat, Rachel accepted Jesus as her Lord and Savior by faith.
- She decided to get baptized and commit to following Jesus for the rest of her life.

## Surrendering to God's will 
- Rachel's journey with Jesus has not been easy, as God continually asked her to give up things.
- She had to surrender more of herself and dedicate her life to Jesus.
- For example, God asked her to give up building her resume and instead serve in the campus ministry.
- He also challenged her dream of a successful law career.

These are the notes for the second batch of the video "Guilty or Not Guilty? | Ricky Sarthou".
## Ricky Sarthou's Journey 

- Ricky Sarthou shares about his journey in the legal profession.
- He mentions that he was rising within the ranks and building his name as a legal professional.
- However, God asked him to leave his law firm and work full-time for CCF's legal department.

## Trusting in God's Plan 

- Ricky Sarthou refers to Romans 8:28, which says that God causes all things to work together for good for those who love Him and are called according to His purpose.
- He shares that on April 19, 2022, he celebrated his 14th birthday as a follower of Jesus Christ.
- Ricky expresses that through all these years, God has blessed him with peace, joy, and contentment as following God's will became his priority.
- He mentions that academic excellence, commendations, and admiration from people are bonuses, but his value is in Jesus and his identity in Him.

## Mentoring and Discipling 

- Ricky Sarthou considers himself privileged to mentor younger lawyers and model Christ's likeness in the workplace.
- He also mentions that he is being discipled by a couple and currently discipling a group of women who have the desire to dedicate their lives to the Lord in the marketplace.

## Restoration and New Relationships 

- Ricky Sarthou shares that despite his past as a self-absorbed and judgmental person, God allowed him to restore his friendships with his friends from university.
- He also mentions that God has allowed him to gain new friends, brothers, and sisters in Christ who have encouraged him to pursue Christ's likeness and reminded him of his value in Jesus.

## Finding Value in Jesus 

- Ricky Sarthou states that he was once defined by the world, but now he finds his value in the sacrifice of Jesus and being a privileged servant of Almighty God.
- He gives all the glory and praise to God.

## Prayer for Ricky Sarthou 

- The video host prays for Ricky Sarthou, thanking God for his grace and using Ricky as an example of God's abundant grace.
- The prayer asks for God's blessing upon Ricky, protection from the evil one and pride, and for the work of his hands and motives of his heart to be pleasing in God's sight.

## The Verdict is Guilty 

- The video host mentions that if the verdict is guilty, our only recourse is to throw ourselves at the mercy of the court.
- He refers to Romans 3:9, which states that both Jews and Gentiles are all under sin, meaning that everyone is guilty.
- He emphasizes that we have no choice but to fall down and plead for the mercy of the Lord.

## Salvation through God's Mercy 

- The video host reads Titus 3:4-5, which speaks of God's kindness, love, and mercy that saved us.
- He explains that our journey into experiencing regeneration and renewing begins with God's mercy.
- The host highlights that it is in Jesus and Jesus alone that we find salvation and righteousness.

## Jesus' Sacrifice for Our Sin 

- The video host shares a passage from Matthew 27:26, where Pilate released Barabbas, a condemned sinner and murderer, instead of Jesus.
- He explains that Jesus took the sin of Barabbas and our sin to the cross.
- The host mentions that Jesus became sin on our behalf, and through his sacrifice, we can become the righteousness of God in Him.

## Conclusion 

- The video host concludes by emphasizing that it is in Jesus alone that we find redemption and righteousness.
- He encourages viewers to put their trust in Jesus and plead for His mercy.
## Introduction and Verdict of "Not Guilty" 

- When we put our faith and trust in Jesus as our Savior, we will hear the verdict of "not guilty."
- The speaker, Ricky Sarthou, praises God for Jesus, leading to applause from the audience.

## Personal Story of Faith 

- Ricky shares a personal story about his wife being hospitalized last year.
- They were on the phone, and Ricky didn't realize that the call would be so brief.
- The last four words Ricky heard from his wife's mouth were, "I'm ready to go."

## Justification in Jesus 

- Ricky explains that his wife said she was ready to go because she knew in Jesus she had been justified.
- Justification means being declared "not guilty" by God through faith in Jesus.

## The Assurance of Being Ready to Meet Jesus 

- Ricky emphasizes that when we put our faith in Jesus, we can also say we're ready to go and meet Him.
- We can confidently meet the One by whose name we have been justified.
- In His glorious presence, we will be forever.

## Application for Followers of Jesus 

- Ricky concludes with some applications for believers.
- He encourages them to be humble and not look down on others, remembering that they are saved by grace alone.
- Believers are also encouraged to tell others about Jesus, pray, care, and share.

## Invitation for Non-Believers 

- Ricky addresses those who are not yet true followers of Jesus.
- He urges them to stop making excuses and relying on their morals or religion for salvation.
- The invitation is to surrender their lives to Jesus Christ and receive Him as their Savior.

## Prayer of Surrender and Transformation 

- Ricky leads a prayer for those who want to accept Jesus as their Savior.
- He encourages them to open their hearts, stop making excuses, and rely on Jesus instead of themselves.
- The prayer includes a recognition of guilt and a surrender of their lives to Jesus.
- The prayer asks Jesus to start a transforming work in their lives, so they will follow Him all their days.

## Assurance of Righteousness and Being Ready to Go 

- Ricky highlights that because believers are righteous in Jesus and declared not guilty, they can confidently say they're ready to go.
- He attributes all glory, honor, and praise to Jesus forever.

## Conclusion and Blessing 

- The video ends with music and a final blessing.
- The audience responds with "Amen" and "God bless us everyone."

# Key Takeaways

- Putting our faith in Jesus results in the verdict of "not guilty" and the assurance of being ready to meet Him.
- Believers should be humble, tell others about Jesus, and demonstrate care and compassion.
- Non-believers are invited to surrender their lives to Jesus and rely on Him for salvation.
- The prayer of surrender includes a recognition of guilt and a desire for transformation by Jesus.
- Believers can confidently say they're ready to go because they are righteous in Jesus and declared not guilty.

# How to use Chat GPT for Learning and Practicing English

## Introduction to using ChatGPT for Learning and Practicing English

- ChatGPT is a cutting-edge artificial intelligence (AI) model that can understand and respond to natural language and can help improve your English skills. 
- By having a personal English tutor and AI language partner at your fingertips, you can make writing, grammar, and vocabulary exercises more interactive and fun.
- ChatGPT was designed as a computer program that can use complex algorithms and data to generate responses to questions or prompts that it receives. 
- You can use it for practice conversation and dialogue, prepare for a job interview, practice vocabulary, and practice grammar.
- Additionally, you can use it to practice pronunciation. 

## Benefits of Using ChatGPT for Learning English

- It can generate scripts for practicing different conversations in different situations
- It can provide feedback on your writing, grammar, and syntax
- You can use it to simulate a job interview
- It can provide you with the meaning of a specific word and give examples of that word in use
- It can generate multiple example sentences using the same grammar tense so you can repeat them out loud and internalize the structure

## Practicing with ChatGPT

ChatGPT is an amazing AI tool which can be used to help you improve your English. Here are some ways you can use ChatGPT for English practice:
- Ask it to help you practice pronunciation by writing a sentence with multiple of a certain letter or sound. Then, use text-to-speech to have it read the sentence back to you and repeat it. 
- Ask it to help you practice the difference between a tense 'ee' and a lax 'i' sound within one sentence by giving it a few words and requesting a sentence with those words. 
- Use it to simplify a challenging text and tailor it to your level.
- Ask ChatGPT to help you write emails. It can make your language more friendly or more formal depending on who you're writing to.
- Use it to ask for information but be aware that it is not always accurate - for deeper English knowledge, consult traditional resources. 

Remember that no matter what AI technology offers, it cannot replace real conversation and interaction in English. Consider joining a community such as InFluency for conversation practice and to build fluency.

# Réseaux : adresse IP et masques de sous-réseaux

## Qu'est-ce qu'un réseau?
- Un ensemble de machines reliées entre elles
- Comprend les PC, les imprimantes, les automates programmables, etc.
- Tous les éléments reliés à un réseau sont appelés "machines"
- Pour communiquer entre elles, les machines ont besoin d'une adresse

## Les adresses IP 
- Une adresse unique pour chaque machine sur un réseau
- Composée de 4 octets (32 bits)
- Chaque octet a une valeur comprise entre 0 et 255
- Les adresses IP sont codées en binaire
- Une partie de l'adresse sert à identifier la machine, l'autre à identifier le réseau

## Les masques de sous-réseau
- Permettent de diviser un réseau en sous-réseaux
- Composés de 4 octets, comme les adresses IP
- 255 représente une partie de réseau, 0 représente une partie machine
- Les masques de sous-réseau sont également codés en binaire

## Comment identifier un réseau
- En utilisant l'adresse IP de la machine et le masque de sous-réseau
- Convertir l'adresse IP en binaire
- Appliquer le masque de sous-réseau à l'adresse IP binaire
- Le résultat donne l'adresse du réseau sur lequel se trouve la machine

## Comment diviser un réseau en sous-réseaux
- En utilisant des masques de sous-réseau différents
- Plus de 0 et moins de 255 permet de diviser un réseau en plus de sous-réseaux
- Plus de 255 permet de diviser un réseau en moins de sous-réseaux
- Le nombre de machines pouvant être connectées à un réseau dépend du masque de sous-réseau utilisé
## Calculating the Network Address 
- To determine the network to which an IP address belongs, a logical AND operation is performed.
- A network address identifies the network on which we are working.

## Logical AND operation
- A logical AND operation involves performing the AND operation between the IP address and the subnet mask of the network.
- This operation is represented by the symbol "&".
- When performing the AND operation, the result is either 0 or 1.

## Using a subnet mask with simple values
- When using a simple subnet mask like 255.255.255.0, the network address can be obtained by simply replacing the last octet of the IP address with 0.
- This allows us to identify the network address and the host address easily.

## IP address classes
- IP addresses are divided into classes, with Class A, B, and C being the most common.
- Class A addresses range from 0.0.0.0 to 127.255.255.255, with a subnet mask of 255.0.0.0.
- Class B addresses range from 128.0.0.0 to 191.255.255.255, with a subnet mask of 255.255.0.0.
- Class C addresses range from 192.0.0.0 to 223.255.255.255, with a subnet mask of 255.255.255.0.

## Identifying the network and host portion of an IP address
- The network portion of an IP address is determined by the class of the IP address.
- The host portion of an IP address is determined by the subnet mask used.

## Number of machines on a network 
- The number of machines that can be placed on a network is determined by the subnet mask used.
- The number of machines that can be placed on a network is limited by the number of unique IP addresses that can be assigned to the network.
- The total number of unique IP addresses that can be assigned to a network is determined by the subnet mask used.
## Identifying the network address and broadcast address
- The network address is the address that identifies the network.
- It is not allowed to use the network address as a host address.
- The broadcast address is an address that is used to send messages to all hosts on the network.
- It is also not allowed to use the broadcast address as a host address.

## Calculating usable addresses on a network 
- To determine the number of usable addresses on a network, subtract the network address and the broadcast address from the total number of addresses.
- The resulting number is the number of usable addresses on the network.

## Exercise: Determining network information

- The exercise involves determining network information using an IP address and a subnet mask.
- The first step is to convert the IP address and subnet mask to binary.
- The network address can then be determined by performing a logical AND operation between the IP address and subnet mask.
- The number of usable addresses on the network can be calculated by subtracting the network address and broadcast address from the total number of addresses.
- The broadcast address can be determined by setting all the host bits in the network address to 1.
- The usable address range can be determined by taking the network address and adding 1 to get the first usable address, and taking the broadcast address and subtracting 1 to get the last usable address.

## Converting binary to decimal

- To convert a binary number to decimal, group the bits into sets of 4, starting from the rightmost bit.
- Convert each set of 4 bits to its decimal equivalent using the chart 0000=0, 0001=1, 0010=2, 0011=3, 0100=4, 0101=5, 0110=6, 0111=7, 1000=8, 1001=9, 1010=10, 1011=11, 1100=12, 1101=13, 1110=14, 1111=15.
- Add up the decimal values of each set of 4 bits to get the decimal equivalent of the binary number.
## Subnet masks and converting to binary
- Converting IP addresses to binary is necessary for subnetting.
- When converting to binary, we end up with groups of 1s and 0s.
- The high part of these groups will be used for coding the address of two machines.

## Determining the number of usable addresses 
- To determine the number of usable addresses, we need to look at the number of bits available for the address.
- From the previous example, we have 14 bits, which can code up to the number 161383 in decimal.
- This means we can have up to 161384 addresses, but two of them are reserved for broadcast and network addresses.
- Therefore, we can use 161382 addresses.

## Broadcast address
- We need to determine the broadcast address of the network.
- To do this, we take the network address we found earlier and convert it to binary.
- We determine the high part of the binary, which is the 14 bits. We then convert them all to 1s.
- Converting this back to decimal gives us the broadcast address.

## Determining the usable address range
- To find the usable address range, we use the network address we found earlier.
- We add 1 to this address to get the first usable address.
- We then subtract 1 from the broadcast address to get the last usable address.

# So now what..?

## Layoffs in Tech
- 59,448 layoffs have occurred in 2023, as of January 25th, that's roughly 2,300 a day. 
- Some of the layoffs were sent as emails at 3 AM
- Imagine the shock of a worker who has been with a company for two decades, suddenly getting a layoff email. 

## Advice for Those Laid Off
- Ask yourself where all the new growth in tech is. Currently, Javascript and React are two of the most hireable skills. 
- Don't limit yourself to those two skills. Think about other skills that will set you apart from other applicants. 
- Prepare for tomorrow by researching what tech will make you hireable over the next few years, or learning a tech you'd like to work with someday. 



## Advice for Everyone
- Interviewing is a skill that can be practiced and improved. 
- Become the type of engineer that other engineers will want to work with. Research and stay updated on new ways to solve problems, and be passionate and excited about tech.

## Conclusion

- Disinformation is a powerful tool that can be used to manipulate public opinion.

## Cartels et inégalités économiques 
- Les cartels sont liés à un coefficient de génie qui mesure les écarts d'inégalités de richesse.
- Les pays avec les plus grandes inégalités économiques ont souvent des problèmes de corruption et de violence.
- Le Brésil, en particulier, a de grandes inégalités économiques, ce qui entraîne des problèmes de corruption et de violence.

## Le Brésil et ses perspectives d'avenir 
- Si le Brésil parvient à régler ses problèmes d'inégalités économiques, cela pourrait être un grand pas en avant pour le pays.
- Le Brésil est considéré comme une terre d'avenir pour les investissements.
- La baisse du taux de chômage au Brésil est un signe positif pour son développement économique.

## Les relations entre la Russie et le Mali 
- Le président russe, Vladimir Poutine, a eu des discussions avec le colonel malien, Assimi Goita, sur les questions de sécurité, d'économie et de céréales.
- Les relations entre la Russie et le Mali se renforcent, alors que la France perd en influence dans la région.
- Le Mali est confronté à une situation délicate, car il doit choisir entre rester du côté français ou se tourner vers les Russes.

## La situation politique au Tchad 
- L'ancien président du Tchad, Idriss Déby Itno, a été assassiné, ce qui n'est pas une théorie du complot mais un fait.
- Son fils est maintenant président du pays, mais la situation est tendue, car les Russes cherchent à étendre leur influence au Tchad.
- Les États-Unis s'opposeraient à une intervention russe au Tchad, ce qui rend la situation encore plus complexe.

## L'Organisation de coopération de Shanghai (OCS) 
- Le ministre russe des Affaires étrangères, Sergueï Lavrov, annonce que l'Iran rejoint l'Organisation de coopération de Shanghai.
- L'OCS a été créée pour contrer l'influence américaine en Asie centrale, notamment en Afghanistan et en Irak.
- Les États-Unis ont utilisé des bombes à sous-munitions à l'uranium, causant de nombreuses morts, ce qui a conduit à la création de l'OCS.

## La formation de l'alliance de sécurité collective 
- Les États-Unis ont décidé d'intervenir en Eurasie, malgré le manque de justification morale, géopolitique et légal.
- Cela a conduit la Chine et la Russie à former une alliance de sécurité collective.
- Cette alliance a donné naissance à l'Organisation de coopération de Shanghai, qui est similaire au Pacte de Varsovie, mais moins solide et pyramidale.
- L'Organisation de coopération de Shanghai est une organisation importante qui s'oppose à la présence américaine au Moyen-Orient et en Asie centrale.

## L'adhésion de l'Iran à l'Organisation de coopération de Shanghai 
- L'Iran a rejoint l'Organisation de coopération de Shanghai en raison de la menace américaine et de son renforcement de la puissance.
- L'Iran avait été sur la liste des pays susceptibles d'être bombardés par les États-Unis.
- La Russie, devenue plus puissante grâce à sa position en Ukraine, a également renforcé l'alliance et rendu l'adhésion de l'Iran plus logique.
- L'adhésion de l'Iran à l'Organisation de coopération de Shanghai est un marqueur géopolitique important.

- Il y a eu une vaste opération de cyberespionnage par un groupe lié à la Chine.

- Un documentaire sur Arte a démontré que la NSA américaine avait des pratiques d'espionnage encore plus problématiques que celles prétendument utilisées par la Russie.
- Les États-Unis violent les droits de l'homme en ouvrant la correspondance de tout le monde et en violant le droit fondamental à la protection de la correspondance.

## Les contrats de gaz entre la Chine et la Russie 
- La Chine a signé un nouveau gros contrat de gaz avec la Russie.
- Dans les années 2000 et 2010, de tels contrats étaient considérés comme problématiques et pouvaient entraîner des conséquences négatives.
- Le film "Syriana" avec George Clooney fait référence à cette situation et montre comment certaines personnes ont été poussées à intervenir dans des pays pour des raisons autres que humanitaires.
- Les États-Unis n'interviennent généralement pas pour des raisons humanitaires, il y a souvent d'autres motivations en jeu.

## Conclusion provisoire
- Cette partie de la vidéo a abordé l'alliance de sécurité collective formée par la Chine et la Russie en réponse à l'intervention américaine en Eurasie.
- L'adhésion de l'Iran à cette alliance renforce la position de l'Organisation de coopération de Shanghai.
- Le cyberespionnage est également un sujet important, avec les États-Unis et la Chine en tant que principales puissances dans ce domaine.
- Les contrats de gaz entre la Chine et la Russie ont également été évoqués, montrant comment ces accords peuvent avoir des implications géopolitiques.
## Geopolitical implications of China's dependence on hydrocarbons 

- China's economy is heavily reliant on hydrocarbons, particularly oil.
- In the movie "Syriana," George Clooney's character mentions China's economic slowdown due to their lack of access to oil.
- This highlights the vulnerability of China's economy and the importance of securing oil resources.

## Potential allies for the United States and China 

- The United States may find natural allies in countries like Qatar, despite their current tensions.
- The idea is that if the United States were to be invaded by Iran, these natural allies would come to their aid.
- This demonstrates the complex network of alliances and partnerships in the geopolitical landscape.

## Russia as a guarantor of neutrality 

- In the event of a U.S. withdrawal, Russia could potentially guarantee the neutrality of certain zones, such as Taiwan.
- This suggests that Russia could play a significant role in maintaining stability and balance of power in certain regions.

## China's cooperation with the Russian navy 

- China has called for strengthening cooperation with the Russian navy, particularly in the Arctic Ocean.
- This indicates the growing naval capabilities and influence of both China and Russia in the region.
- It also suggests a potential alliance between the two countries to counterbalance the United States.

## The role of BRICS in resolving diplomatic conflicts 

- If BRICS becomes a diplomatic authority with its own security council and peacekeeping forces, it could arbitrate internal conflicts.
- This could include disputes between countries like Iran and Saudi Arabia.
- While it may not eliminate all conflicts, it could lead to more peaceful resolutions and reduce geopolitical tensions.

## Vietnam's role as a key partner in the Indo-Pacific 

- Vietnam is considered a key partner for maintaining a free, peaceful, and prosperous Indo-Pacific region.
- This is significant because Vietnam was formerly an enemy of the United States during the Vietnam War.
- The fact that Vietnam is now a member of the ASEAN and is concerned about China's rise indicates the shifting dynamics in the region.

# Key Takeaways
- China's dependence on hydrocarbons poses challenges to its economy and drives its geopolitical strategies.
- Russia potentially playing a role in maintaining stability and balance of power.
- The growing naval capabilities and influence of China and Russia in the Arctic region.
- BRICS potentially becoming a diplomatic authority to resolve conflicts.
- Vietnam's evolving role as a key partner in the Indo-Pacific region.
## The Korean Peninsula and the Nuclear Threat 
- The president is talking about the Korean Peninsula and its economic situation.
- The Korean Peninsula serves as a source of cheap labor for South Korea.
- The president warns that the Korean Peninsula is on the verge of a nuclear war, but he doesn't want to downplay the seriousness of nuclear wars.
- Pyongyang, the capital of North Korea, heavily relies on nuclear weapons as its main bargaining chip due to its non-existent economy.
- North Korea's only valuable resources are its natural resources, which could potentially be a reason for positive relations between Washington and Pyongyang.
- The president clarifies that he doesn't want to alarm the viewers and considers the news about the situation in North Korea to be exaggerated.
- The North Korean regime uses its limited resources to create trouble in the region, particularly with its nuclear capabilities.

## The Correlation Between Resources and Power 
- North Korea possesses significant natural resources, making it a country with spectacular geology.
- This is one of the reasons why Donald Trump had considered establishing positive relations with North Korea.
- However, the president cautions that North Korea's resources are not in the form of innovation or patents, but rather in their ability to cause trouble in the region with their nuclear capabilities.

## The Need for Diversification and De-dollarization 
- The discussion shifts towards the importance of diversification and de-dollarization.
- The president mentions that North Korea's reliance on nuclear weapons as a bargaining chip highlights the need for other countries, such as the BRICS nations, to reduce their dependence on the US dollar.
- De-dollarization is seen as a strategic move to counterbalance the power of countries like the United States.
- The president believes that the BRICS nations have the potential to create a new global economic order by diversifying their currencies and reducing their reliance on the US dollar.

## The Impact of De-dollarization on Global Power Dynamics 
- De-dollarization is seen as a way for countries to assert their power and influence in the global economy.
- By reducing their reliance on the US dollar, countries like the BRICS nations can challenge the dominance of the United States.
- The president highlights the importance of understanding the role of currencies in shaping global power dynamics.
- The ability to control and manipulate currencies can significantly impact a country's position in the world.

# Le Temple du Peuple : La SECTE la plus meurtrière de l'Histoire ☠️

## Jim Jones 

- Jim Jones was born in 1931 in a rural and poor area of Indiana.
- He was raised by a single mother who was a union activist and often absent due to her work.
- Jones was interested in different religious movements during his adolescence and would preach to other children his age.
- He combined his religious, political, and moral knowledge to create his own preaching style.
- He worked in a hospital and provided free medical care to the poorest people in Richmond, a city with a large black population.
- He married a nurse named Marceline Baldwin at the age of 19 and had six children, five of whom were adopted.
- Jones became a pastor in 1952 and started to show interest in Marxism a year later.
- He collected $20,000 to create a recreation center without distinction of race or religion.

## The Peoples Temple 

- Jones founded his own religious movement, The Peoples Temple, in Indianapolis in 1955.
- The movement was initially composed mostly of white people before gaining authority in the black neighborhoods of the city.
- The temple practiced communalism, which meant that all members had to give up their material possessions to the temple, and the temple would provide for their needs.
- Jones engaged in recruitment tactics that included hiring private detectives and passing off the information he received as divine intuition.
- He continued to organize popular events, provide free medical care, and educational support, and fought against racial segregation.
- In 1959, The Peoples Temple joined the Christian Church of the Disciples of Christ, a large church with over 2 million members.

## Expansion 

- Jones wanted more black families to join his church and went to Cuba to bring 40 families who had been trained in communism.
- The temple continued to grow in Indianapolis, and Jones started to present himself as a prophet.
- He preached that those who didn't give their possessions to the temple would be reincarnated as inferior creatures.
- The temple became increasingly paranoid and surrounded itself with barbed wire and armed guards.
- Jones took many medications and became dependent on amphetamines and tranquilizers, which led to changes in his behavior and physical appearance.
- He started a relationship with a temple member named Caroline Leighton.
## Jim Jones déménage à San Francisco 
- Les problèmes de Jim Jones l'ont poussé à déménager à San Francisco avec une annexe à Los Angeles.
- Le temple du peuple est devenu un mouvement de plus en plus important, avec des autobus du temple faisant le tour des quartiers pauvres de Los Angeles et convertissant de plus en plus de fidèles.
- Jones a réussi à sortir de prison de nombreux membres de l'Église et a même reçu le soutien de personnalités telles que Jane Fonda ou Angela Davis.

## Le Temple du Peuple devient politique 
- En 1976, Jim Jones s'intéresse de plus en plus à la politique.
- Il favorise l'élection de George Moscone à la mairie de San Francisco, qui en échange le nomme à la Commission des logements publics.
- Les médias ne parlent qu'en positif de la secte, mais en coulisses les choses avancent.

## Les pratiques abusives de Jim Jones 
- Au début, les punitions publiques étaient des confessions, des critiques constructives et des remises en question.
- Mais au fil du temps, les punitions corporelles sont apparues, où la victime pouvait recevoir des coups de bâton ou se battre avec une autre personne en public.
- Jim Jones a fait signer à tous les membres de la secte des documents indiquant qu'ils ont déjà violé un enfant ou qu'ils souhaitent tuer le président des États-Unis.
- Il peut ainsi les faire chanter et garder sous son emprise, il leur fait même signer d'autres documents vierges au cas où le pasteur voudrait ajouter d'autres éléments.

## Le Temple du Peuple se politise 
- Le Temple du Peuple commence à s'allier avec toutes les minorités, les mouvements noirs, les associations juives, les homosexuels, ainsi que les blackmuslims.

## Le déménagement au Guyana 
- Jim Jones prépare doucement mais sûrement son exil et celui du temple.
- En 1973, il cherche un plan de secours au Canada, en Jamaïque ou au Guyana. C'est le Guyana qui est choisi.
- Des terres agricoles sont achetées et le pays est également propice à la corruption.
- Jim Jones ne lésine pas sur les millions et parvient à faire entrer illégalement plusieurs centaines de personnes.
- Il ordonne même à une membre de la secte d'avoir des relations avec l'ambassadeur du Guyana aux États-Unis.
- Le nouveau terrain que le Pasteur Jones est en train de construire va s'appeler Johnston.
- La presse se méfie de plus en plus du Temple du Peuple.
## Conditions de vie à Johnston 
- Johnston est situé au Guyana, au milieu de la forêt, à la frontière avec le Venezuela.
- En 1977, le campement compte 50 personnes, mais ce nombre augmente considérablement pour atteindre 1200 personnes.
- Les cuisines et les ressources ne sont pas adaptées, les habitants doivent parcourir 11 km pour trouver de l'eau potable.
- Les millions du peuple sont stockés dans des paradis fiscaux et ne sont donc pas dépensés en nourriture.
- Un quart des habitants ont plus de 50 ans, et un tiers sont des enfants, ce qui signifie qu'il y a peu de travailleurs et ceux-ci sont surmenés.

## Organisation à Johnston 
- Le pavillon central de Johnston est au centre de la ville, où le pasteur prononce ses sermons.
- Les haut-parleurs diffusent ces discours dans tout le campement, où il parle de communisme, de persécution et d'apocalypse nucléaire.
- Les journées sont chargées, les habitants travaillent de 6h30 à 18h avec une heure de pause déjeuner, puis ils doivent participer à une des activités obligatoires.
- Tout cela dans le but de maintenir les habitants dans un état de fatigue constant et les empêcher de réfléchir.

## Communication avec l'extérieur 
- Les membres du Temple doivent envoyer régulièrement des lettres à leurs proches, toutes identiques.
- Les jeunes femmes célibataires indiquent qu'elles vont se marier avec un docteur, cela rassure les parents.
- Les membres sont entraînés à répondre aux interviews et éviter d'en dire trop.

## La violence se fait plus présente 
- Nous sommes clairement dans une secte, rien de nouveau, mais un tournant beaucoup plus violent va arriver en août 1977.
- Jim Jones tire des coups de feu dans la jungle et prétend avoir échappé à un sniper.
- Il révèle la ville et annonce que la CIA est en route pour les attaquer.
- Pendant six jours, la ville est en état de siège en tout cas c'est ce que croient les fidèles.

## Punitions violentes infligées par Jim Jones 
- Jim Jones réveille souvent les habitants en pleine nuit, il leur parle d'apocalypse et de suicide révolutionnaire.
- En 1978, il commence même à leur donner du jus de fruit qu'il prétend empoisonner.
- Le pasteur demande d'écrire leurs peurs les plus profondes et il les réalise comme punition s'ils remettent en cause les ordres.
- Les enfants désobéissants ont également leur punition, ils reçoivent des décharges électriques, sont enfermés dans un puits pendant des heures, doivent manger du piment rouge ou se l'insérer dans le rectum.

## La surveillance et l'isolement 
- Tout est surveillé, les lettres, les poubelles, les appels téléphoniques, les passeports et les effets personnels sont confisqués, bref, on ne peut pas s'enfuir.
- Les rares personnes qui ont tenté l'évasion étaient blanches, les Noirs se retrouvaient avec des conditions souvent plus favorables qu'aux États-Unis, surtout les personnes âgées.
- Il n'avait donc aucune raison de partir, par contre cela n'empêche pas l'agacement au sein même de la famille du pasteur.
- Sa femme Marceline et ses enfants souhaitent le tuer.
## Background on the Jones family 
- The father of the child was Jean Jones.
- The mother was sterile, which created a problem for the couple.

## The Joneses leave the Temple 
- In 1977, the parents of the child, who were both former members of the Temple, pretended to take a trip to New York.
- They left the sect and became vocal opponents of the People's Temple.
- Despite being divorced, they both demanded the return of their son.

## Legal action against the Temple 
- The American justice system issued an arrest warrant for Jones if he ever returned to the United States.
- The Stones, a family opposed to the Temple, created the Family Concerned Association to repatriate members of the Temple who left without their family's consent.
- When American legal action proved insufficient, the Stones filed a complaint with the Guyanese government.

## Investigation into the Temple 
- Guyanese inspectors tried to investigate John Stone but were driven away by gunfire.
- The Guyanese government requested the arrest of Jones in September 1977.

## Legal battles against the Temple 
- Throughout 1978, a legal battle between the Stones and the People's Temple was fought.
- An interview with Jane Jones was so altered by the Temple that newspapers refused to publish it.
- Numerous letters from faithful members of the Temple to the United States indicated that it was better to die than to be harassed.

## Investigative journalism 
- Journalist Katie Hunter traveled to Guyana to visit the Temple but was prevented from doing so by the sect.
- Her hotel was evacuated every night due to bomb threats.

## Congressman Leo Ryan visits the Temple 
- Congressman Leo Ryan, whose jurisdiction included many members of the Temple, traveled to Guyana with a group of visitors.
- Jones initially refused the visit, but it was eventually allowed under Guyanese pressure.
- Ryan was impressed with the Temple and believed it could continue to exist peacefully.
- However, he also arranged for those who wanted to leave to be repatriated.

## Assassination of Congressman Ryan 
- After the visit, a Temple member tried to stab Congressman Ryan.
- Larry Layton, a Temple member who wanted to leave, brought a gun and opened fire.
- Ryan and four others were killed.
- Jones realized that the Temple was finished. 

## The mass suicide plan 
- The United States government would not allow Leo Ryan's death to go unpunished.
- The Guyanese government would not support the Temple.
- Jones decided to carry out the mass suicide plan.
## Suicide collectif 
- Jim Jones convinced 914 members of the People's Temple to commit a mass suicide in Jonestown, Guyana in 1978.
- Jones praised the revolutionary merits of suicide and convinced his followers to drink poison.
- Not all members of the cult were voluntary. Some were drugged or forced to drink the poison.
- 914 members of the cult, including 304 children, were found dead by the authorities.

## Christine Miller's Opposition 
- Christine Miller, an African-American woman, opposed Jim Jones' plan and begged for the survival of the temple.
- Other members of the cult booed her and she was forced to concede.

## Survivors 
- Only 20 members of the cult survived by hiding when they realized what was happening.
- The last person to die was the temple's nurse who shot herself in the head after writing a letter saying, "We are dead because you would not let us live in peace."

## Aftermath 
- The incident at Jonestown resulted in 914 deaths, making it the largest civilian loss of American lives before the 9/11 attacks.
- The People's Temple lost its status as a religious and charitable organization.
- The tax returns deposited in Paradise were recovered and given to the families of the victims.
- Some members who survived the incident struggled to reintegrate into society.

## Mike Prokes and Others 
- In 1979, Mike Prokes, the public relations representative for the People's Temple, defended the group and denied that it was a cult.
- In 1983, former members of the cult, including Laurence Mann and Richard Dwyer, committed suicide.
- Tyronne Mitchell, whose parents and four sisters died in the Jonestown massacre, committed a school shooting before killing himself.

## Responsibility 
- It is difficult to hold anyone responsible for the Jonestown massacre since almost all of the victims were American.
- Jim Jones was a socialist pastor who blamed the church and socialism for the incident.
- Some black pastors believe that black churches at the time should have taken responsibility for helping the community rather than leaving it to the People's Temple.
